# CLU Negative-Results Registry

> **Purpose & policy (Head directive, 2026-07-07 → charter C-9).** *Negatives are documented, never dropped.* Every negative / null / refuted result across all verticals is recorded here, one entry per result. The **most prominent** negatives go in the respective papers' **appendices** as future-work anchors — this file is what the paper-writer mines for those appendices. A paper that hides its negatives fails Hub review.
>
> **Schema per entry:** what was tried · exact numbers (copied verbatim from source report + section) · why it failed (mechanism if known) · scope of the negative · **prominence tier** (**A** = goes in a named paper's appendix / **B** = ICLR appendix or future-work / **C** = internal caveat only) · owning vertical · source report.
>
> **Conventions.** Nomenclature per F5 Def-2 (inertial mass $M$ / spectral mass $\mu$ — never bare "mass"). Numbers are transcribed, not reinterpreted; where a source and the handover disagree the discrepancy is flagged, not resolved. Status tags follow the ledger's two-layer scheme.

## Entries

### N1 — Squeeze / boost retries recover nothing at single-unit scale  · tier A · V1
- **Tried:** mass-weighted squeeze $S^{(M)}$ retries, raw squeeze, kinetically-matched random kick, and "relax-longer" as recovery moves on a CLU-EBM associative memory (MQAR), gated vs un-gated.
- **Numbers:** $S^{(M)}$ pooled recovery **0.140** vs relax-longer **0.149** ≈ random kick (single seed, `v1-l0-gate §Q2`); un-gated retries *hurt* easy levels, τ-gating repairs. Powered pivot (5 seeds, 90 models) did not revive it.
- **Mechanism:** $S^{(M)}\approx S$ operationally *because learned inertial $M$ is near-uniform* (see N7) — the boost's mass-differentiation had no dynamic range to exploit. "The two failures (no mass hierarchy; retries don't help) are the same fact seen twice."
- **Scope:** single-unit / single-shell, MQAR, laptop scale. NOT a test of squeeze-as-*access* (basin-crossing) — that is a distinct claim (see §8.4 of the primer; paid-access-theory w6/w7).
- **Disposition:** parked for V3-scale multi-shell / mass-banded experiments; appendix-grade ("we own a potentially useful mechanism; where it helps is open") if they fail there too.

### N2 — Abstention-vs-Hopfield unwinnable; Hopfield dominant in all reachable cells  · tier A · V1
- **Tried:** CLU-gate vs modern Hopfield head-to-head on accuracy + calibrated abstention across a capacity×stress regime map (kv 16–96 × correlation ρ≤0.95 × eval-noise σ≤0.9).
- **Numbers:** **26/26 cells `hopfield_dominant`** (`v1-hopfield-stress §Findings`). Hopfield accuracy 0.983–1.0 at low stress ⇒ AURC≈0 ⇒ abstention head-to-head is unwinnable (`v1-pivot §3`). Both stress axes DO break Hopfield (1.0 → ~0.47–0.67) but the CLU-EBM degrades *faster* (storage fidelity 1.0→0.44 by ρ=0.95; noise-fragile basins); Hopfield stays better-calibrated (AURC ≤0.22 vs CLU-gate 0.6–0.82 at max stress). Compute-allocation win collapses 7×→~1× once the workload is uniformly hard. Vanilla side-by-side: Hopfield calibration 0.18→0.88 ≈ CLU 0.43→0.87 (`minus-the-physics B`).
- **Mechanism:** the gap driver is **CLU-EBM memory fidelity, not the gate** — the CLU is out-of-capacity past kv≈32 before stress is applied. A crossover requires a competitive memory first.
- **Scope:** laptop scale, MQAR vocab-256. A harder regime (kv≥128, noisy cues, capacity-stressed Hopfield) is the only place the head-to-head could be winnable — a plan, not a result.
- **Disposition:** V1 short frames as *compute-rationing of an already-accurate conservative memory* + honest boundary map; Hopfield dominance stated plainly. "CLU memory competitiveness at high capacity" named as a V1/ICLR prerequisite workstream.
- **⚠ RE-TIER (w6, `anchor-robustness item 2`; CM-8 → PROVISIONAL):** the "26/26 dominant" map was **under-trained (500 ep)**. At **2000 ep** (4× budget), 3/3 sampled losing cells close entirely — CLU-EBM fidelity **0.40–0.91→1.00**, gated acc **0.05–0.53→0.99–1.00**, **matching/beating Hopfield at 9–10× compute savings** (incl. the kv64 "capacity collapse" = a training-budget artifact, not a capacity wall at kv≤64). But this is **2 seeds × 2 episodes × 3 cells only.** Per the Hub's CM-8 freeze: **DO NOT SHIP EITHER DIRECTION** until the w7 `regime-remap-2000ep` full-grid ≥5-seed re-map at compute parity (Hopfield-budget fairness check). This entry's tier-A prominence and *verdict direction* are both provisional pending w7. See N30 (the anchor does not help memory — a separate finding).
- **⚠ w7 SPLIT (`regime-remap-2000ep` Item 3, COMPLETE; CM-8 refined) — the double-provisional resolves along its two axes:** (i) **COST is now FINAL** — modern Hopfield hits its accuracy ceiling in ~**1 matvec** ($O(kv\cdot d)$; 0.947–0.979 at β≥5, ≤0.003 change over 10× iterations), so it stays the cheaper retriever; the "9–10× savings" was **intra-CLU** (gate vs full-budget CLU, ≥300 Verlet steps), **not** vs Hopfield (now its own entry **N32**). The "unwinnable on cost" statement is settled. (ii) **ACCURACY-reversal is still small-$n$ and grid-pending** — the full ≥5-seed grid is w8 `regime-remap-complete`. So: *cost story FINAL / accuracy story pending w8 grid*. The `regime-remap-2000ep` report itself is **partial** (Item-3 fairness check done; Items 1/2/4 grid still filling). Do not let V1 draft the accuracy-reversal until w8.
- **✅ w8 SETTLED (`regime-remap-2000ep` §w8-completion, full 198-job grid, 0 failures; CM-8 → SETTLED).** The accuracy story is resolved and is **regime-specific, not a general win.** Under-training confirmed (500 ep gate 0.02–0.31 vs Hopfield 0.95–0.98). At convergence CLU storage fidelity → ≈1.0 and the reversal appears, but **only** on clean/correlated cues at **kv≤64** (gate 1.00/0.99 vs Hopfield 0.98/0.97, Δ +0.02, **n=8 pooled**; widens to Δ +0.08…+0.16 at ρ=0.9 **only because Hopfield collapses on correlated keys** 0.72/0.59, not because the CLU rises). Beyond kv64 is an **epoch-budget wall, not a capacity wall** (kv96 closes at 4000 ep +0.03; kv128 only ties; required epochs scale with kv). **Tally at 2000 ep: 6/15 cells close** (all correlation-axis kv≤64); eval-noise axis **0/6**. **Two hard qualifiers now travel with the entry as their own negatives:** the **noise wall** (N37 — 0/6 under cue noise despite fidelity ≈1.0, the dominant negative) and **over-training** (N38 — kv32 1.00→0.89 at 4000 ep). **Cost + noise-robustness both stay Hopfield's** (N32). Net (approved CM-8 wording): *escalatable accuracy under a rationing gate on clean/correlated retrieval at kv≤64; Hopfield keeps the cost AND the cue-noise-robustness advantage.* Tier A retained; the verdict direction is no longer provisional. Output↔handover agree (handover §10 WAVE-8 entry: "CM-8 SETTLED & SPLICED … THE NOISE WALL = the dominant negative").

### N4 — Learned inertial $M$ does not isotropize on symmetric data  · tier A · V2
- **Tried:** falsifiable (v): does learned $M$ self-repair (isotropize) under an SO(2)-symmetric channel, or drift? Measured across the v2-full-runs battery (3rd independent look).
- **Numbers:** **NO — neither** visibly. Kinetic symmetry-breaking is *invisible to the Hessian and to the latch* and shows up only in the charge law, linear in $\lVert[M,X]\rVert$; EP onset slope 0.5165 (pred 0.5) (`v2-full-runs`; "3rd corroboration"). Unequal-$M$ gives a **bounded $O(1)$ Noether-charge non-conservation — an excursion, not a drift** (F5 toy, check g). V2-isotropization-under-mass-lr not re-run (deferred, `mass-lr-doctrine-test §Item4`).
- > **Update (wave-13 curator; source `f5-corrigendum` §2, delivered w12, reconciliation item assigned to this file).** ⚠ **The number "2.6" is RETRACTED and has been removed from this entry.** It was a **running-supremum excursion** $\max_n |L_n - L_0|/|L_0|$, not a drift rate — monotone in the observation window (**2.62 at 10⁵ steps → 2.96 at 10⁶ steps**) and **not reproducible**: two algebraically identical spellings of $\nabla V$ give **2.625 vs 2.734** (the off-ring orbit is a chaotic rosette). Both readings kill "drift". **The negative itself stands and is strengthened** — the corrigendum proves the *inertia* (not merely the rank) is preserved (Sylvester), and the blindness theorem replaces the false $\mu^2 \propto$ splitting corollary. Per C-9 nothing is deleted: the retraction is recorded here rather than the number. **Do not re-introduce "2.6" into any doc or draft.**
- **Mechanism:** Schur/kinetic-isotropy constraint (F5 §4.1): an SO(2) channel requires $M_1=M_2$; unequal inertial masses silently break the channel through the kinetic term, but the standard diagnostics can't see it.
- **Scope:** designed SO(2) testbed, dim 4. The predicted-then-refuted item of Chapter 1.
- **Disposition:** V2 appendix — a measurement-discipline point (measure the charge law, not just Hessian/latch, to detect kinetic breaking).

### N5 — Wake–sleep CD inverts a designed degenerate vacuum (negative → law + cure)  · tier A · V2
- **Tried:** train the designed SO(2) vacuum for the full 1000 epochs (exp-d default) with wake–sleep contrastive divergence.
- **Numbers:** vacuum destroyed **8/8** at 1000 ep; ring depth **+0.079 → −0.126**, $r^*$ **1.0 → 0** (`v2-full-runs Finding 0`, `sleep-erosion-study`). Inversion epoch set by **CD-update frequency racing the wake-clamp schedule, independent of chain length**: ~**116 (f1) / 442 (f5) / 959 (f20)** ep; sleep_steps 50 ≡ 500 (±1 ep); PCD-vs-CD ≤9 ep. Mechanism quantified: 22–31% of initial negatives sit in the ring band → CD raises $V$ there (neg mean $H$ 3.4→12.3 monotone as ring depth falls) → expel (neg radius 1.45→3.9). **Cross-check (`minus-the-physics A`):** broken-volume arm collapses $r^*\to0$ at 150 ep where CLU survives ⇒ CD-vacuum survival is itself a symplecticity payoff. **Demarcation:** non-degenerate Exp-B sine vacuum is IMMUNE (wake+sleep ≈ wake-only; well_gap even higher with sleep). **Cure:** V(data) energy-anchor (λ=10) — ring depth flat +0.068…+0.072 over 1000 ep, $r^*≈0.96$, noise_gap **+0.244 > wake-only +0.199** (preserves prior AND improves noise rejection). Energy-gating on H FAILS (kinetic energy defeats the gate).
- **Mechanism:** CD has no anchor on $V$'s *value*; the wake trajectory-MSE cannot see a flat coset direction, so sleep fills it in. Contrastive divergence on a symmetric landscape is not vacuum-preserving.
- **Scope:** degenerate/flat vacua only (that is the demarcation). Novelty claims (designed-vacuum inversion, degeneracy-specificity, frequency-horizon law, anchor cure) **pending scout confirm** (venue-follow-up #5) — landscape *distortion* itself is classical (Fischer–Igel, Nijkamp).
- **Disposition:** V2 short methods/appendix (placement pending Jul-11 novelty confirm) or candidate standalone short. The anchor is a shippable contribution, not just a caveat.

### N7 — Mass hierarchy is not emergent; designed magnitude never induced  · tier A · V3 (a reframe, not a wall)

On a 2-unit lattice, $\langle\cos\Delta\theta\rangle$/Gibbs = 1.006 / 1.040 / **1.134** at $T$ = 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10, with drift ≈ 0 ⇒ **a genuinely different stationary measure, not a transient.**

### N22 — Friction never stabilizes a saddle; governor blind to isoenergetic escape  · tier A · V2/V3 + F5 note (proven negatives)

- **Numbers:** $\lambda_+>1\ \forall\gamma$; $\min_\gamma(\lambda_+-1)=$**1.4×10⁻⁵**>0; escape rate exact = fitted 1.000112449 (F5 Prop-10, check b). The governor triggers on $H-E^*$ but saddle rolloff is $V\to T$ at constant $H$ ⇒ blind (Prop-11).
- **Mechanism:** damping only *slows* escape (mirror image of the memory law); the *only* levers that bound expanding/isoenergetic modes are curvature control of $V_\theta$ (a *working* Lyapunov reg — N17) and the relativistic velocity cap $v^{\max}_i=c/\sqrt{M_i}$.
- **Scope:** exact, all modes. Reshapes V3's depth-stability story ("no vanishing, but explosion is real; only curvature + $c$ contain it").
- **Disposition:** Tier A — these are the "two negative results" already in the F5 arXiv note §5; V3 must state which forgetting column it assumes.

### N23 — Wormhole smooth z-gate mis-routes ~10–12%; calibrated head over-routes local at N=8  · tier B · V1
- **Tried:** energy-gated sparse non-local routing on a chain lattice (smooth z-gate arm and a calibrated-head arm), N∈{4,8}, 2 seeds.
- **Numbers:** smooth z-gate mis-routes ~**10–12%** (12/96 each way at N=4) ⇒ gated distant accuracy 0.875/0.729 < 1.0 even though the *mechanism* delivers distant perfectly when it routes (calibrated distant = 1.000, AUROC(head)=1.00 at N=4). At N=8 the learned head over-routes local (local precision 0.500) ⇒ balanced smooth gate (0.812) beats the head (0.750) overall (`v1-wormhole-routing §4`).
- **Mechanism:** raw/normalized residual R is a strong-but-imperfect gate (third confirmation of "raw R needs calibration"); the write-time head's impostor composition degrades as N grows.
- **Scope:** 2 seeds, easy difficulty band, single archive/edge — indicative, not powered. The mechanism (gated 0.875/0.812 vs 0.50 ceilings; 1-hop beats N−1-hop chain) is the positive result; also blocked from headline until a **router-MLP baseline (P9)** exists.
- **Disposition:** V1 pillar-3 appendix caveat + impostor-composition study queued. **w6 extension:** the router-MLP baseline this entry was "blocked until" now exists (P9) and the router *wins* (see N24); the mis-routing % here is superseded as a headline by N24's cleaner FLOPs+accuracy comparison, but remains the mechanism-level routing-error caveat.

### N24 — Energy-gated wormhole LOSES to a physics-free learned router  · tier A · V1 · (the CM-7 reversal)
- **Tried:** the boring baseline the wormhole must beat — a parameter-matched (449-param, 2-layer, physics-free) learned router MLP on the raw query cue, vs the energy-gated wormhole, ≥5 seeds, non-50/50 workloads, cost measured in FLOPs.
- **Numbers:** the router **wins in FLOPs AND accuracy at both N and every workload mix** — router **1.000±0.000 / 0.948±0.070** (N=4/N=8) @ **8.81e7 FLOP/query** vs gated **0.887±0.139 / 0.715±0.172** @ **1.18e8**; router AUROC(→distant) = **1.000** vs energy-residual R0 AUROC 0.963/0.865, calibrated head 0.999/0.907 (`v1-router-baseline §1`). Per-mix {50/50, 80/20, 95/5}: router leads on accuracy AND FLOPs throughout. The **old 2-seed gated 0.812 was optimistic** (true N=8 gated 0.715).
- **Mechanism:** the embedding is (near-)linearly separable by which unit's key-cluster the cue sits in (disjoint per-unit keys), so the router learns local-vs-distant trivially, while the energy gate must *discover the same partition via relaxation* and does so more noisily. **Physics buys nothing over the cheap classifier on this task** — a clean CM-2/CM-3 confirmation ("energy ≈/< a learned signal; the gate mechanism is memory-agnostic"). Energy-as-routing-signal is now **forbidden** — the third instance of the pattern (after N3/CM-3, N21).
- **Scope:** MQAR-style, N≤8, laptop; **task-difficulty ceiling drives the router's dominance** (linearly-separable cues). A harder band (overlapping key clusters / higher kv-per-unit / smaller embed_dim) is the fair stress test of whether energy *ever* adds value — untested; honest read is "on the laptop testbed it does not."
- **Disposition:** **V1 appendix (tier A), and the CM-7 rewrite driver.** Reframe the routing pillar to CM-2: the salvaged, physics-independent claim is the **1-hop edge (flat 1.18e8 FLOP) ≫ N-hop chain (1.76e8→2.94e8, distant acc 0.41→0.28)** — claim the direct edge as the mechanism, never the energy gating of it.

### N25 — Learned friction field γ_φ does NOT recover the fit gap  · tier B · V2/V3 · (the wrong-tool lesson)
- **Tried:** the +γ_φ learned-field rung of the fit-gap recovery ladder (K=2 learned field, sleep phase on) — can targeted friction buy back the contraction-forbidden fit the twin steals?
- **Numbers:** **−24 %** (eval-MSE 0.2548 vs the CLU-conservative 0.2066 baseline; twin gap = 0.202, so the rung is *below* the γ=0 floor) (`fit-gap-anatomy item 3`). By contrast **+γ global recovers 92 %** of the same gap with BIBO (1.0), latch (0.778) and flat μ² (5.2e-3) all preserved.
- **Mechanism:** γ_φ is a *targeted-forgetting* tool (Thread 1: leakage↓200×), not a fit lever — the stationary circle-vacuum task has **no trash region to forget**, so pushing γ_φ up at hallucinations while protecting data doesn't reduce reconstruction error (it slightly perturbs V; μ² rises to 2.1e-2). **The paid mechanisms are not interchangeable — match the cheat to the mechanism** (γ_global buys contraction fit; γ_φ buys selective forgetting).
- **Scope:** stationary circle-vacuum, dim 4, 3 seeds. **Caveat (source-stated):** this rung retrained from scratch with the sleep phase on, so it is not a perfectly matched single-knob delta from the γ=0 model — the qualitative "wrong tool" verdict is robust, the exact −24 % is not.
- **Disposition:** appendix "mechanisms are not interchangeable" panel (feeds the CM-1 recovery ladder in all shorts' Pareto frame).

### N26 — CLU is NOT the lowest long-horizon plateau  · tier A · all (CM-1 scope guard)
- **Tried:** the fit-vs-horizon loan curve (cumulative MSE, matched-parameter arms: chlu 4549 / broken_volume 4557 / twin 4551 / LSTM), stationary circle-vacuum, 3 seeds.
- **Numbers:** at horizon 5000 the twin **diverges to 196** (loan called ~700 steps) but **broken-vol plateaus at 0.14 and LSTM at 0.13, both BELOW CLU's 0.22** (`fit-gap-anatomy item 2`). So "physics costs raw fit" persists as a *small steady-state penalty* even long-horizon — CLU is bounded, not lowest-MSE.
- **Mechanism:** LSTM stays bounded by tanh saturation, broken-vol by its learned near-contraction; CLU is bounded *by construction* (symplectic, no attractor guarantee needed). Boundedness ≠ lowest plateau.
- **Scope:** stationary synthetic vacuum, dim 4, laptop. The crossing (~700 steps) and the divergence are seed-stable.
- **Disposition:** **CM-1 scope guard for every short** — DO claim the loan-crossing + boundedness-by-construction; **do NOT claim CLU has the lowest long-horizon plateau.** Prevents an over-read of the Pareto frame. (A negative that disciplines a headline, not a failure.)

### N27 — Reach-pricing is real but secondary + not locally concentrated  · tier B · V1/V3
- **Tried:** isolate the reach-priced term of the fit gap — a relativistic arm with the causal cap *active* (the arm w5 lacked) swept over c on a high-velocity shuttle task (required peak latent speed A·ω = 2.0), 3 seeds.
- **Numbers:** MSE rises monotonically as v_max = c/√M falls below req (**+77 % at c=0.5**, +53 % at c=1) and **collapses to the uncapped baseline once v_max ≥ req** (c≥2, MSE ≈ newtonian 1.48). BUT: (i) **no per-step far-region concentration** — corr(err, |q̇|) ≈ 0 (−0.01…+0.05), high-velocity-quartile error ≈ low-velocity-quartile; (ii) the reach increment (≤+1.0) rides on a **large ~1.4 representation floor** that no single conservative unit clears (`fit-gap-anatomy item 1`).
- **Mechanism:** the cap degrades the *whole* autonomous rollout globally (the capped orbit drifts as a whole rather than clipping at peaks). Reach-pricing is fundamentally a **lattice** phenomenon (sync ∝ √κ across units, F5 §7.2), not a single-unit effect — which is exactly why intra-unit reach (N31-adjacent, paid-access) is a genuine unfilled gap.
- **Scope:** single-unit, dim 2, synthetic shuttle, laptop. A reach task a single unit *can* fit (lower A·ω) would sharpen the increment.
- **Disposition:** V1/V3 appendix — decomposes CM-1: contraction-forbidden is dominant, reach real-but-secondary-and-aggregate-only. Feeds the w7 lattice-reach follow-up.

### N28 — masslr_init induce-then-snap band selection is fragile  · tier B · V3
- **Tried:** the optimizer-native alternative to the spectral band selector — induce ordering with mass_lr_mult=10 for 150 ep, snap masses to oracle magnitudes in the induced order, freeze mass, retrain (5 seeds, 2-unit, 16× ratio, 300 ep).
- **Numbers:** eval-MSE **3.527 ± 4.493** vs oracle/selector **1.180 ± 0.216** — induced the correct ordering on **4/5 seeds** (those → MSE 1.09–1.52 ≈ oracle), but **seed 2 inverted the ordering → snapped to the anti-band → MSE 12.5** (the full mis-banded penalty, N8-class), driving mean/variance up (`v3-band-selection item 2/4`).
- **Mechanism:** the induce-then-snap recipe inherits the induction's ordering errors *catastrophically* — snapping to a wrong ordering is exactly designing-in the anti-band. This documents **why the spectral FFT selector (MSE gap 0.000, 5/5) is preferred** over the optimizer-native one.
- **Scope:** 2-unit, 16× ratio, one recipe realization.
- **Disposition:** V3 appendix — the "fragile foil" against which the spectral selector is the recommended method (CM-11).

### N29 — Anchor cure not seed-bulletproof at λ≤10  · tier B · V2
- **Tried:** the V(data)-anchor envelope over λ × 5 seeds × 3000 erosive epochs on the exp-d SO(2) vacuum.
- **Numbers:** at **λ=10** one seed (s45) fully collapses (**r*=0, ring_depth −1.42**) while 4/5 are clean (r*≈0.87–0.89); at **λ=1** the vacuum holds 5/5 but wake MSE blows up on 2/5 seeds (s43/s45, wake→3.5). Only **λ=100 is bulletproof 5/5** (r*=0.911±0.016), at ~35× wake-MSE cost and halved noise rejection (0.60 vs λ=10's 1.85) (`anchor-robustness item 1`).
- **Mechanism:** a seed-specific training instability (seed-45 pathology) that stronger anchoring (λ=100) suppresses but weaker anchoring does not eliminate — the anchor *reduces but does not remove* training-instability risk at λ≤10.
- **Scope:** exp-d SO(2), dim 4, 5 seeds, 3000 ep, f32 training. A λ-fine-sweep {10,30,100} × ≥8 seeds to locate the smallest stable λ is the recommended follow-up.
- **Disposition:** V2 appendix caveat on the anchor "cure validated" claim — state as "robust for λ∈[1,100], seed-bulletproof only at λ=100 (~35× wake cost)."

### N30 — V(data)-anchor does NOT transfer to memory-fidelity  · tier B · V1
- **Tried:** apply the SO(2)-vacuum anchor cure as a *memory-fidelity* intervention on three losing Hopfield-stress cells (anchor to epoch-0 per-pattern energies), 2 seeds × 2 episodes.
- **Numbers:** anchor **does not help** — kv32 anchor fidelity **0.44±0.02 < baseline 0.66±0.18**; kv64 anchor **0.51±0.12 ≈ baseline 0.40±0.05**, both with gate acc ≈ baseline or worse (`anchor-robustness item 2`). (By contrast, *longer training* 500→2000 ep closes the gap entirely — that is the positive; the anchor is orthogonal.)
- **Mechanism:** the memory EBM has **no designed epoch-0 structure to anchor to** — pinning stored-pattern energies to their *random-init* values is meaningless (unlike the SO(2) ring, a designed structural prior). The anchor is the right tool for **designed degenerate vacua**, the wrong tool for **capacity/retrieval-limited memory**.
- **Scope:** MQAR memory, kv≤64, 2 seeds × 2 episodes, laptop. A warm-start or variance-only anchor was not tried (low priority — longer training already closes the gap).
- **Disposition:** V1/V2 appendix — the honest boundary on the anchor's scope (designed-vacuum cure ≠ memory-fidelity cure). Pairs with N2's provisional re-tier.

### N31 — State-dependent jump-gate breaks volume by ∇g·Δ  · tier B · V1/V3 + F5 (design guard, proven)
- **Tried:** analysis of a *smoothly state-modulated* intra-unit wormhole jump q' = q + g(q)Δ (a plausible "soft gate" for the paid-access wormhole).
- **Numbers:** ∂q'/∂q = I + Δ(∇g)ᵀ ⇒ by the matrix-determinant lemma **det J = 1 + ∇g·Δ ≠ 1** in general (`paid-access-theory` Prop-A6, verified check C to 2.2×10⁻¹⁶). A *constant* translation q→q+Δ keeps det J = 1 exactly.
- **Mechanism:** a state-dependent multiplier on the jump is an **unpaid contraction (Thread-8 cheat (i)) sneaking through the back door** — it silently breaks the volume law the whole primitive rests on.
- **Scope:** analytic/proven; applies to any intra-unit wormhole construction. **Design rule for the engineer:** freeze the gate over the jump epoch (hard gate held constant → det J=1, pay only the energy ledger) OR make the gate a smooth term *inside V_θ* (throat construction, escape-aid only) — never a state-dependent multiplier on Δ.
- **Disposition:** F5 note / paid-access §7 design guard; V1/V3 appendix. A *proven* negative that constrains the mechanism design (like N22).

### N32 — CLU-gate does NOT beat Hopfield on COST (the intra-CLU-savings correction)  · tier A · V1
- **Tried:** the reviewer fairness question "did you give Hopfield the same budget?" — sweep modern-Hopfield retrieval ($z_{t+1}=\mathrm{softmax}(\beta z_t X^\top)X$, key-half clamped each step) over iteration-count × β, corr=0, 3 seeds × 3 episodes, and compare its cost floor to the gated CLU.
- **Numbers:** at **β≥5 Hopfield hits its accuracy ceiling in a SINGLE matvec** — N128/kv32 0.976, N256/kv64 0.967–0.969, N384/kv96 0.941–0.950; **10× more iterations change accuracy by ≤0.003** (only weak β=2 benefits from iter 1→2, converging by iter 2) (`regime-remap-2000ep §3`). Hopfield cost floor = **1 matvec, $O(kv\cdot d)$**; the *gated* CLU runs **≥300 Verlet steps**, each a potential-MLP forward+grad.
- **Mechanism:** the "9–10× savings" reported at 2000 ep (N2 w6 re-tier) is **CLU-gate-vs-CLU-full-budget** (3000 Verlet steps) — an *intra-CLU compute-rationing* number, **NOT** savings relative to Hopfield. At matched accuracy Hopfield is the cheaper retriever; "matching Hopfield" means the gate *reaches* Hopfield's accuracy, not that it does so at lower cost.
- **Scope:** laptop, corr=0, kv∈{32,64,96}, MQAR vocab-256. Cost story is **FINAL** (Item-3 complete); the *accuracy-reversal* (N2) is still grid-pending (w8 `regime-remap-complete`).
- **Disposition:** **V1 appendix (tier A)** — the honest cost framing for the CLU-vs-Hopfield map. The V1 short must say plainly: the compute-rationing advantage is against a full-budget CLU; Hopfield is cheaper per query. Pairs with N2 (the accuracy axis) and the CM-2/CM-3 "physics buys nothing over a cheap baseline" pattern (N3, N21, N24).

### N33 — Reversible O(1)-memory BPTT is exact only at γ=0  · tier B · V3
- **Tried:** the adopted V3/ICLR claim "γ=0 lattice training admits reversible O(1)-memory recompute-backwards BPTT" — measure the exactness of the leapfrog inversion at γ=0 and the horizon degradation at γ>0 (round-trip: T forward then T inverse steps, error on the recovered init).
- **Numbers:** at **γ=0** the reconstruction error is pure float accumulation (float64: 9.1e-17 @T=16 → 3.3e-15 @T=1024 → 2.0e-13 @T=16384; float32: 2.5e-6 @T=1024) — no structural blow-up. At **γ>0** the $(1-\gamma)$ contraction is invertible only in exact arithmetic and amplifies error as $(1-\gamma)^{-n}$ ⇒ finite usable reversal horizon (rel-err <1e-6): **float64 ≈ 3.3e4 @γ=1e-3, 4.1e3 @γ=1e-2, 5e2 @γ=0.05, 1.3e2 @γ=0.1; ~100× shorter in float32** (`v3-reversible-o1` Item 1). Beyond the horizon error explodes geometrically (float64 γ=0.05: 8e-12 @T=256 → 21 @T=1024 → 2e51 @T=4096 → inf).
- **Mechanism:** dissipation is a deliberate volume-losing map; its inverse *inflates* momenta by $1/(1-\gamma)$ each step, so any float error is amplified geometrically. The property that makes γ>0 a *forgetting* knob is exactly what makes it un-reversible in finite precision.
- **Scope:** untrained models, CPU, D≤16, laptop; the *memory* $O(1)$-vs-$O(T)$ ratio (946× @T=1024) is structural and generalizes, the exactness caveat is precision-bound.
- **Disposition:** V3/ICLR appendix — the honest boundary on the reversible-training claim: *"reversibly-O(1)-trainable memory = the conservative (γ=0) memory."* Dissipative segments fall back to stored activations / gradient checkpointing. Not a failure — the scope clause that keeps CM-13 clean, and it dovetails the γ=0-memory / γ>0-forgetting budget framing.

### N34 — Squeeze reach is a bracket, not a knife-edge at L  · tier B · V1
- **Tried:** the falsifiable heart of the paid-access reach test — does the squeeze's landing rate step from 1 to 0 exactly as the target distance $d$ crosses the causal box $L$?
- **Numbers:** the squeeze landing edge sits at **$d\approx3.2$**, not exactly $L=2.5$ — landing rate {1,1,1,1,**0,0**} over $d\in\{0.8,1.6,2.4,3.2,4.0,5.0\}$ (`paid-access-experiments §7.1`). The crossover is a two-sided **bracket $[L,\,L+p_0\sinh\zeta/M_0]$**, not a step at $L$.
- **Mechanism:** a squeeze grants an instantaneous *displacement* $(p_0/M_0)\sinh\zeta$ (Def-A10 term (i)) *on top of* the capped flow — so the squeezed state can land slightly beyond $L$ before the causal cap dominates. This *matches* theory (Def-A10), it does not contradict it — but it softens the clean "squeeze drops to 0 for $d>L$" wording.
- **Scope:** dim 2 & 4, band [4.0,0.25], γ=0. A sharper knife-edge would use a heavier reach coord (smaller displacement) or measure reach from squeezed-momentum only.
- **Disposition:** V1 appendix / CM-12 inherited caveat — **state the bracket $[L, L+p_0\sinh\zeta/M_0]$**, not a step at $L$. The load-bearing claim survives: squeeze reach is **bounded** (fails $d=4,5$), wormhole reach is not. An honesty caveat that disciplines the headline, not a failure.

### N35 — Learned entrance-steering for paid-access channels is unsolved  · tier A · V1
- **Tried:** the paid-access battery (wormhole + squeeze) was run with **oracle** channel placement — entrances/exits placed by construction. Learning *where* to open a channel was explicitly out of scope.
- **Numbers:** none — this is a **scoped-out** capability, flagged as `paid-access-theory` **open-risk 1** and reiterated by `paid-access-experiments §Open-3`: *"learned entrance-steering is explicitly out of scope (theory open-risk 1) and remains the true engineering crux / likely failure point at scale."*
- **Mechanism:** the certificates (det J=1, ledger, latch transport) all assume a *given* channel; a learned, state-conditioned placement policy risks re-introducing the state-dependent-gate volume break (N31) and has no certificate yet. This is where the physics-specific win could fail to translate to a trained system.
- **Scope:** all paid-access results are oracle-placement; the ICLR long is where learned steering must be solved at scale.
- **Disposition:** **V1 appendix (tier A) + explicit future work.** Head decision (2026-07-08): V1 ships as an ML4PS position/theory paper leading with the *certificate-backed* oracle-placement win; **learned entrance-steering = named future work, addressed at scale in the ICLR long.** The single most important open risk for the pillar-4 story.

### N36 — (process) v2-referee caught a genuine §3.4↔App D contradiction pre-submission  · tier C · V2 (process negative)
- **Tried:** adversarial pre-submission review of the V2 short (`v2-referee`) — cross-reading the emergent-lifetime numbers across §3.3 table, §3.4 prose, and Appendix D.
- **Numbers:** §3.4 claims "measured $n_{1/2}=277/257/303$ vs prediction $247/227/263$ — a **consistent +12–28%** bias" (computed ratios **1.121/1.132/1.152 = +12–15%**), but Appendix D's per-seed ratios are **1.125/1.288/1.052 (+12.5/+28.8/+5.2%)** — the "+28" is imported from a *different* number set (App D seed-44), and one seed at **+5.2%** falls *outside* the advertised band, so "consistent" is false against the paper's own appendix. The softest emergent μ² also disagrees (§3.4 max $5.9\times10^{-2}$ vs App D $1.07\times10^{-1}$) (`v2-referee` MF-3).
- **Mechanism:** §3.4 (source `v2-full-runs` item 4/5) and App D (`v2-prefreeze-baselines` item 4) are *different probes* on the same emergent checkpoints, presented as if App D "decomposes" §3.4's exact triple. This is exactly the M4/CM-7 cross-section contradiction the flag-provenance discipline exists to prevent — **caught pre-submission**, not by a reviewer.
- **Scope:** a drafting/consistency defect (not a scientific negative); MUST-FIX before V2 submission. Also logged by the referee: a fresh predictor-substitution attack (SF-1 — the Mo head-to-head "predicts" with the exact Jacobian gap, not Mo's own estimator).
- **Disposition:** **internal process record (tier C)** — evidence that the adversarial-referee stage works, and a reminder that differently-sourced numbers on the same checkpoints must be reconciled to one coherent range before drafting. Fixed in w8 `v2-revision` (MF-3). Not a paper-appendix item; a program-hygiene note.

### N37 — The noise wall: the CLU gate never reaches Hopfield under cue noise  · tier A · V1  (THE headline V1 negative)
- **Tried:** the 2000-ep clean-cue accuracy-reversal (N2) re-run under **eval-noise** cue corruption σ∈{0.3,0.6}, capacity kv∈{32,64,96}, 5 seeds (paired 500 vs 2000 ep).
- **Numbers:** **0/6 cells close at any capacity, even kv32** — gate acc vs Hopfield: at **σ=0.3** kv32 0.90 vs 0.94 (Δ −0.05), kv64 0.81 vs 0.89 (−0.08), kv96 0.62 vs 0.85 (−0.23); at **σ=0.6** kv32 0.36 vs 0.71 (**Δ −0.35**), kv64 0.29 vs 0.57 (−0.28), kv96 0.19 vs 0.52 (−0.33). CLU **storage fidelity is still ≈1.0** in every cell (`regime-remap-2000ep §w8` Item 1-stress / Item 4).
- **Mechanism:** the patterns are stored (fidelity 1.0) but the **governed relaxation gate is markedly less robust to cue corruption than Hopfield's single matvec** — the relaxation likely over-commits to the noisy cue. This is a *readout/dynamics* fragility, not a storage-capacity failure.
- **Scope:** laptop, MQAR vocab-256, f32, `langevin_noise=legacy`. The axis most relevant to real retrieval — an FDT-correct sampler / noise-aware τ / longer relax budget / denoising init are untested mitigations.
- **Disposition:** **V1 appendix (tier A) — travels with EVERY accuracy-reversal claim.** The source analyst calls it "the sharpest negative in the study" and "the V1-narrative threat to settle before ICLR." The V1 short must state the reversal is a **clean/correlated-cue phenomenon that dies under cue noise**. Pairs with N2 (the reversal it qualifies) and N32 (cost). Diagnosing the noise-robustness gap is the top recommended next experiment.

### N38 — Small CLU memories over-train past their saturation epoch  · tier B · V1
- **Tried:** the epoch-scaling frontier {500,1000,2000,4000} ep × kv{32,64,96,128}, corr=0, n=3 (`regime-remap-2000ep §w8` Item 2).
- **Numbers:** kv32 gate acc **1.00 (2000 ep) → 0.89±0.05 (4000 ep)** — falling below its own Hopfield 0.976 (Δ −0.09). Fidelity also softens 1.00→0.99. Larger cells still improving at 4000 ep, so **there is no single epoch at which all four kv simultaneously beat Hopfield** — each capacity has its own optimum (kv32 ~1000, kv64 ~2000, kv96/128 ~4000).
- **Mechanism:** past the saturation epoch the PCD-trained EBM degrades (over-fitting the small stored set); the compute–fidelity frontier is a **diagonal ridge**, not a monotone ceiling.
- **Scope:** kv32 at 4000 ep, n=3 (std non-trivial). Laptop/MQAR/f32.
- **Disposition:** V1 appendix + a design lesson: **early-stop on write-time fidelity** would save compute and avoid the regression. Qualifies the "just train longer" reading of N2.

### N39 — Non-monotone intermediate-epoch fidelity dip at large kv  · tier C · V1
- **Tried:** same epoch-scaling frontier (`regime-remap-2000ep §w8` Item 2).
- **Numbers:** storage fidelity is **non-monotone in epochs** for large kv — kv96 **0.39 (500) → 0.24 (1000) → 0.97 (2000)**; kv128 **0.40 → 0.09 (1000) → 0.71 (2000)**. Fidelity gets *worse* before it gets better.
- **Mechanism:** a transient PCD/buffer instability at intermediate epochs for large kv (self-heals by 2000 ep). Flagged to the engineer as a training-curve smoothness note, not a blocker.
- **Scope:** kv≥96, 1000-ep point, n=3, laptop.
- **Disposition:** internal caveat — **do not read the 1000-ep checkpoint as monotone progress** when reporting the frontier; a smoother buffer schedule is a cheap follow-up.

### N40 — "≈4× longer retention" does not survive compute normalization (it inverts)  · tier A · V2
- **Tried:** the V2 headline "CLU-emergent retains 263 vs LSTM 69 map-steps ≈ 4× longer" re-expressed in compute units (retention_steps × per-step cost), per-step cost measured directly (`v2-referee-experiments` SF-2).
- **Numbers:** one CLU dissipative-Verlet step (h64, dim4, KDK, 2 ∇_qV backprops) = **36148 FLOPs / 1554 ns**; LSTM cell (h16) = 2512 / 252; LEM cell (h16) = 2400 / 500. Per-step CLU/LSTM = **14.4× FLOPs, 6.2× wall**; CLU/LEM = 15.1× / 3.1×. **Retention-per-compute INVERTS: 23.5× more wall (54.8× FLOPs) vs LSTM, 14.6× wall (70.7× FLOPs) vs LEM.**
- **Mechanism:** map-steps are the physics-native unit; the Verlet step is intrinsically expensive (two potential-gradient evals). Per unit of retention the CLU spends ≈15–24× the wall of the RNN it "beats."
- **Scope:** single-core CPU, XLA, batch-1; **not width-matched** (CLU h64 vs baselines h16 — the dominant confound; a width-matched CLU would narrow but not flip the sign, which rests on the two backprops). The 263/69/56 retention numbers are themselves from those exact configs, so this is the honest apples-to-apples for those results.
- **Disposition:** **retire the "≈4× longer" as a compute claim (CM-4 amended).** Lead §3.3 with the **qualitative structural triad** (latch / μ⁻² budget law / bounded drift) — architecture- and compute-independent, and the stronger claim. If a compute line is kept, state the honest per-step ≈6×(LSTM)/≈3×(LEM) wall factor. A negative that disciplines a headline, not a scientific failure.

### N41 — Certified squeeze-MH retry erodes the latch unless coset-projected  · tier B · V1 + F5  (design-rule negative, proven)
- **Tried:** analysis of whether the squeeze+Metropolis retry kernel (Thread-9) preserves stored coset memory under repeated certified retries (`thread9-mh-kernel` Part 3, Check 3).
- **Numbers:** the Gibbs measure is exactly flat along the Goldstone coset, so a coset-tangent proposal has ΔH=0 and is **accepted with probability 1** → the register random-walks: $D_\varphi=\tfrac12 s^2$/step, $\mathrm{Var}(\varphi_N)=s^2N$, erased after $N_{\rm erode}\approx(\Delta_{\rm read}/s)^2$ (verified accept=1.000, D=**1.29e-3** vs predicted 1.25e-3; off-coset proposal D=0 exactly). **Critical:** the w7 charge-preservation certificate (isotropic squeeze ΔQ=1.2e-7) does **NOT** protect the coset *position* — with momentum refresh the isotropic squeeze diffuses φ strongly (**D=1.7e-2**). **Charge-preservation ≠ position-preservation.**
- **Mechanism:** no restoring force along a broken continuous symmetry ⇒ unbounded diffusion of the order-parameter phase (Mermin–Wagner-flavoured). The conserved charge Q is the conjugate momentum, not the stored register φ.
- **Scope:** toy EBMs (numpy f64); the erosion budget is exact for the analysed kernel. Δ_read on trained MQAR checkpoints is unmeasured (needed to make N_erode concrete) — w9 spec item.
- **Disposition:** **F5 / V1 design guard (like N22/N31, a proven negative that constrains the mechanism).** The fix is to run the certified kernel in the **coset-orthogonal complement** (project proposals off the coset tangent) → latch quenched, moved only by explicit writes. Any V1 MH paragraph must either adopt the projection or quote N_erode as an explicit retry cap. Also states the honest deflation (CM-3): MH's asset is the *certificate*, not parameter parsimony or performance.

### N47 — ⛔ BLOCKING: `fdt` noise has a NaN gradient at γ=0 (no FDT-correct model has ever been trainable at repo defaults)  · tier A · all (physics-audit ¶)
- **Tried:** `xy-lattice-theory` §5(i-b) attempted to train an FDT-correct lattice — the blocking prerequisite for every Thread-10 experiment.
- **Numbers:** `integrators.py:~170` computes `noise_scale = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(0.0, m_eff * temperature * gamma * (2.0 - gamma)))`. At **γ = 0** this is `sqrt(0)`, whose derivative w.r.t. the **learnable `log_mass`** inside `m_eff` is `∞·0 = NaN`. Measured: `losses[0] = 145.99` (finite), **`losses[1:] = NaN`**, all parameters NaN. Reproduced on a plain `CHLU` **and** on `CLULattice`. **Still live at HEAD `d6f8bac`** (post-`fix-pack-5`; orthogonal bug).
  - grad NaN @ γ=0: `newtonian_learned` **True**, `relativistic` **True**, `newtonian_identity` False. @ γ=1e-12 and γ=0.05: False for all three.
- **Trigger — all four conditions, and three of them are repo defaults:** `langevin_noise="fdt"` (the only non-default) · `sleep_temperature = 0.5` (default ⇒ sleep uses `stochastic_step`) · `sleep_friction = 0.0` (**default**) · a `log_mass`-carrying kinetic mode. Since `epoch % sleep_frequency == 0` always fires at epoch 0, **`train_chlu` NaNs every parameter on the first sleep step.**
- **Mechanism:** `legacy` is immune *only* because its sqrt argument (`2γT·dt`) contains **no parameter**, so JAX never back-propagates through it. `newtonian_identity` is immune (no learnable inertial $M$).
- **Scope:** **⇒ No FDT-correct model can currently be trained at repo defaults.** Blocks the 2-D KT experiment, the `T_φ(q)` build, and **every Gibbs-sampling claim**. It does **not** contaminate any stored result (no `projects/*/config/config.yaml` sets `langevin_noise`; `fix-pack-5`'s audit found zero contamination) — it means the experiments were never *runnable*, not that they ran wrong.
- **Disposition:** **tier A — physics-audit paragraph; the program's highest-priority code item.** → `fix-pack-6`. Fix verified bit-identical on the `arg>0` branch with gradient `0.0` (not NaN) at `arg==0`:
  ```python
  arg  = m_eff * temperature * gamma * (2.0 - gamma)
  safe = jnp.where(arg > 0.0, arg, 1.0)
  noise_scale = jnp.where(arg > 0.0, jnp.sqrt(safe), 0.0)
  ```
  **Methodological note for the appendix:** the bug is a *gradient* pathology invisible to any forward-value test — the shipped expression's **value** is correct at γ=0. It survived because nothing ever differentiated it.

### N48 — `GatedCoupling` returns the mean energy, not the free energy (the shipped wormhole repels its endpoints)  · tier B · V1/V3 + F5 (design guard, proven)
- **Tried:** `xy-lattice-theory` §6.1–6.2 derived the exact annealed average of a discrete Ising gate $\sigma_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ with edge Hamiltonian $H_e = \sigma(v-t)$ at gate-temperature $w$, and compared it to the shipped `GatedCoupling.__call__`.
- **Numbers:** The gate **is** exactly the annealed Ising bond: $\langle\sigma\rangle = \mathrm{sigmoid}((t-v)/w)$. But its **free energy** is $F(v) = -w\,\mathrm{softplus}((t-v)/w)$, with $\partial F/\partial v = \langle\sigma\rangle$ = the annealed **mean force** (verified to 2.3e-10; force ∈ [0,1] everywhere, always attractive). The code instead returns $\langle\sigma\rangle\cdot v$ (the mean **energy**), whose force is $\langle\sigma\rangle - (v/w)\langle\sigma\rangle(1-\langle\sigma\rangle)$ (verified to 1.5e-9) and which:
  - **changes sign at `v = 0.8020`** — *inside* the nominally-open region ($v < t = 1.0$, repo defaults `t=1.0, w=0.25`), reaching a minimum of **−0.718**. $V_{\rm wh}(v)$ is **non-monotone** ⇒ **the shipped wormhole repels its endpoints** over a finite range of separations.
  - On an XY bond $v(\Delta\theta) = J(1-\cos\Delta\theta)$ with $(J,t,w) = (0.1, 0.05, 0.02)$: shipped $J_1 = \mathbf{-0.0072}$, $J_2 = +0.0048$, $J_3 = +0.0078$ — **the effective exchange flips antiferromagnetic** — vs the correct free energy $J_1 = \mathbf{+0.0223}$, $J_2 = +0.0123$, $J_3 = +0.0040$ (ungated: $J_1 = +0.1000$, no harmonics). **A wormhole array built on the shipped gate would frustrate itself.**
- **Mechanism:** confusing $\langle H\rangle$ with $F = -w\ln Z$. The gradient of the mean energy is not the mean force whenever the gate's occupancy depends on $v$.
- **Scope — NOT contaminating (Hub audited the blast radius directly).** `GatedCoupling` is constructed only for `wormhole_edges` in `build_lattice`, which **nothing calls outside `v3-lattice-build`'s smoke**; **V1's wormhole uses its own held sigmoid on `R0` with `channel_spring_coupling`**, so its force is $g\cdot\nabla v$ — no pathology. **A latent trap, not a live defect.**
- **Disposition:** **tier B** — same class as N31 (state-dependent jump-gate breaks volume): a **proven design guard** on an un-shipped path. Promote to **tier A** the moment any wormhole-array result ships. **Fix:** return `-width * jax.nn.softplus((threshold - v) / width)`; keep the old expression behind a flag. → `fix-pack-6` / `lattice-xy-prereqs`.
- **⭐ The methodological lesson (this is the part worth an appendix paragraph):** `v3-lattice-build`'s smoke checked the gate's **energy** suppression (5 orders) and **never its force** — that is why this was invisible for eleven waves. *A gate is a force law, not a number. Test the derivative of everything you gate with.* (Companion to N47, whose value was right and whose *gradient* was NaN — **two defects in one wave, both in the derivative nobody tested.**)

### N49 — `spring_coupling`'s default random `W` breaks the lattice's global U(1) (and a trained lattice does not learn an XY exchange)  · tier A · V3/Thread-10
- **Tried:** `xy-lattice-theory` §2.5/§2.7 — (a) harmonic decomposition of the shipped `spring_coupling` at random init (400 inits); (b) two students, identical but for the coupling's **initial** projections (both fully learnable), trained 400 wake-only epochs on data from a **ground-truth XY lattice** (`J_true = 2κr*² = 0.100000`, exact global U(1)), 3 seeds.
- **Numbers:**
  - **At init** (`W ~ N(0, 0.1²)`): `coupling_dim k=2` → **P(J<0) = 0.517** (the exchange is antiferromagnetic *half the time*), median `h₂/|J| = 1.00`, median U(1)-breaking/`|J|` = **1.48**. `k=3` → 0.550 / 1.08 / 1.56.
  - **After 400 epochs, generic (repo default):** `J/J_true` = **+0.019, +0.018, −0.004** (one seed learns the **wrong sign**), `h₂/|J|` = 0.613, 0.713, 2.148, U(1)-break/`|J|` = 0.803, 1.234, 1.864.
  - **After 400 epochs, conformal init (`W = 𝟙₂`):** `J/J_true` = **+1.034, +1.070, +1.037**, `h₂/|J|` = **0.0134, 0.0053, 0.0169**, U(1)-break/`|J|` ≤ 0.0337 — **at equal-or-better wake loss** (seed 0: **0.01032** conformal vs 0.02631 generic; seeds 1–2 statistically indistinguishable). **The symmetry is free; no fit is paid for it.**
  - **Training repairs U(1) only very slowly:** a 3.75× budget (400 → 1500 ep, generic seed 0) moves `J/J_true` 0.019 → 0.074 and `h₂/|J|` 0.613 → 0.262 — nowhere near converged.
- **Mechanism:** for independent $A_i, A_j$ the exchange $a = \mathrm{tr}(A_i^\top A_j)/2$ has **zero mean**, while the $p=2$ single-site anisotropy $h_2$ and the U(1)-breaking $\cos(\theta_i+\theta_j)$ term have **nonzero mean magnitude**. Exact U(1) holds **iff** each $A$ is a conformal embedding **and** $C = A_i^\top A_j$ is complex-linear **and** the spectator field terms vanish. **Training does not break U(1) — the random init does.**
- **Why it is load-bearing, not hygiene:** a $p$-fold anisotropy has scaling dimension $x_p = p^2\eta(T)/2$ at the KT fixed point, so with $\eta(T_{\rm KT}) = 1/4$, **$x_2 = 1/2 < 2$ ⇒ the $p=2$ anisotropy is a RELEVANT perturbation** (JKKN 1977; *evidenced*, quoted not re-derived). It destroys the KT phase and drives the array to Ising universality. **The shipped default would silently destroy any 2-D memory phase.** Additional structural cost: the generic coupling **both gaps the would-be Goldstone** (measured $\mu^2_{\rm global}$ 0.00198–0.00493) **and fails to price communication** (true relative-mode price $\mu^2_{\rm rel} = 4\kappa/M = 0.2$ missed by ~40×, because $|W|$ stays small).
- **Scope:** 2 units, 3 seeds, one data distribution, `so2_invariant + spring` only. Not tested: `mlp` couplings, `N > 2`, emergent units. **The DM phase is pure gauge on a tree but a flux on a cycle** ⇒ a ring/torus lattice with learned projections is a *frustrated* XY model (proven, not simulated).
- **Disposition:** **tier A — V3 / Thread-10 (Nature-MI) appendix.** Justification: it is a genuine **experimental** negative about *learned* couplings (not merely a design guard), and it is the **single biggest threat** to the leading Nature-MI thesis — with a **free fix**. Ships as: *"the shipped parameterisation does not learn an XY exchange; the symmetry must be designed into the coupling, and doing so costs nothing."* **Design rule → `lattice-xy-prereqs`:** add `coupling_type="channel_spring"` (or a conformal constraint on `W`) and make it the default for `so2_invariant` units. Mandatory **broken-symmetry control** for the KT experiment (predict: no `2/π` jump).

### N50 — `two_timescale_orbits.py` cannot identify a coupling (the exp-lattice smoke says nothing about coupling physics)  · tier B · V3
- **Tried:** `xy-lattice-theory` §2.8 asked whether the shipped lattice training smoke could identify $V_c$ or exhibit Goldstone structure.
- **Numbers:** `generate_two_timescale_orbits` draws **independent uniform phases per unit** and gives the units different $\omega$ (**0.5, 2.0**). Consequences: (i) the data carries **no inter-unit phase correlation** ⇒ $V_c$ is **not identified** by it; (ii) circular-orbit data is fit by an isotropic **harmonic** well, so trained `so2_invariant` units place their minimum at the **origin** — measured **`r* < 1e-3`, both units, all 3 seeds** ⇒ **no vacuum ring, no coset, no XY model.**
- **Mechanism:** a data-design fact, **not a bug**. You cannot infer a two-body interaction from data whose two bodies are statistically independent.
- **Scope — read this carefully, and do not over-read it.** It invalidates only *coupling-physics* and *Goldstone-structure* readings of the `exp-lattice` banded-vs-uniform training smoke. It **does NOT touch the banding claims (CM-5 / CM-10)**, which are about **inertial mass $M$**, not coupling, and are measured elsewhere (`v3-band-selection`, `v3-interference-ntk`). Any Goldstone/XY claim *about that smoke* is vacuous; the banding results stand untouched.
- **Disposition:** **tier B** — V3 appendix scope note + a standing caveat on the smoke. Also explains why the XY framing is, for now, a **designed-symmetry** result: emergent units have no exact ring to start from (N46; `xy-lattice-theory` §9.5).

### N51 — (methodological) Raw `n₁/₂` exponents cannot discriminate designed from emergent — the instrument, not the physics  · tier A · V2/V5 (instrument validity)
- **Tried:** `v5-gate` §3.5 measured the `T>0` retention exponents on emergent checkpoints **and ran a matched designed control on the same (γ,T) grid** — a control the task did not ask for.
- **Numbers** (median FPT to `|Δθ| ≥ 0.5`, walkers started at $q^*$, `fdt`, 96 walkers, cap 150k/60k, **0/45 cells censored**):

  | | `d log n₁/₂ / d log T` (γ=0.01 / 0.05 / 0.2) | `d log n₁/₂ / d log γ` (T=2e-3 / 4e-3 / 8e-3) |
  |---|---|---|
  | emergent s42 | −0.910 / −1.104 / −1.333 | +0.770 / +0.608 / +0.602 |
  | emergent s44 | −1.073 / −1.161 / −1.327 | +0.574 / +0.592 / +0.580 |
  | **designed s44 (matched control)** | **−0.534 / −0.599 / −1.044** | **+0.777 / +0.633 / +0.546** |

  The designed control gives **the same shallow slopes as emergent.** Both are far below CM-16's designed **+0.955 ± 0.042** — which was measured at `T ≤ 1e-2`, `γ ∈ {0.05,0.1,0.2}`.
- **Mechanism:** **CM-16(d)'s `ℓ_θ/Δ` boundary-layer bias**, present in *both* families and large on this grid because it reaches `T = 3.2e-2` and `γ = 0.01`, where **`ℓ_θ/Δ` climbs to 2.03**. ($\ell_\theta = \varepsilon\sqrt{T/M}/(\gamma r^*)$ = the thermal persistence length = a coset register's resolution limit.) Correcting by the `t-lever` toy bias `1 + 3.099·ℓ_θ/Δ` and keeping only deep-diffusive cells (`ℓ_θ/Δ < 0.06`, i.e. γ=0.2) recovers the physics: designed **1.045 ± 0.095**, emergent 2.75/3.40 at T=2e-3 → 0.94–1.25 at T ≥ 4e-3.
- **Scope:** any `n₁/₂` observable measured by first-passage to a finite tolerance `Δ`. The bias is an **estimator** property, not a model property.
- **⭐ Disposition: tier A — the methodological finding of wave-13, and it travels with every retention claim in V2/V5.** *"**Any** designed-vs-emergent claim quoted from raw exponents would have been an artifact."* **Standing rule, to be enforced in every draft, table and figure caption: never quote `n₁/₂` without `Δ` and `ℓ_θ/Δ`.** Corollary rules: (i) the **`D̂` (diffusion-coefficient) estimator is the unbiased instrument**, raw FPT is the honest number only when its `ℓ_θ/Δ` is stated (cf. N-note in `v5-gate` §2.7: raw vault 86.97 ± 2.94× vs `D̂` vault 107.77 ± 4.78×, the outside arm sitting at `ℓ_θ/Δ = 0.0791`); (ii) a matched control **in the arm you are *not* testing** is what exposed this — budget one.
- **Epistemic classification:** unlike N43/N44 (drafting defects, tier C), this is a **measured instrument-validity result with its own control**, which *prevented* a false claim rather than catching one after the fact. It belongs beside N17/N18 in the "our instruments were wrong before our inferences were" family — see the wave-13 ledger addendum.

### N52 — R7's causal memory floor is FALSE as written on a curved coset (falsification-with-repair)  · tier A · V1/V3 + F5

- **Tried:** `causal-memory-floor` (F-10/F-11) attacked R7's proposed lifetime floor `n ≥ Δ/(ε·θ̇_max)` with an **adversarial impulse train** on the actual trained ring — the "attacked version" the task named as the experiment.
- **Numbers:** the floor **as written is FALSE — broken in 332/787 adversarial cells, by up to 3.14×.** An adversary that *dives toward the origin* trades radius for angular speed (`θ̇ = v/r`, and `r` is the adversary's to choose), so a bound written in the *angular* rate is not assumption-free. **The repair** (returned by the same report): the assumption-free object is a **Cartesian light-cone bound** `|q_{n+1}−q_n| < ε·c/√M_min` — **never violated (0/787)**, verified to **1 ulp at `|p|=1e18`**, and **exactly attained** (`n = ⌈d_min(Δ)/(ε v_max)⌉`, with `d_min(Δ) = r* sin Δ` for `Δ≤π/2`, `= r*` beyond). Newtonian mode has **no** such bound (per-step displacement `0.034 → 302` over `T ∈ [1e-2,1e6]`; a single step erases the register).
- **Mechanism:** `θ̇_max = c/(√M r*)` is a bound on angular speed *at fixed radius*; a curved coset lets the adversary shrink `r`. Causality bounds **Cartesian** displacement per step, not angular. Two new closed forms derived en route (relativistic diffusion-saturation constant, arcsine law + its dimensional generalization).
- **Scope:** trained relativistic ring, adversarial; the light-cone bound is assumption-free (any noise, any adversary, any temperature — pathwise, no invariant measure needed).
- **Disposition:** **tier A — V1/V3 + F5.** *This is the healthiest outcome the program has produced: a falsification WITH a repair that returns the correct, stronger object.* The task was written to **invite** it (an attack task on the program's own proposed bound). The paper ships the **light-cone bound**, never R7's angular form. Companion self-refutations from the same report: **N53** (R6 refinement) and **N54** (R3 transport law). See the wave-14 ledger addendum, Ch. 3/4.

### N56 — "Raise `c`" is refuted as a native fix for the relativistic-Gibbs defect  · tier A · all (physics-audit ¶) / F5

### N61 — Gradient-based address search across basins is measured dead (4 protocols, 2 independent agents)  · tier A · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** learning the memory *address* by gradient descent through the CLU rollout, from a deliberately-bad (wrong-basin) initialization. **Four qualitatively different protocols, two agents, two independent harnesses:** engineer — plain GD and γ-annealed GD on `(q₀)` through a hand-designed `RingRegisterPotential` (Adam, lr 0.05, 300 steps, K=8, offsets {1,2,4}); theorist — plain GD, Adam, damped-read GD, naive hybrid (GD then dissipative capture) and energy-annealed GD (Toy F) on `(q₀,p₀,log M)` through a 1200-step rollout, K=4, 18 inits.
- **Numbers (verbatim):** engineer **0.042 (1/24)** plain GD and **0.042 (1/24)** γ-annealed; **0.125 (1/8)** at adjacent-site init (offset 1), **0.000** at offset 2, **0.000 antipodal**; median 233 steps when it succeeds (`clu-retrieval-demo §5a`). Theorist — plain GD **2/18 strict** (11%) vs pre-registered ≥50%; **9/18 basin-level** (median loss 7.90 → 2.65); **Adam 1/18**; **damped-read 0/18**; **naive hybrid 3/18 ≈ chance 0.25**; **energy-annealed (Toy F) 0/18** vs an in-script commitment of ≥6/18 (`clu-memory-architecture §3/§5/§9`).
- **Mechanism (identified, consistent across both harnesses):** the failure is localized to **capture** — cross-basin re-localization. Escape and transport *do* work (9/18 basin-level; GD raises `‖p₀‖` and the window-mean migrates toward the target). Strict success is an **energy** criterion: GD must shed energy *while positioned over the target*, i.e. end on a small-measure low-energy manifold reached by crossing a **separatrix layer with fractal basin boundaries** — the one place Prop 4's chaotic set intersects the retrieval pipeline. The engineer's independent form: the loss-vs-θ₀ surface is a **staircase** — 8 local minima at K=8, **cliff ratio 1.7e7**, flat plateaus separated by discontinuities. Adam is *worse* (per-coordinate rescaling amplifies separatrix roughness). Toy F's penalty forces capture into **whichever basin the orbit currently occupies** (8/18 end at wrong-well bottoms, final E ≈ −0.79).
- **⭐ Candidate no-go worth stating as a proposition (transcribed, not adjudicated):** *a dynamically-robust addressable memory has no useful address gradient.* A readable memory requires the retrieved state to be a fixed point — exactly `∂(final state)/∂(q₀) → 0` inside a basin — and **the address gradient IS that derivative**. Making retrieval robust is precisely the act of destroying the signal address-descent needs.
- **Scope:** ⚠ **This is a negative about the ADDRESS SELECTOR ONLY.** Write (payload to 1e-3), read (linear probe 1.000/0.992), durability (flat over 1200 steps) and locality (corruption 4.17e-7) **all work**. Both harnesses are 2-D, hand-designed, K≤8, single-seed-per-arm; the mechanism (separatrix roughness) predicts the negative gets *worse* at higher `d`, which is itself untested. Untested bypasses: derived addresses, write-side restructuring, retry-as-capture, distillation from content-addressable relaxation (see `future_work.md`).
- **Disposition:** **Do not fund further gradient-based cross-basin address search without a new mechanism** (both agents independently). The surviving learnability story is the §5 redirection. Appendix-grade tier A: this is the wave's most important negative and it *redirects* an architecture rather than killing one.

### N62 — The folk BPTT objection is INVERTED: dissipation, not conservation, kills address gradients  · tier A · memory-architecture · (retracts a Hub pre-registration)

- **Tried:** measuring, rather than assuming, the gradient behaviour of a rollout-through-address loss. Theorist: exact tangent maps on a quartic well and Hénon–Heiles (Toy C, Benettin renormalization every 50 steps); damped-read GD arm (Toy D). Engineer: a γ-scan at fixed launch point and fixed loss, plus a rollout-length sweep of `‖∇_address loss‖`.
- **Numbers (verbatim):** **Prop 4 (proven + verified)** — the γ=0 Verlet tangent map is symplectic ⇒ singular values pair `(σ, 1/σ)` ⇒ **‖J_N‖ ≥ 1 always**; regular growth log-log slope **1.0014** (prereg 1.00±0.15), chaotic λ = **0.098** (matrix-norm fit) vs **0.111** (independent vector-Benettin, 12% apart); at t=1000 chaotic ‖J‖ = **10^47.6** vs regular **10^2.8** — **44.8 orders apart**. **Prop 5 (proven + verified)** — the damped arm's loss is **frozen at 7.9035443 to 7 significant digits across 4000 GD steps**, 0/18. Engineer γ-scan: `‖∇_address‖` **3.3e-1 → 5.0e-8** across γ = 0 → 0.05 (**7 orders**) while settling error (read quality) only becomes usable at **γ ≳ 0.01**; rollout-length sweep **7.7e-2 → 2.9e-4** (falls 2.6 orders) over 25 → 800 steps.
- **Mechanism:** for γ>0 the read endpoint is the basin fixed point — locally **constant** in `(q₀,p₀,m)`; residual gradient decays as `((1−γ_r)|λ_int|)^n` (≈e^{−18} at γ_r=0.02, n=900, below any FD/SGD noise floor). Conservative reads are *rough but gradient-transparent*. **The memory-useful structures and the gradient-benign structures are the same set** — basins, coset registers and invariant tori are regular; the pathological regime is chaotic transport *between* them.
- **⚠ What this retracts:** the Hub predicted **exploding/chaotic gradients from non-contraction**; the engineer pre-registered *"gradient norm GROWS with rollout length"* (P5b). **Both are falsified, and the truth is worse:** friction contracts, and contraction is what kills addressability. **Retrieval robustness and address learnability are the same derivative with opposite sign requirements, governed by one knob (γ), with no window where both are good.**
- **Scope:** Prop 4's norm bound is exact (symplecticity of the splitting) and kinetic-agnostic; the growth *laws* are measured on two 2-D systems. Prop 5 verified on one damped arm plus the engineer's independent γ-scan. The relativistic mode-coupling at finite `p` (F5 Prop-2) could shorten regular horizons — **unchecked**.
- **Disposition:** tier A, and **a positive as much as a negative** — it answers the standing "BPTT-through-rollout is hopeless" objection in CLU's favour (conservative reads *never* vanish) while killing the damped-read training story. Design consequence: **learn addresses at γ_r = 0, deploy content-addressable retrieval at γ_r > 0.**

### N63 — `dt=0.05` on cycle-indexed data: a units bug that makes the potential a passenger in its own Hamiltonian  · tier A · CAFE/eval path

- **Tried:** auditing the time-units assumption of the CAFE/C-MAPSS eval path, where the data is **cycle-indexed** (one sample = one engine cycle) but the integrator runs at `dt=0.05`.
- **Numbers (verbatim, `clu-latent-io-audit §Item 4`):** `p₀ = Δq/dt = 20·Δq` ⇒ **K inflated by 1/dt² = 400×**. At init on real FD001, identical batch: mean `H` **2351** (`dt=0.05`) vs **6.588** (`dt=1.0`), ratio 357× ≈ 400×; `predict_mse` **112** vs **5.924**; **`E_reg` = 6.52e4 = 99.2% of total loss** (vs 0.514 = 7.6% at `dt=1.0`); **`E_reg` = 99.8% of the mass gradient** (vs 30.6%); **R-1 spread term vs base gradient 1.6e-6 (invisible)** vs **0.071 (usable)**. On trained models, force/free-streaming `‖Δq_force‖/‖Δq_free‖`: **0.0166** for the training wake rollout (⇒ **98.3% ballistic free-streaming**, `V_θ` contributes 1.7%), **0.0674** for the default encode relax → `q*` (⇒ **93% free-streaming**), 0.9490 for the tuned γ=0.5/64 arm. **`H` ≡ `K`: kinetic share 14.7, corr(H,K) = 0.999996, corr(H,V) = 0.055.**
- **Mechanism:** a pure time rescale keeps the *velocity* scale self-consistent, **but the force and friction do not rescale with it** — force enters `q` at `O(dt²)` while free-streaming enters at `O(dt)`, so **the potential's share of the rollout is `O(dt)`**. The energy-magnitude regularizer then dominates both the loss and the mass gradient, and its only lever is inflating `M` uniformly (→ N64).
- **Scope:** the CAFE/`clu_scorer` eval path at cycle-indexed C-MAPSS. ⚠ **The `dt` fix is UNTESTED end-to-end** — the mechanism is measured thoroughly, but no full FD001 arm was run at `dt=1.0`. **Caution recorded by the source:** at `dt=1.0` the potential is strong enough to collapse `q*` to a single point under damping, so the relax budget must be retuned simultaneously — **do not vary `dt` alone.**
- **Disposition:** ⇒ **all SDR / anti-collapse work (R-1…R-6) is gated on this one-line fix**, not on priority. **Candidate common cause** of physics-scalars-at-chance, the non-predictive rollout, and the pattern that every "improvement" works by *suppressing* dynamics. ⚠ **CM-3 discipline, new instance: every prior CLU-on-CAFE number was produced with `H`≈`K` and a 98.3%-ballistic rollout — all FD00x numbers are PROVISIONAL pending the fix and a re-run.**
- > **✅ Update (wave-20, `dt-units-split`): the fix is DELIVERED and end-to-end, and it is FD001-NEUTRAL.** `data_dt` split from the integrator `dt`, integrator retuned to **`dt=0.125`**, all 6 w19 rows re-measured, 6/6 preregs held. FD001 h-AUROC: **0.6540→0.6569, 0.7092→0.7102, 0.7158→0.7125** — all within seed noise (≈0.002) ⇒ *the physics is corrected at zero metric cost; the raw-stats 0.7486 gap is unchanged.* ⚠ The apparent **−0.08 "regression" was a pure unstable-integrator artifact at `dt=1.0`** and must not be recorded as a finding (the task's own do-not-vary-`dt`-alone warning was right and nearly cost the conclusion). **Two w19 conclusions REVERSE:** `H≡K` → **`H≈V`** (corr(H,V) 0.075→**0.945**) and "training compresses the mass spectrum" → **expands it** (1.164→**1.349** vs init 1.265). ⛔ **Do not re-quote "98.3% ballistic"** — the legacy repro gives **79.7%**, unreconciled (see § Open reconciliations, R20-1). ⚠ New standing hazard recorded as **N72**: `dt·ω` has no comfortable margin (the model self-organizes to the stability edge).
- > **✅ Update (wave-23, `r19-r20-reconciliations` → R20-1 RESOLVED): the "98.3% ballistic" figure in this entry is SUPERSEDED and RETIRED.** It was a **40-epoch / 2000-window under-trained fit** (independently reproduced as the ~95–98% under-trained regime: 94.75% global / 96.33% per-sample at 40 ep/2000 w). **The quotable numbers are: ≈77–80% ballistic at legacy `dt=0.05` (canonical 150-epoch fit: 76.97%; dt-units' 79.7% confirmed) and ≈50% at the shipped `dt=0.125` default (50.49%).** Carrier of the discrepancy = **training maturity, not `dt`** (both originals were legacy `dt`): epochs −10 pp · window count −7.5 pp · aggregation convention ±9 pp · preprocessing ~2 pp. **The entry's *qualitative* conclusion is unchanged — at legacy `dt` the rollout was free-streaming-dominated and the potential was a passenger** — only the digit changes, and the shipped-`dt` model is now only ~half ballistic. ⚠ Generalized as **N94** (standing caveat: `<40`-epoch CAFE diagnostics are not properties of the shipped model). Approved sentence: *"free-streaming-dominated — ≈50% at the shipped `dt`, ≈80% at legacy `dt`; the 98.3% was an under-trained-model artifact."*

### N64 — The mass spectrum is inert by COMMON-MODE RUNAWAY, not frozen parameters; and the EBM objective is structurally blind to mass  · tier A · V3 / CAFE path · **(amends N7 — see the N7 Update block)**

- **Tried:** measuring, on the real eval/CAFE code path, whether `log_mass` actually moves; the per-loss-term gradient partition (theorist OQ1); and what 150 epochs of training does to the mass *spectrum*.
- **Numbers (verbatim, `clu-latent-io-audit §Item 1`):** per-parameter RMS gradient at init on real FD001, batch 64 — `predict_mse` gives `|g|` **1.336e+01** on `log_mass` (n=14) vs **5.697e-04** on `V_θ` (n=5185); **`E_contrast` gives EXACTLY 0.000e+00 on `log_mass`**; `E_reg` gives **7.739e+03** vs 9.435e-01; **TOTAL 7.752e+03 vs 9.440e-01 ⇒ `log_mass` receives a gradient 8,200× larger per-parameter than `V_θ`.** After 150 epochs (seed 42, default arm): common drift **+3.5634**, differential **0.0906**, **c/d = 39.3**, movement rms_ratio **4.28**, **`M_max/M_min` = 1.153** — *below its random init of* **1.265**. At `mass_lr_mult=10`: Std(log M) 0.0877 → 0.5609, common +8.2454, **ratio only 1.283**. FD001 h-AUROC: default **0.6540**, mass10 **0.7092** (+0.055), tuned **0.7158**, tuned+mass10 **0.7137** — **non-additive, both plateau ≈0.714, still below the 56-d raw-statistics baseline 0.7486**.
- **Mechanism — three, all fixable:** (i) **99.8% of the mass gradient comes from `E_reg`**, whose only lever on `H` is inflating `M` *uniformly* — pure common-mode pressure; (ii) ⭐ **the EBM contrastive term has EXACTLY ZERO mass gradient** — negatives are made by perturbing `q` only, so kinetic terms cancel identically in `H(data) − H(neg)`: **the objective's representational half is structurally blind to the mass**; (iii) **softplus trap** — `M = softplus(log_mass)` is linear for `x ≫ 0`, so once `E_reg` drives `log_mass` to ≈3.5 (≈8.2 at mult=10) a *log*-scale spread stops buying *exponential* dynamic range. Both measured levers (`mass_lr_mult`, relax budget) work by **suppressing ballistic free-streaming**, not by "more physics" — force share *falls* 0.170 → 0.101 under mass10.
- **⚠ What this overturns, and what it confirms:** **N7's "masses stay at init" is WRONG on this code path** (`log_mass` moves +3.56) and **the theorist's D1 premise is INVERTED here** (the mass gets the *rich* gradient, not the starved one). The Hub's "`mass_lr_mult` unreferenced ⇒ mass inert" inference is **half right** — the knob was genuinely absent (now ported, `98be102`) but its absence is not why there is no hierarchy. **The Head's conclusion — no timescale hierarchy — is CONFIRMED. Both proposed mechanisms were wrong.**
- **⚠ Correction that propagates:** the D1 lr-partition constant is **K-dependent — `η_m/(η_m + K·η_k)`** (K=2 → **1/21**, matched to **13 digits**, `clu-memory-architecture §2 Prop 6`). **The old `1/11` is wrong for multi-item settings**; anyone reusing `anti-collapse-characterization` §5.1 must use the K-form. Prop 6 also shows the escape: with **per-item masses**, only the overall *scale* stays gauge and **all ratios become wake-visible and exactly learnable** (verified to **2.2e-14**) ⇒ **masses must be PER-ADDRESS codebook entries, not a global model parameter. As shipped, `m` is not an address component at all.**
- **Scope:** single seed (42) on the 4 new CAFE arms; prior 3-seed spread on this path ≈0.0017, so +0.055 is ~30× noise and safe, but the **−0.0021** for tuned+mass10 is *within* noise and must not be read as a regression. `newtonian_learned` kinetic mode; the Exp-A default `newtonian_identity` ignores `log_mass` entirely. Entangled with **N63** — 99.8% of the mass gradient is an `E_reg` artifact of the `dt` bug, so this negative may partly dissolve at `dt=1.0` (**untested**).
- **Disposition:** tier A. Fix the common mode (normalize `log_mass` to zero mean) or reparameterize before any mass-hierarchy mechanism is attempted; otherwise it is fighting the `E_reg` runaway.
- > **✅ Update (wave-20, `mass-visible-objective`): the blindness is FIXED AT SOURCE — and it ships OFF.** The defect **reproduces exactly post-`dt`-fix and is structural, not a units artifact**: `∂E_contrast/∂log_mass` is **bit-zero** (`np.all(g==0.0)` True; analytic — negatives are `(q+δq, p)`, kinetic terms cancel identically). **Mass-perturbed negatives** (`neg_momentum_scale`, default **0.0** — no shipped default changed) take `E_contrast`'s mass-gradient share **0.00% → 42.70%**; combined arm reaches **`M_max/M_min` = 4.1051** vs baseline 1.3489 (init 1.2656). **The spectrum is FUNCTIONAL: τ ∝ M^0.779 (R²=0.9968)** on a bit-identical fixed landscape via the new per-launch `mass_override`; mass-attributable timescale spread **1.27× → 3.05×**. ⚠ **Corrections that travel:** `τ ∝ √M` is RETIRED — the registered P4 exponent +0.5 FAILED as registered (wrong damping limit); quote **τ ∝ M^0.79**. The **softplus trap is DOWNGRADED to a largely dead issue post-`dt`-fix** (exp reparameterization buys only **1.089×**). ⛔ **NO TASK METRIC WAS MEASURED** — do not let "the mass spectrum is fixed" propagate as "CLU improved". ⚠ And w21 sharpens the scope (**N76/Prop F1**): mass is **address-side — it SELECTS, it cannot STORE** — and contributes zero observable dimensions for any separable `V`; a functional spectrum is a *selection* mechanism, never a storage channel.

### N65 — (positioning) Four novelty/framing claims do not survive the literature — three by external prior art  · tier B · all papers

- **Tried:** an adversarial prior-art read of CLU-as-addressable-dynamical-memory against S4/Mamba/HiPPO, NTM/DNC, modern Hopfield and Hamiltonian sequence models, with four independent novelty verdicts (`scout-dynamical-memory-priorart`).
- **The four refutations (numbers/citations verbatim):**
  1. **⛔ "Continuity is our NTM/DNC escape hatch" is FALSE.** The canonical NTM **and** DNC were **already fully soft, continuous and end-to-end differentiable** — NTM's own abstract: *"differentiable end-to-end, allowing it to be efficiently trained with gradient descent"*, with *"'blurry' read and write operations"* defining *"a continuous distribution over the memory locations."* RL-NTM (hard addressing) is a **separate, later** line. ⇒ **the precedent transfers as a WARNING, not an escape**, and **2 of 3** diagnosed DNC failure modes (Csordás & Schmidhuber, ICLR 2019, whose fixes improved bAbI mean error by **43%**) bite CLU directly: **key/value entanglement — the one they rank "most importantly" — is ARCHITECTURAL in CLU, since `q₀` is simultaneously the key and the initial condition of the value**; and de-allocation aliasing maps onto the `γ_φ` trash region. Chained-read degradation (exponential in chain length) maps onto wormholes + multi-particle consolidation.
  2. **⛔ "Retrieval is a rollout, not a weighted sum" is NOT ours to claim.** **Kong, Brewer & Lai, *Nature Communications* 15 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41467-024-49190-4** — location-addressable retrieval of dynamical attractors via an **index channel**; capacity `N_c ∝ K^γ` with **γ = 1.08 ± 0.01** (one-hot/binary), **1.17 ± 0.02** (2-D coding). Not fatal (not symplectic, not Hamiltonian, not mass-structured, address injected as bias rather than initial condition) but **must be cited**.
  3. **⛔ "A retention guarantee attention has no analogue for" is wrong.** **HiPPO-LegS** has approximation error `O(tL/√N)` (Prop. 6), **gradient `Θ(1/t)` — polynomial, not exponential** (Prop. 5), and **Prop. 3 is exactly timescale-equivariant with NO discretization step-size `Δt` at all**. ⚠ **Unanswered challenge, recorded as owed:** *a reviewer will ask why a learned mass spectrum beats provable timescale invariance — we have no answer.*
  4. **⛔ "Competitor to the transformer" is currently INDEFENSIBLE.** Long Range Arena enforces parameter-matched comparison (*"within at best 10% larger… compared to the base Transformer"*); Jelassi et al. (ICML 2024) prove **a fixed-size latent state is fatal on copying/retrieval — and symplectic conservation prevents *decay*, not *capacity***. Against modern Hopfield's **exponential-in-dimension** capacity, ours is **1–1.6 bits/register** with no win over a trivial baseline. ⚠ **Even Mamba-3 (ICLR 2026) only claims to *"advance the performance-efficiency Pareto frontier."***
- **Also narrowed (not refuted):** **tunable-permanence writes** are largely occupied by Karuvally et al.'s energy-memory line — **EDEN (NeurIPS 2025)** *"analytically compute[s] memory escape times, revealing a phase transition between static and dynamic regimes"*, capacity `O(γ^N)`. **What survives as ours:** permanence as a **per-item design parameter chosen at write time**, three qualitatively distinct modes, one **symmetry-protected** (`μ²≡0` exactly) — *"the broad claim 'we can tune memory permanence' is taken."*
- **What SURVIVES contact (record both halves):** energy-landscape retrieval as a principled competitor-class mechanism to attention (**Ramsauer et al.: the modern Hopfield update *is* the attention mechanism** — cite prominently); retention specified per item at write time; **symplectic structure-preserving test-time retry (novelty c) — no prior art found, genuinely unoccupied** (but "a mechanism in search of a demonstrated benefit"); the reframing that **CLU is a latent information carrier, not a model of the observed dynamics** (consistent with how HiPPO/SSMs are understood); and *"a symplectic + mass-structured **addressable** memory has not been built"* — **moderate-to-low confidence, four targeted searches, needs a citation-graph sweep before print**.
- **Scope / ⚠ retrieval gaps stated not reconstructed:** **Ramsauer's exact capacity constant was NOT obtained from primary source** (the `N ≥ √p·c^((d−1)/4)` exponent form is **SINGLE-SOURCED, secondary — do not put in a paper**); **UnICORNN's Hamiltonian claim unverified**; PonderNet's arXiv ID/authors are from training knowledge, unverified. ⚠ **SRNN (Chen et al., ICLR 2020) "initial state optimization" is the single most likely place a reviewer finds us preempted on learned-`(q₀,p₀)` and the passage could NOT be extracted** — must be read before any such novelty claim.
- **Disposition:** tier B (positioning/framing, no experiment overturned) but **binding on every draft**. **Defensible framing to adopt:** *a physics-structured associative memory in which retention is a designed, per-item property — permanent (symmetry-protected), finite half-life (`μ²`-set), or actively deletable — rather than an emergent consequence of a learned recurrence*, evaluated on **associative-recall diagnostics**. This claims **controllability** (evidenced) instead of **capability** (not). ⚠ **Frame CLU's contribution as retention control and temporal structure, explicitly NOT capacity, and say so before a reviewer asks** — the scout flags capacity as *"the program's most exposed flank."*

### N67 — Learning destroys what design provides: no learned rung preserves the loop, and write locality does not survive  · tier A (proposed) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the w19 write→address→read loop on a **learned** landscape (`DesignFreedomPotential`, 5 rungs designed→`free_mlp`, static write objective, two-phase read), 5-seed check on the minimum-viable-design point (`learned-landscape-write-read`).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** **no learned rung clears strict 0.9 at both K=4 and K=8** (5 seeds); minimum viable design = **at least rung 1** (the FULL designed landscape + a small learned residual), *"and even that is marginal"* — the single-seed answer (rung 2) was **overturned by the agent's own 5-seed replication**. Write locality: designed **0.000** → learned **2.9e-2 … 5.0e-1**; the rung that best passed items 1–2 is **destroyed by ONE subsequent write (strict 1.000 → 0.000)** (§0.2–0.3). w19's 4.17e-7 is **confirmed designed-only** and must always be quoted that way.
- **Mechanism:** an MLP write has global support — every write perturbs every stored item; additive separability is a property of the design, not of learning.
- **Scope / w21 amendments (do not quote the w20 ladder unqualified):** `potential-function-class` recon 1 — with a better learned family, **rung 1 goes 0.903±0.101/0.959±0.043 (failing) → 1.000±0.000/0.986±0.005 (passing, 20× less seed variance)**: the *point* barely moves, the *curve* moves a lot — w20's ladder is what an **MLP** learned landscape can do. Recon 2 — **w20's `local_rbf` failure (0.623/0.348) is an INITIALISATION artifact** (fixed parameterisation + flat start → 0.980/0.741): do not cite w20 rung 3 as evidence about locality. And no learned *class* clears 0.9 at K=8 either (7 classes, 5 seeds — the class is not the problem; the write operator is, N74).
- **Disposition:** the founding negative of the "design keeps beating learning" arc (w20–w22). What survives learning: write→relax consistency (basin ≥0.98, rungs 0–2, K≤8) and value recovery. What does not: locality, the full loop at freedom >1.
