- **Why it failed (mechanism):** kNN-in-φ is *already* a perfect static content-addressable read of the same features — the store's settling dynamics can at best reproduce it, and at high load its basins begin to overlap (`s = 0.3·median-NN` puts the store **exactly at the packing bound**, `spacing/Δ_req ≡ 1.08` by construction, **no slack**), so CLU decays first. **The designed store's differentiating capabilities (per-item retention, deletion/decay, admission, retry, sequential-write locality) are exactly the axes a static masked-recall capacity/noise sweep cannot score.**
- **⭐ The positives that MUST travel with it (approved wording, `phi-read-in` recon 2 / handover 2):** the **phase-doctrine PREMISE is validated** — `φ` fixes the "CLU on raw data" losses *for everyone*: raw-space CLU is at **chance (0.012–0.062)** on CIFAR and **CLU-in-φ is 0.81–0.97**; closed-form Hopfield-in-φ also recovers from raw chance (P-φ); and **CLU-in-φ ≫ closed-form Hopfield-in-φ at load and under noise (CIFAR M=256: 0.973 vs 0.008 AE-softmax; MNIST σ=0.4: 0.852 vs 0.250)**. ⚠ On MNIST-at-high-M Hopfield is slightly *ahead* (0.957 vs 0.871 PCA) — the CLU>Hopfield margin is a **CIFAR / hard-feature-geometry** effect, not universal (the agent's own prereg "CLU>Hopfield everywhere" was too broad). ⚠ AE-softmax Hopfield **re-collapses** at high M (0.008): φ fixes Hopfield for *localized* reads (CLU, sparsemax), not universally for softmax. **And: the retry hook SURVIVES φ** (confidence = distance-to-nearest-well; AUROC **0.845–0.988** across all four cells, pre-registered ≥0.65; incorrect reads settle 1.6–8.7× farther) ⇒ the feature-space extension of the retry thread is **GREEN**.
- **Scope:** static masked/noisy recall, single seed (0), one φ family per arm, `phi_dim = 32`, one fixed well-width rule. The verdict is unambiguous **on this benchmark** (max CLU margin 0.000 everywhere) and says nothing about capability axes.
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **new forbidden claim — "a designed CLU store beats a trivial feature baseline on associative recall" (CM-22 class).** The "it only loses because there's no embedding" defence is **closed**: the embedding now exists, in two independent forms, and the store still does not win. **Approved framing:** *"a learned read-in makes the CLU register competitive with closed-form modern-Hopfield in feature space and far above its own raw-pixel line, but a trivial kNN in the same feature space is the ceiling on static masked recall."* Every future φ-space claim carries **kNN-in-φ as a mandatory laundering control** (the C17-3 lesson, now twice-instantiated).
- > **✅ UPHELD + EXTENDED (wave-24) — TWICE.** **(a) Under stream discipline** (`phi-stream-discipline`, Split-MNIST 5×2, M=160, 3 seeds): laundering fires in **all 4 headline cells AND all 16 stress cells** (4 `phi_dim` × 2 arms × 2 regimes), kNN-in-φ ties-or-beats CLU-in-φ everywhere, max CLU margin ≤ 0. The pre-registered watch-item — *does strictness (task-1-only φ) reveal a store advantage?* — **does NOT fire** (delta = margin(strict) − margin(generic) = −0.004…+0.019, laundering fires in the strict regime too). *The win is φ's, not ours — now also under stream discipline.* **(b) Multi-seed** (`multi-seed-w23`, MNIST 5 seeds / CIFAR 4 seeds): laundered in **4/4 cells at every seed, 0 CLU wins in 22 cell-seed pairs**; pooled mean ≤ 0.01 in all four cells. **N89 is not a seed artifact.** ⚠ New binding protocol parameter from (a): **`phi_dim ≥ 16` for any strict-φ claim** (the ≈0 cost of leakage-free task-1-only φ is *capacity slack*, not absence of cost — gap +0.117/+0.190 at `phi_dim=4` → ≈0 at 32; the strict basis captures 10–18 pp less later-task variance at every dim). Tier A unchanged.

### N90 — ⛔ The feedforward-NN floor dominates CLU-gated retry in every cell: CM-23's retry claim splits into a surviving SHAPE claim and a falsified DOMINANCE claim  · tier A (HUB-CONFIRMED) · memory-architecture / all papers

- **Tried:** promoting w22's single retry point into a defensible **accuracy-vs-compute curve** on the anchored U-Hop retrieval protocol — retry ladder k∈{0,1,2,4,8}, confidence-gated (τ swept), with five pre-registered controls (ungated-all · ensemble-of-k · equal-energy random-kick · **matched-compute feedforward-NN** · Hopfield-k-steps), 8 cells = 2 loads (M=128/256) × 2 protocols (mask p∈{0.5,0.7}; noise σ∈{0.2,0.3}), MNIST, seed 0 (`retry-compute-study`).
- **Numbers (verbatim, `retry-compute-study` §2 — "NN gap" = gated minus feedforward, best-over-ladder):** MASK **−5.5 / −13.3 / −3.5 / −17.6 pp**; NOISE **−7.8 / −26.6 / −11.3 / −42.2 pp** ⇒ **negative in all 8 cells.** The feedforward-NN line sits at **0.996 (k0) → 0.926 (k8)** — **flat at ceiling 0.99–1.00**, and TTA even nudges it *down*. Flagship cell (MASK M=256 p=0.5): clu_gated **0.359@1.0× → 0.961@1.64×** vs feedforward **0.996@1.0×**.
- **Why it failed (mechanism):** identical to N81 — on masked-pixel retrieval the **surviving pixels uniquely identify the pattern**, so a nearest-neighbour read over the store is already at ceiling; there is no headroom for any method to win. The NN floor is a property of *this protocol*, not of retrieval in general.
- **⭐ The positive that MUST travel with it (approved wording, the wave's ⭐ survivor):** **the mechanism attribution SURVIVES ALL CONTROLS.** Equal-energy **random-kick** and **ensemble-of-k independent restarts** are **DEAD FLAT in all 8 cells** (e.g. flagship: kick 0.359→0.348, ensemble 0.359 at every k) while **CLU-gated rises +6.6 … +76.2 pp and AUTO-STOPS at ×1.2–1.8 compute** ⇒ *the lift is the **directed** symplectic re-launch, not stochastic restart and not "just k tries."* **The confidence gate is load-bearing:** ungated retry-all **collapses 0.96 → 0.004** at 9× compute, and the τ-sweep shows over-retry costs accuracy *and* compute (τ=1.00: 0.828@1.81× vs τ=0.99: **0.961@1.64×**). Hopfield-k-steps *declines* with iteration. ⇒ **the honest claim is a mechanism/capability claim, not a leaderboard claim.**
- **Scope:** MNIST only, seed 0, designed/closed-form on all six lines (N46-admissible, nothing learned). Baselines are placed at their *budget* multiplier (k+1) — **generous to the baselines** (one NN/Hopfield read ≪ one CLU settle); a wall-clock axis would favour them further. Protocol-dependence is itself a finding: the boost recovers **mask** queries strongly (+36…+76 pp) and **Gaussian-noise** queries weakly (+6.6…+34.8 pp), and at σ≥0.4 every arm is at chance (the query has left every basin).
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **CM-23(b) MUST BE SPLIT.** Surviving: *"CLU draws a rising, auto-stopping accuracy-vs-compute curve that a saturated feedforward memory structurally cannot draw"* (**shape**). **RETRACTED:** any text asserting CLU "beats feedforward via test-time compute" (**absolute dominance**) — correct wording is *"…while remaining below the saturated NN floor."* Design note recorded so nobody re-derives it: **cosine-to-nearest-well is a good *ranking* signal but a useless *acceptance* signal post-settle** (correct 0.998 vs wrong 0.949) ⇒ gate + lock-on-retry, never a per-item accept rule. The created-benchmark spec (**RUD-C**, `retry-compute-study` §6, anchored to U-Hop `@cdac754`) makes the four controls **mandatory for a valid submission** — it is appendix-ready.
- > **✅ MULTI-SEED-CLEAN + ⚠ NN-GAP RANGE SUPERSEDED A THIRD TIME (wave-24, `multi-seed-w23`).** The mechanism half is decisive at 5 seeds: `best_acc(control) − first_pass ≤ +3 pp` is violated in **0 of 40** (seed, cell) pairs for **random_kick** (max lift +1.56 pp) and **0 of 40** for **ensemble** (max +0.39 pp). Gated lift restated **+0 … +79.7 pp** (was seed-0 "+6.6…+76.2"); saturation **mean ×1.53, range ×1.0–1.8** (the ×1.0 floor is the ceiling cell where the gate correctly declines). ⚠ **The NN gap moves a THIRD time and BOTH prior ranges are too narrow at both ends:** measured at 5 seeds, **mask −3.9 … −20.7 pp; noise −9.7 … −48.2 pp** (per-cell means, negative in **40/40** pairs). ⛔ **Do not quote either prior wording** — neither the direction doc's "3–13 pp", nor the seed-0 "−3.5…−42.2 pp" / the Hub-corrected "3.5–17.6 pp mask, 42 pp noise" (both seed-0). ### N91 — ⛔ The controller's retention-per-OFFERED loses to every primitive on a fixed address space (0.081 vs gru 0.57 at K=64)  · tier A (HUB-CONFIRMED) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the hand-coded **MVC-0 controller** (admission spacing-gate + refuse-and-relocate · derived placement · staleness/depth eviction · leaky-well decay; **no learning anywhere**) on a designed `AtomStorePotential` (α=0.02, s=0.35, dim=3), run as the **N75 rematch**: retention-vs-K (K=1…64), controller ON/OFF, **per-admitted AND per-offered**, 5 seeds paired, against the four w21 primitives (`controller-mvp`).
- **Numbers (verbatim, `controller-mvp` §2, K=64):** **ON fixed geometry, per-offered 0.081** (admitted **5.2 ± 0.4** of 64; intervention rate 0.97) vs **gru 0.57 · mlp 0.43 · attention 0.34 · learned-CLU 0.16** ⇒ **last of seven.** Controller OFF collapses `1.000 → 0.110 (K=16, EXACTLY w21's designed_ungated) → 0.009 (K=32) → 0.000 (K=64)`.
- **Why it "failed" (mechanism — it is an abstention price, not a malfunction):** on a fixed radius-2 disk the **packing bound is N_pack = 6.12**; the gate certifies isolation (live-site min-spacing **1.61 ≥ d_safe 1.54**) and therefore *refuses* everything beyond ~6 items. Per-offered is capped at `N_pack/K`. Densifying past the bound is what the OFF arm's 0.000 looks like.
- **⭐ The positives that MUST travel with it (both halves are mandatory — a single-number rematch claim is FALSE):** **per-ADMITTED is 1.000, flat at every K to 64 — best of five**; and with **sized geometry** (`R = 0.808·√K`, so the packing bound ≥ K) **per-offered 0.669 at K=64 BEATS all four primitives** (gru 0.57). ⇒ **the binding constraint is the ADDRESS SPACE, not the controller.** Also demonstrated: **permanent + leaky wells coexist in one store** (permanent retention 1.000 through 8 decay ticks; leaky amplitude exactly `exp(−0.35·t)`, half-life 1.98, `decayed_out = 6/6` self-evicted), staleness eviction removes the LRU non-permanent item, and a full all-permanent store raises a **capacity alarm rather than silently overwriting**. ⭐ The gate **demonstrably fires** on this geometry (intervention 0.20 → 0.97 over K) — contrast **N74**, where on the w20 ring the same gate was arithmetically vacuous.
- **Scope:** designed store only (the spacing certificate is **meaningless for a global-support learned write**, N75); single geometry family, Newtonian, `p₀=0`, scalar payload; `on_evict` was never stressed on the rematch curve (budget 6 ≥ admitted 5.2) — the eviction verb is proven in the decay demo and unit tests only; primitive lines are **reused** from w21 (same harness/protocol/seeds), not re-run.
- > **⚠ CORRECTION (wave-25, `mia-decay-measurement` §6 / defect D2) — the decay-demo retention row quoted from `controller-mvp` §3(b) is a BEST CASE, not the store's retention.** The positives block above (and `controller-mvp` §3(b)) states *"permanent retention 1.000 through 8 decay ticks; leaky amplitude exactly `exp(−0.35·t)`"*. The **permanent row is unaffected and stands (1.000 ∀t)**, and the amplitude law stands (verified independently to the digit: `0.7047` at t=1, self-eviction at tick 9). ⛔ **But the implied "a leaky item answers perfectly right up to the floor" is FALSE, for two measured reasons in the demo's own instrument:** `item_decay_demo.retention_of` passes a **1-element `sites` array** to `evaluate_items`, so `basin_of`'s `argmin` is always 0 and **the basin criterion is vacuous** (only the value criterion is tested); and its `leaky_id = 1` happens to carry payload **+0.1429**, the codebook value **most robust to decay**. Re-measured with the **full live-site basin test and all 8 codebook values at the same amplitude (A = 0.0608)**: retention is **0.886 ± 0.19** (8-value mean) and **0.500 ± 0.11 for the item whose payload is +1.0** — while that same item-1 scores **0.999**, agreeing with the original. ⇒ **correct every quoting site to "a permanent item retains 1.000 while leaky wells decay and self-evict; a decayed leaky item's retention is payload-dependent (0.886 mean, 0.500 at `a = +1`) — it does NOT answer perfectly up to the floor."** Root cause of the payload dependence is registered as **N108**'s exploratory finding / §7-CURRENT defect **D3** (`r = −0.846` with `a_i²`; theorist ruling owed before the potential changes). Engineer fix (D2): score against the store's full live-site set and average over several `leaky_id`s. **No other N91 number moves.**
- **Disposition:** **both metrics always travel together.** Quoting per-admitted alone claims "CLU+controller is a perfect memory" — true only of the 8% it agreed to hold. Binding on any continual-learning entry: a CL benchmark on a bounded CLU store must either **(a) size the address space to the task's item count** (packing bound ≥ K) or **(b) accept abstention and be scored per-admitted with the admitted fraction reported.** Betting on per-offered without (a) reproduces the GRU loss.

### N92 — ⛔ (scope guard + superseding law) The raw-sweep base √2 is not the capacity exponent — the law is `min(2^d, K_ceiling≈32)`, and the ceiling belongs to the WRITE OPERATOR  · tier A (HUB-RE-TIERED from B, w23) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the owed dimension-aware re-run of the w22 primitive-decider — `K_learned(d)` for a designed atom-dictionary mechanism with **learned content**, under a budget that scales with the address **dimension** (`n_atoms ≥ max(32K, 384, 512·(√2)^d)`; floors d={2,3,4,5,6,8} = {1024,1448,2048,2896,4096,8192}), 3 seeds, plus **per-point budget-adequacy re-checks at 2× atoms** and a **d=4 capacity-vs-budget saturation curve over a 16× atom range** (`dimension-aware-budget`).
- **Numbers (verbatim, `dimension-aware-budget` §1/§3):** raw 6-point sweep fits base **1.44 [1.31, 1.72], R² 0.889** (poly `d^1.62`, R² 0.917) — **and that fit is an artifact of averaging two regimes.** The budget-adequate curve is **{4, 8, 16, 32, 32, 32}** at d = {2,3,4,5,6,8} = **`min(2^d, ~32)`**. Adequacy evidence: d=4 first-fail K=16 passes at 2× atoms (0.876 → **0.977**) and the K=16 row is **flat 0.929–0.977 across 2048→32768 atoms** while K=32 is **flat ~0.83, a firm wall**; d=5 K=32 clears at 2× (0.886 → 0.906); **d=6 K=64 fails HARDER with more atoms (0.855 → 0.809 at 2×, 36.9k → 73.7k params)** and d=8 K=64 is flat (0.883 → 0.894).
- **Why the single exponent is wrong (mechanism):** there are two regimes. For **d ≤ 5** capacity **doubles per dimension — exactly the designed `4·2^d` rate** ("the wall is geometry" **VINDICATED** there). For **d ≥ 5** a **d-INDEPENDENT ceiling at K≈32** binds: **K=64 is unwritable at d=6 AND d=8 despite 4× different geometric room** (site sep 0.795 vs 0.908), it is **not geometry** (designed reaches ≥256, censored) and **not parameter count** (more atoms make it *worse*) ⇒ the binding constraint is the **static GLOBAL WRITE's ability to dig many disjoint wells jointly** — w22's hypothesis (c), now isolated.
- **⭐ Positives that travel with it:** the **w22 d=8 stall is a CONFIRMED budget artifact — RESOLVED 8 → 32, monotonicity restored**, and **H-LEARNING-at-8 is REJECTED** (the wall rises 4 → 32). The **designed/learned tax stops widening** (w22 ¼ → ⅛ → ≤1/16 monotone; here it plateaus/narrows to ~1/8 for d≥5). Items 2–4 reconfirm w22: **mass null** (coupling 0.145 ± 0.085; per-item mass Δstrict **+0.008 ± 0.011**, `mass_helps False` — Prop F1's 4th confirmation) and **masked-write locality amplifies (8474× at d=2, 3434× at d=4)**; best learned cell = **32 items at d=6 AND d=8**.
- **Scope:** one geometry (d-ball, farthest-point sites, R=1), one write-hyperparameter configuration, scalar payload, designed line censored at k_cap 256. ⚠ **The budget-adequate d=4 = 16 and d=5 ≥ 32 rest on 2-seed re-checks** (the 3-seed strict sweep gave 8/16 — the write is **seed-fragile exactly at the 0.9 rung**); d=2,3,6,8 walls are 3-seed. A declared PREREG deviation: `c` was set to **√2** (not the registered 2.0) after a timing probe measured near-site atom thinning ≈√2/dim — K-predictions unaffected, adequacy verified per point.
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **never quote 1.44 (or `d^1.62`) as the learned capacity exponent**; quote the two-regime law. This **supersedes N82's "exponent unpinned / base 1.2–1.7"** and N82's d=8-as-optimizer-failure reading (confirmed, and now cured). ⭐ Learned capacity is capped by the write side — **but the mechanism ATTRIBUTION is now CONTESTED (see the wave-24 update).**
- > **✅ WAVE-24 — the untested lever is CLOSED, the walls get more seeds, and the "write operator" attribution is put UNDER CONTEST.** **(a) The lever question is answered (`write-ceiling-break` → N96):** a masked/sequential/curriculum write does **NOT** break `K_ceiling≈32` — it **lowers** capacity below 32 (the sequential/masked family collapses to 0.01–0.36; masking starves each item to `atoms/K`; free sequential lets later items overwrite earlier). The scale-invariance ablation moves d=6 K=64 by **\|Δ\|=0.010** ⇒ the ceiling is **not** quantization/normalization/signal dilution. The law `min(2^d, ~32)` is now **robust to the write operator**, not merely un-improved by it. **(b) The 2-seed walls get a third seed (`multi-seed-w23` follow-up, Hub-directed):** **d=4 = 16 SURVIVES at 3 seeds (0.928)**; **d=5 = 32 SOFTENS — 0.898 mean, straddling the 0.90 bar** ⇒ quote the low-`d` regime as **"≥16, consistent with 32", NOT a clean 32.** **(c) ⚠⚠ MECHANISM CONTESTED (Hub ruling, w24 — the wave's key registry-discipline call, DO NOT SETTLE):** the phrase *"the ceiling belongs to the WRITE OPERATOR"* must now carry a qualifier — **"(mechanism CONTESTED: a geometric width-lock account is under test; decisive check is the free §5.0 trained-`log_width` dump)."** `write-ceiling-break` concludes "optimization interference / representational limit of the static write" and that scale-invariance "closes the numerics hypothesis"; `lattice-capacity-theory` §4.2 offers a competing geometric account (critical separation `sep_crit ≈ 2.4–3.0 × well width` at **every** designed AND learned wall d=2…8; predicts the d-independence via `minsep ∝ K^{-1/d}` flattening; reproduces the tax as `2^{-d}` from `well_width 0.15` vs `atom_init_width 0.30`). Crucially write-ceiling's scale-invariance arm rescaled **depths/margins/barrier, NOT width+radius**, so it does **not** test §4.2. **What IS settled:** scale-dilution ruled out by measurement (\|Δ\|=0.010). **What is NOT settled:** whether the ceiling is the write operator (write-ceiling) or a fixed-width geometric lock (lattice). Both are recorded as live; the §5.0/§5.2 experiments are the adjudicator. **Do not re-word N92's mechanism as settled either way** (this is why N96 is worded around the *measured levers that fail*, not around a mechanism).
- > **✅⭐ WAVE-25 — THE CONTEST IS SETTLED, AND NEITHER CONTESTANT WON: the ceiling is a READ-OUT REACH condition (`r2-geometry-revival` → N100).** The w24 adjudicator ran in both stages and both stages behaved as pre-registered. **(a) The `sep/width` account survives as a CORRELATE and is REFUTED AS A CAUSE.** On *trained* widths it classifies all seven d ≥ 4 cells perfectly (boundary **2.30 | 2.49**, including the d=8 K=64 crack cell, out of sample) and the critical ratio moves only **1.36×** across d — but **forcing the ratio to 4.90, deep inside the "safe" zone, destroys retrieval (0.594)**, and capacity is **monotone *increasing*** in width over 0.15→0.40, the opposite sign to `K ∝ (sep/s)^d`. **`lattice-capacity-theory` §5.2 is REFUTED BY EXPERIMENT** (`atom_init_width 0.30→0.15` moves `K_learned(4)` **below** 16: 0.9368 ± 0.0133 → 0.5944 ± 0.0164, 3 seeds, **28 SE**, flat at 2× atoms); **§4.2 is a correlate only.** **(b) The "d-independent WRITE-OPERATOR ceiling" phrasing is also not the mechanism** — a pure operator/representation ceiling cannot produce a critical `sep/width` stable to 1.36× across d, nor a failure **perfectly ordered by the STORED VALUE rather than the address** (corr **−0.887** with `|a_i|`; small-`|a|` 1.000 vs large-`|a|` 0.172). **(c) What binds is REACH:** the read launches on the payload = 0 manifold, so the well width is bounded below by `σ_q` **and above-usefully by `|a|_max/κ`, κ ≈ 3** — the shipped 0.30 sits at that second bound, and the write pushes any narrower init back toward it (+23 %). **The w23 walls sit on the excursion's far side** (half excursion, tolerance halved: d=4 K=32 **0.824 → 1.000**; d=4 K=64 → **0.9922**, at both widths) ⇒ ⚠ **mechanism result at a different task point, NOT a capacity number — no `K_learned` at pscale ≠ 1.** **(d) A SECOND, ADDITIVE contribution is measured the same wave (N98/w25):** atoms starting inside *other items'* wells cost **+0.051 (monolithic) / +0.082 (sharded)** at d=6 K=64 when repaired ⇒ part of what read as "operator interference" is an **initialisation** defect. **Every measured number in N92 and N96 STANDS unchanged**; only the *attribution* moves. ⛔ **New never-quote: "the ceiling is the write operator" and "width-lock as cause" are BOTH retired** — quote *"the learned-capacity ceiling is a read-out reach condition (well width bounded below by σ_q, above-usefully by `|a|_max/κ`); `sep/width` is a sharp d≥4 correlate, not the cause."* The CONTESTED flag is **CLEARED with a third answer.**

### N93 — (two refined pre-registrations) sized geometry stops at per-offered 0.669, and refuse-and-relocate costs ~4× a read  · tier B (HUB-CONFIRMED) · memory-architecture

- **P7 — refined, not confirmed (`controller-mvp` §5, recon 2):** registered *"sized geometry reaches per-offered ≈1.0 and beats all primitives"*; measured **0.669 at K=64 — it beats all four primitives (gru 0.57) but does NOT reach 1.0.** Mechanism: **achieved packing of *random* disk proposals is below the ideal bound — admitted 42.8 of 64** (the `d_eff < d` shell-concentration effect already measured in `address-space-dimension-scaling`). **A packing-efficiency limit, not a controller limit**; farthest-point proposal sampling (untested) is the named cheap lever. On fixed geometry the same effect shows as **5.2 ± 0.4 admitted vs N_pack 6.12 (0.85× the bound)**, consistent with N74's 6.0 ± 0.9.
- **P9 — falsified as stated (`controller-mvp` §3(d), §5):** registered *"admission < 5% of a gradient write"*; measured **the gate itself is trivial — 0.006 ms** (O(n_stored) distances) **but refuse-and-relocate reaches 3.1 ms at n_stored=64 ≈ 4× one 0.70 ms read** (400 relocation candidates × min-separation). **≪ a gradient-trained write (~200 steps), but NOT free relative to a read.** Knobs that trade admitted-quality for speed: `n_relocation_candidates`, proposal-disk width.
- **Disposition:** both are **honest refinements of the controller's approved wording**, not defects: quote per-offered-under-sized-geometry as **0.669 (packing-limited)**, never ≈1.0; and quote admission cost as **"gate cheap, relocation ~4× a read"**, never "admission is free." Recorded so the numbers do not drift upward in a draft.

### N94 — ⭐ (methodological, standing caveat) Diagnostics computed on `<40`-epoch CAFE fits are not properties of the shipped model  · tier A (HUB-CONFIRMED) · all (instrument validity)

- **The pattern:** of the three measurement conflicts adjudicated at w23, **two dissolved into training-maturity artifacts** — not physics disagreements, not bugs (`r19-r20-reconciliations` recon 4: *"the harnesses behaved as written"*).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** **(i) ballistic fraction** — 40 epochs/2000 windows gives **94.75% global / 96.33% per-sample** (reproducing the audit's under-trained *regime*, whose reported digit was **98.3%**), while the fully-trained 150-epoch fit gives **76.97%** at legacy `dt=0.05` and **50.49%** at the shipped `dt=0.125`. Carrier ranking: **epochs (−10 pp)** > window count (−7.5 pp) > aggregation convention (±9 pp) > preprocessing (~2 pp); **`dt` is not the carrier** (both originals were legacy). **(ii) single-basin collapse** — `q*` spread by epoch at dt=1.0, seed 42, γ=0.5: **9.15e-08 (10 ep)** → 0.0872 (20) → 0.1305 (40) → 0.6202 (80) → **0.31–0.67 (150, 3 seeds)**, **100% finite and f32 ≡ f64 to 6 digits** at every point.
- **Why it matters (mechanism):** an under-trained potential is *a different physical object* — one trivial well, weak forces, everything settling to ≈one point — and its order parameters (ballistic fraction, `q*` spread, force/free ratio) sit in a regime the shipped model never occupies. Both artifacts **anneal away monotonically** with training.
- **Standing rule adopted:** **every diagnostic quoted from a CAFE fit must state its epoch count**, and no `<40`-epoch diagnostic may be presented as a property of the shipped model. This *joins*, and does not replace, the w17 rule (*an order parameter that hits a floating-point-exact value is an overflow suspect until proven otherwise* — here the overflow explanation was correctly retracted and the true cause was under-training).
- **Scope/limitation:** the audit's exact 98.3% digit was **not bit-reproduced** (its manual global z-score + seed subsample differ) — the *regime* was; and the analyst could not construct a *trained* model with both a strong potential and a point collapse (the residual gap; the named decider is to log per-epoch spread of the audit's literal `ballistic.py` model). R19-1 and R20-1 rest on **seed 42 alone** (R19-2 used 3 seeds); the verdict margins are ≫ the known FD001 seed spread (≈0.002 h-AUROC), so the **verdicts** are seed-robust and the **digits** are single-seed.

### N97 — ⛔ Post-settle (relaxed) energy is NOT a routing / confidence / match signal at equal well depth  · tier A (HUB-CONFIRMED) · memory-architecture (broad guard)

- **Tried:** three candidate routers for a sharded/product store, on the real Gaussian functional form, d=2, geometry sized to the load (`R = 0.808√K`), 3 seeds × 8 queries/item, σ_q = 0.10, N∈{2,4,8} shards, K up to 32 (`lattice-capacity-theory` §2.1, checkD). **R1** = `argmin_r V_r(x_final)` (post-settle energy) · **R2** = `argmin_r V_r(q)` (pre-settle / nearest-well score) · **R3** = `argmin_r ‖x_final − q‖` (settling displacement).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** **R1 routes AT OR BELOW chance** — 0.365 (N=2) / 0.099 / **0.031** (N=4, chance 0.25) / **0.031** (N=8, chance 0.125), global allocation. **R2 and R3 are EXACT** — **1.000/1.000 route/value** up to N=8 shards and K=32, with **zero learning and fully interleaved shards** (shard centroids coincide near the ball centre, so a centroid/Voronoi router fails where R2 succeeds).
- **Why it failed (mechanism — structural, not tuning):** every shard's wells have the **same depth**, so the post-settle energy measures **which well the query fell into, not how well it matched.** Pre-registered as P6 and **REFUTED.**
- **Scope:** analytic Gaussian stores with gradient-flow settling (not the two-phase `γ_addr→γ_read` Verlet rollout), 3 shard counts; the router scores are evaluated on the real functional form, so the R1-broken / R2-R3-exact conclusion depends only on the scores (R3's constants could shift under the true settling path; R2 is pre-settle and does not).
- **Disposition:** **a BROAD warning across the program:** if anything relies on relaxed / post-settle energy as a confidence, routing, or match score, that assumption is **wrong at equal well depth.** Route on pre-settle energy (R2) or settling displacement (R3); explicitly **do not ship R1.** ⚠ Companion caveat (N89 discipline): R2 is, at the read moment, a classical nearest-neighbour score over stored addresses — the routing half of a sharded store is classical indexing; **"capacity multiplies by sharding" must never be presented as a dynamical result.**
- > **⛔ EXTENDED (wave-25, `lattice-sharded-store` §2 → N104) — the recommendation NARROWS to R2 alone: settling displacement (R3) is broken too on the shipped geometry.** The original text above recommends *"route on pre-settle energy (R2) **or settling displacement (R3)** — both exact (1.000)"*. Measured on the **shipped designed store** (d=4, K=32, 3 seeds, no write, global allocation): **R3 = 1.000 / 0.549 / 0.236 / 0.228 at N = 1/2/4/8 while R2 stays 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000.** Structural, not tuning: `BallRegisterPotential` is **flat inside the address ball by design**, so at an item's site the **owning** shard's gradient is ≈0 (it is a minimum: `V = −0.991`, ‖∇V‖ **2.9e-4**) *and* a **foreign** shard's is ≈0 (flat vacuum + an exponentially small tail: `V = −8.0e-5`, ‖∇V‖ **2.3e-3**) — the displacements are comparable small numbers while the **energies differ by 4 orders**. **Same failure class as R1.** ⇒ **Corrected disposition: post-settle energy (R1) AND settling displacement (R3) are both broken; only pre-settle energy (R2) and the classical registry (RG) survive**, and the design rule generalises to *"the routing statistic must be evaluable **without running the dynamics**"* (R2 and RG are; R1 is not — and R1 is also the one that does not work). **N97's original numbers are unaffected** — they were measured on analytic Gaussian stores with gradient-flow settling, where R3 *was* exact, and N97's own scope line anticipated exactly this (*"R3's constants could shift under the true settling path; R2 is pre-settle and does not"*). Enforced in code: `router_scores("R1", …)` raises with the N97 reason (`test_r1_router_is_not_shipped`).

### N98 — Shard independence is violated by atom INITIALISATION, not physics (a design guard that carries its fix)  · tier B (HUB-CONFIRMED) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** is a masked write on disjoint atom groups bit-identical to N independent optimizers? — the write-locality claim behind capacity-by-sharding (`lattice-capacity-theory` §1.4, checkB: real `write_loss` + `AtomDictionaryPotential(n_groups=K)` + `optax.adamw`, K=4 items, 4 groups × 32 atoms, sites 1.414 apart, 200 Adam steps).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** NOT bit-identical — `centers` max‖Δ‖ **6.50e-3** (rel 2.4e-3), `log_width` **1.29e-2** (8.7e-3), `amp` **8.23e-3** (rel **1.4e-2**); `V` at the stored sites max Δ **2.9e-3** (≈0.5% of well depth). This residual is **~3 orders LARGER than the site tail** `exp(−1.414²/2·0.3²) = 1.5e-5`. Pre-registered P3 (residual at the site tail) **FAILED.** Control (same loop without the mask): **128/128 atoms move**, max Δamp 0.725.
- **Why it failed (mechanism — init defect, not physics):** `init_scale=1.0` scatters *every* group's 32 atoms over the whole ball, so group *j* has atoms inside item *i*'s well from step 0; the write for item *i* must compensate for foreign atoms, and a shard-independent write cannot. **Prop L2 is sound** — AdamW's `(m,v)` state is per-parameter, so under masked writes the optimizer factorizes into blocks and *N* independent optimizers ≡ one masked joint optimizer, given W3 (loss-gradient separability). W3 fails here **only** because of the init scatter.
- **Scope:** 200 write steps (not w23's 600), K=4 at d=2; the frontier-size (d=6, K=64, 4096 atoms) violation is extrapolated. Budget with the defect left in: `√N · 1.4% < 10%` ⇒ **N ≲ 50 shards** before the init defect alone costs a tenth of the well depth — not binding for anything planned.
- **Disposition:** carries the **fix** (localize group *j*'s atoms in a ball of radius ~`2s` around site *j*, or spatially partition the atom init — a ~5-line change plus a flag); then W3 holds to the site tail and Prop L2 is exact in practice. A design guard for any w25 sharding build, not a wall. Companion trap from the same audit (for the w25 engineer, not a negative): `fixed_norm` query jitter `σ/√d_total` per axis silently shrinks per-shard query noise if shards are coordinate blocks of one wide unit — fix query noise **per shard**.
- > **⭐ WAVE-25 — THE FIX IS BUILT AND MEASURED, AND IT IS A FIRST-ORDER LEVER, NOT A SIDE-ISSUE (`lattice-sharded-store` §5 → the wave's biggest single knob).** Applied identically to both arms, 3 seeds, d=6 K=64, radius `2s = 0.6`, **address axes only**: **monolithic 0.8288 ± 0.0186 → 0.8802 ± 0.0075 (+0.051)** and **sharded 2×32 0.8434 ± 0.0253 → 0.9251 ± 0.0030 PASS (+0.082)**; it also **repairs the dynamical router (R2 route accuracy 0.913 → 0.970)** and halves the payload error (0.1345 → 0.0678). Pre-registered P10 (≥ +0.02 / +0.01) **CONFIRMED 2–4× larger than registered.** Two load-bearing design choices: **(a) it ships OFF by default and is bit-identical when disabled** — the localized draw uses `jax.random.fold_in(key, 1)` so even the RNG stream of the default path is untouched (`test_localized_atom_init_is_bit_identical_when_disabled`); **(b) address axes ONLY** — the payload axis keeps the w23 `init_scale = 1.0` scatter, because localizing it would hand the writer the value it is supposed to learn (N46) *and* destroy the basin-reach property N100 shows is load-bearing (a well initialised at payload 0 cannot reach `|a_i| = 1`). ⚠ **It is an INITIALISATION, so it is a finding about w23's init, not about sharding** — which is why it was pre-registered on a separate axis and kept out of the headline 2×2; note it does **not on its own** lift the monolithic cell over the bar (0.880 < 0.90) — **sharding + the init fix does** (0.925). ⭐ **It bears directly on the N92/N96 mechanism question as a SECOND, ADDITIVE contribution** (part of what read as "operator interference" is atoms starting inside other items' wells) — distinct from, and additive to, N100's reach condition. ⛔ **NOT promoted to a default:** the Head ruled *NOT YET* (Addendum-2 decision 4, 2026-07-28) — the **2×2 init × width factorial with the interaction term** must run first (`r2-excursion-reach` Stage A, w26), because the two levers may be the same effect twice. **Tier B unchanged** (it remains a design guard that carries its fix — the *lever* status is recorded here, not re-tiered; Hub may re-tier).
- > **⚠⚠ WAVE-26 — CROSS-HARNESS CAVEAT (READER WARNING, Hub-owed, `r2-excursion-reach` §1 → N111). N98's +0.051 DOES NOT REPRODUCE on the designed-mechanism harness.** The 2×2 init × width factorial the Head required before promotion ran at the same nominal cell (**d=6, K=64, monolithic, 3 seeds, value-blank on all 12 cells**) and measures the localized init's main effect at the shipped width as **+0.0068 ± 0.016 — a NULL** (vs N98's +0.051 on `exp_sharded_store`). The two harnesses differ (allocator / partition / router vs a value-blank-gated designed-mechanism run), so **this is a cross-harness NON-REPLICATION, not a refutation of N98's own measured number — both stand, in their own harnesses.** What it forbids is the *generalisation*: ⛔ **`atom_init_local` may not be quoted as a general localized-init gain.** What the factorial does show is that the two levers are **SUBSTITUTES** (interaction **+0.4590, SE 0.0321 ⇒ 14.3 SE**; the localized init recovers 65 % of a bad width's damage — 0.1429 → 0.6087 — and buys **nothing** once the width is right). ⛔ **Still NOT a default** (`atom_init_local = False`); the Head's precondition has now been met and the answer was *no promotion*. **Tier B unchanged.** ⚠ One confound the factorial did not close: the localization radius is `mult × atom_init_width`, so the two width arms localize at **different radii**; the fixed-radius control is NOT RUN.

### N99 — ⛔ (blocking technical gap) The MVC-0 controller makes the store HISTORY-DEPENDENT ⇒ CLU cannot claim even EXACT deletion  · tier A (HUB-CONFIRMED) · memory-architecture / positioning

- **Tried:** the web-scout audit of R1's "certified per-item lifetimes" against the machine-unlearning literature — pin what *certified* formally requires, whether "deletion by construction" is already owned, and whether the store can claim exact deletion (`unlearning-recon`, item 3 / recon 3).
- **The gap (verbatim):** the MVC-0 controller's **refuse-and-relocate** places item *j* as a function of item *i* being present, and **LRU/staleness eviction** removes item *k* because *i* occupied budget (`controller-mvp` §1, N91). ⇒ **removing item *i* from the store does NOT reproduce the store that would have existed had *i* never been written** — which is the definition of *exact* unlearning. R1 cannot claim exactness without either **(a)** re-running placement on the retained set (= retraining the store — the thing unlearning tries to avoid) or **(b)** a placement rule **proven order-independent.** Nobody owns this yet; it is a real technical gap, not a framing gap.
- **Why it matters (mechanism):** *certified* in this literature = formal (ε,δ)-statistical indistinguishability from retraining (Guo et al., ICML 2020, Def 1–2) and requires a randomized mechanism + explicit noise + a proof — CLU's deterministic decay/evict path satisfies **none** of the four requirements. But the controller history-dependence means the store fails even the *weaker*, unqualified **exact** deletion claim. Thudi et al. (USENIX'22): unlearning is well-defined only at the *algorithmic* level — which is the one form of claim the field accepts, **provided** this history-dependence is fixed.
- **Scope:** the MVC-0 controller as built (designed store). Also unanswered by measurement: whether a partially-decayed well (amp 0.06) is distinguishable to an MIA adversary at one half-life, and what the payload retains after `evict` — both untested, both flagged for w25.
- > **⭐⭐ WAVE-25 — TWO UPDATES IN ONE BLOCK: the gap now has a MAGNITUDE, and exit (b) is DELIVERED at theory+reference level.**
  > **(a) The magnitude (`mia-decay-measurement` §2 → N108's companion).** The history-dependence gap is **not a technicality — it is the dominant residual leak, and it is stronger than every amplitude-channel effect measured in the same harness.** Under the shipped `refuse-and-relocate` + budget placement, writing item *i* guarantees a `d_safe = 1.54` **exclusion disk** around `c_i` that survives *i*'s eviction, so **distance-to-nearest-live-site (`z_hole`) separates IN from OUT at AUC 0.99985 ± 0.00070, TPR 1.000 @ FPR 1 %** — *after the item is physically gone from `V`*. Contrast the clean half: with **placement held fixed** (paired-placement OUT) every post-evict statistic is **0.5000 ± 0.0000** on all four statistics (the two stores are bit-identical) — **so the amplitude channel closes exactly and the ALLOCATOR channel does not.** Other history-condition statistics: `s2` address-capture 0.7828 ± 0.1435, `s4` white-box address-channel 0.7599 ± 0.0644 (TPR 1.000 @ 1 %), `s5` 0.7106 ± 0.0796, `n_live` 0.8114 ± 0.0349. ⚠ **Occupancy caveat, stated by the source:** measured at **7/8 of the packing bound — near-full, the most favourable case for a "hole" statistic** — and it **must be re-measured at low occupancy before being quoted as a general number** (`carried-remeasurements`, w26). Companion defect **D1**: `evict` clears `active`/`amps` only — `centers[slot]`/`payloads[slot]` retain the written values verbatim (max err 5.62e−8 / 0.0 over 3 072 evictions); invisible to `V`, so no measured result moves, but *"the item is gone"* is false at the data-structure level.

- **Scope:** Split-MNIST only (the CIFAR arm is **N102**); one φ family (PCA-32); baselines are internally-matched **reimplementations**, not Mammoth/Avalanche runs; ⚠ **LwF is the one baseline not reproduced** (19.6 vs published 23.9, 4.3 pp low) — **it must be re-tuned before this table is published** (it changes no conclusion here, but it *is* the best rehearsal-free baseline on CIFAR, where CLU loses to it); SI uses an end-of-task displacement estimate of the path integral; the read decodes by **nearest live address after settling** — classical indexing (N89), which is exactly why both laundering lines are mandatory; per-admitted is deliberately **not** reported as an accuracy number (in Class-IL the test set is independent of what was admitted).
- **Disposition:** **the three computed sentences ALWAYS travel together** — *wins the rehearsal-free class +0.510 (over a class that fails by construction)* · *deficit vs replay −0.153 (a CM-23(n) publishable success)* · *laundered −0.036*. ⚠ **Whether this counts as "an external benchmark won" was a Head call, and the answer is NO for the score sentence** (Addendum-2 decision 2, 2026-07-28): supplementary only, two-clause form, **the program's score sentence is unchanged until a contested win lands**. ⭐ The non-laundered axis this identifies — **forgetting at matched BYTES** (24.5× fewer floats) — is the program's nearest primary-claim candidate and is commissioned as `matched-bytes-frontier` (w26).
- > **⛔⭐ WAVE-26 — THE MATCHED-BYTES AXIS RAN, AND IT REVERSES THE MATCHED-ITEMS PICTURE WITHOUT RESCUING THE CLAIM (`matched-bytes-frontier` → N113/N114/N115).** At matched **bytes** (6 budgets × 50× span × 3 seeds) the ACC ordering against replay **inverts**: CLU is **higher at 6/6** (**0.903 ± 0.003 vs iCaRL 0.885 ± 0.002** at 1.2 MiB) where at matched **items** it sat **0.153 below** iCaRL — ⇒ ⚠ **N101's −0.153 is a matched-ITEMS statement and must never be quoted as a matched-bytes one.** ⛔ **But the launder is never beaten** (ring buffer lower forgetting 6/6, higher ACC 6/6) and ⭐⛔ **the *same-keys* launder — the settle deleted, nothing else changed — also beats the store 6/6 on both axes (mean +0.013 ACC, −0.011 forgetting)** ⇒ **on this benchmark the physics is a measured ≈1 pp net negative** (N114). ⚠ **NUMERIC CORRECTION that travels wherever N101's table is quoted: "24.5× fewer floats" → 19.1×** (the pinned accounting charges the store **41**, not 32, floats/item: `centers` 32 + payload + amp + active + the non-redundant `ItemRecord` scalars; the ring buffer 34; a raw exemplar 785). ⚠ Also: **iCaRL ran up to 2.5× OVER its item budget** at small budgets in the w25 table (fixed in w26; **at 200 items the w25 number is unaffected**), and **LwF's 4.3 pp deficit is a CE-scope convention, not a tuning failure** (N116) — the re-tune N101's scope line demanded is **done and closed as "not a fix"**.

### N102 — ⛔ Split-CIFAR-10 is a NULL for the CL entry, and the failure is the FEATURE SPACE, not the stream discipline  · tier A (HUB-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the same entry, same code path, on **Split-CIFAR-10** under a declared **reduced protocol** (`apply_cifar10`: 3-layer CNN 16-32-32+128 for the baselines, 1 000 train / 500 test per task, 150 optimizer steps — identical for every method), 3 seeds, φ = **PCA-32 of raw pixels** fit on task-1 classes only (`cl-entry-build` Item 5).
- **Numbers (verbatim, 3 seeds):** ⛔ **CLU entry (task1_only) 0.149 ± 0.013 / BWT −0.157** — **below every rehearsal-free baseline**: LwF **0.162 ± 0.001**, EWC 0.154 ± 0.004, SI 0.153 ± 0.005, finetune 0.152 ± 0.010 ⇒ `wins_rehearsal_free_class = **False**` (−0.013 vs LwF). Replay: iCaRL 0.419 ± 0.003, ER 0.369 ± 0.006, GDumb 0.301 ± 0.023, joint 0.480 ± 0.005 ⇒ `deficit_vs_replay = −0.270`. Launder: kNN-in-φ ring buffer **0.219 ± 0.014** ⇒ `laundered = True`, **−0.070**. **`strict_phi_cost = +0.0011`.**
- **Why it failed (mechanism — three independent lines, all measured):** (1) **the strict/leaky φ split costs nothing** (0.149 vs 0.150) ⇒ whatever is broken is broken in **both** — this **falsifies the report's own pre-registered F1 band (+0.02…+0.15)** and, more consequentially, **refutes the w24 expectation that "CIFAR is where a strict φ should bite": strictness does not bite, the feature space does**; (2) **a 200-prototype kNN over the same φ keys only reaches 0.207–0.222** ⇒ *no store built on those addresses can be competitive, because the addresses do not separate the classes*; (3) **the store's own retrieval on those same addresses is essentially perfect** (stored-item recall **1.000 at p=0.5, 0.863 at p=0.8**) ⇒ **the memory works; what it holds is uninformative about the label.** Geometry rules out crowding as the differentiator: corrected packing slack **0.337–0.345**, essentially MNIST's 0.33.
- **⭐ The mechanism still shows in the same place as on MNIST:** CLU BWT **−0.157** vs the parametric rehearsal-free methods' **−0.70 … −0.78** — a 4.5–5× smaller backward-transfer loss at 0.149 absolute. *The store does not forget; it never knew.* Item 4 (retention) reproduces identically on CIFAR: permanent amplitude exactly 1.000 (max err 0.0), slow/fast follow `exp(−leak·t)` to ≤6.8e-8, **only the fast cohort self-evicts (82/75/76 items), zero slow, zero permanent**.
- **Scope:** ⚠ these are **not literature-comparable Split-CIFAR-10 numbers** (reduced protocol, stated in-code and in the report) — they are an internally-matched comparison; the finding is about **that φ** (PCA-32 on raw pixels), not about CIFAR.
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **The entry's scope is MNIST-class data until a CIFAR-capable φ exists — say so in every CL sentence.** Reported as the pre-registered F4 headline finding, not buried. ⭐ **A CIFAR-capable φ is now R4's single blocking dependency** (cheap next test: the existing `ae` arm at `phi_dim ∈ {32,64}`; the real answer is a small conv/SSL φ fit on task-1 classes only) — commissioned as `cl-encoder` (w26) with a **cheap decisive gate: does kNN-in-φ on Split-CIFAR-10 clear 0.35 (now 0.21)?** ⚠ **Trap stated in the w26 task and worth restating here: a better φ raises the launder by construction.**
- > **⭐ WAVE-26 — THE NULL NOW HAS TWO CAUSES, AND ONE OF THEM IS FIXED (`cl-encoder` → N121/N122).** **(1) The address space, fixed:** a task-1-only SSL conv φ (`simclr`, `phi_dim = 256`) moves the kNN-in-φ ceiling **0.219 ± 0.017 → 0.339 ± 0.015 (8 000 fit steps) → 0.357 ± 0.019 (20 000)** with **zero** change to the store or the stream discipline ⇒ ⛔ **N102's *"a 200-prototype kNN over the same φ reaches only 0.207–0.222"* is SUPERSEDED — restate this entry's scope boundary at the new number.** The 0.35 gate is **MISSED at the registered arm and CLEARED at 2.5× fit compute, by less than one seed-σ** ⇒ ⛔ **never "the gate was cleared" without the fit budget.** **(2) The 200-item budget, measured:** the gate goes 0.339 → **0.357 (400 items)** → **0.398 (1000)** → **0.455 (5000)** at the 8 k arm ⇒ ≈ **+0.02 per doubling**, and **it clears at 400 items even at the under-trained arm** — so w25's single-cause framing is now **the larger half of a two-term explanation.** ⚠ **AND THE ENTRY'S OWN CONCLUSION IS PARTLY REVERSED: strictness DOES bite on a working φ.** N102's `strict_phi_cost = +0.0011` is a property of a **broken** φ; at the SSL arm the pool-matched cost is **+0.020 ± 0.010 (3/3 seeds)** and it is **exactly the difference between clearing and missing** (leaky 0.358 clears, defensible 0.339 misses) — N122. ⚠ **Every number here is a kNN/launder number**; the store's own retrieval at the new φ is **unmeasured** (no settle was run), and the **CIFAR entry run is a pre-registered, Head-DECLINED NOT-RUN** — filed as registered-and-declined, ⛔ **never as a null** (N121). Unchanged: the packing slack at the new arm is **0.332**, indistinguishable from N102's 0.337–0.345 ⇒ **a better φ does not de-crowd the store.**

### N103 — ◐⭐ The first NON-LOSING anytime read is a TIE, in the one regime where no oracle can be constructed  · tier A (HUB-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture / all

- **Tried:** the R3-**native** measurement the w24 review named as the only untested route — retry inside the running CL entry, where the corruption is applied in **pixel space** (dropout `p` on the stored image) and the store is addressed in **φ**, so there is **no "known-erased" coordinate subset of the store's space** and the `feedforward_nn_masked` oracle that sat at 1.000 and beat CLU in all 8 w24 cells **cannot be constructed**. Honest floors: 1-shot **kNN-in-φ** and its matched-compute version **feedforward-in-φ** (which is also the laundering control). Headline cell: end-of-stream, crowded store (199–200 wells), `p = 0.8`, **6 seeds** (`cl-entry-build` Item 3).
- **Numbers (verbatim, 6 seeds, mean ± sd):** first pass **0.839 ± 0.025** → **gated best 0.885 ± 0.018 @ 1.40 ± 0.20× compute**; **random-kick 0.839 ± 0.025**, **ensemble 0.841 ± 0.026**, **ungated-all @k=8 → 0.000**; floors **kNN-in-φ 0.874 ± 0.025**, **feedforward-in-φ 0.877 ± 0.025**. ⇒ **gated − kick = +4.6 ± 2.2 pp, 6/6 seeds** (the equal-energy kick **never once** improves on the first pass); gated − ensemble **+4.4 ± 2.2 pp**; **gated − ff-in-φ = +0.8 ± 1.6 pp (3/6 positive)**; gated − 1-shot kNN **+1.1 ± 1.4 pp (5/6)**. Mid-stream (after task 3, 3 seeds): first 0.828 ± 0.012 → gated **0.858 ± 0.018 @ 1.30 ± 0.14×**, gated − kNN **+0.010 ± 0.007** ⇒ **the picture does not change between mid-stream and end-of-stream.** Confidence signal: cosine-to-nearest-well AUROC **0.65–0.85**; distance-to-well 0.51–0.60 (near-useless in φ).
- **Why this is a TIE and not a win (the discipline that produced it):** the agent **pre-registered** that a CLU win here must be re-run before belief; **seeds 3,4,5 are that re-run, and they turn an apparent +0.7 pp win (seeds 0–2) into a tie.** Neither floor margin is separated from zero. ⭐ **It is nonetheless the first regime in the program's history where the anytime read is not *below* the correct floor** (w24: −3.5 … −38 pp in **8/8** cells).
- **⚠ Two caveats that must travel:** (1) **one dataset, one corruption level** — at `p = 0.5` the cell is saturated (first pass 0.99, floor 1.000) and every line is flat; **on CIFAR the kNN-in-φ floor is 1.000**, so the anytime read cannot win there either (gated − kNN **−0.055 ± 0.019** end-of-stream) — *a saturated floor is unbeatable, which is why the MNIST p=0.8 cell is the one that carries the result*. (2) ⚠ **τ is NOT the binding element of the gate in φ-space** (`a95e213` + a dedicated seed-3 probe at the hardest level): τ ∈ {0.99, 0.999, 0.9999, 1.0} give **identical curves** (0.830@1.0× → 0.870@1.1× → 0.880@1.2× → **0.905@1.4×** → 0.900@1.8×) because after a damped settle in a crowded φ store essentially every read sits below cosine 0.99 — what produces the curve is **the ranking + the 10 %-per-round budget + the lock**. **This is a behavioural difference from w24** (where τ = 1.0 demonstrably over-retried and cost accuracy) and it is **1 seed** ⇒ the gate's *threshold* clause must not be quoted as load-bearing in φ-space until multi-seeded (`carried-remeasurements`, w26).
- **⭐ Free companion finding (inverts an assumption in the R3 framing):** there is **no forgetting-by-age in the store** — task-age spread is **6.2 pp** (≤10 pp as pre-registered) and the trend runs **opposite** to the registered direction: the **newest** task's items are hardest to recall (0.796 ± 0.069) because they were admitted last into an already-crowded store, while task 0's items (0.846 ± 0.073) have had every later item pass the spacing gate against them. ⛔ Do not write "retrieval degrades as the store crowds with age."
- **Disposition:** **approved wording — *"in the one regime with no constructible oracle, the anytime read TIES the honest matched-compute floor while beating every mechanism control"* — never "wins".** A control had to be rebuilt to get an honest floor at all: `exp_retry_compute._feedforward_ladder`'s `clip(|q+noise|, 0, 1)` TTA is **valid for pixels and destructive for a signed zero-mean φ vector** (the line collapsed to ~0.005 with k, i.e. it was never a floor); `_feedforward_ladder_phi` (additive noise scaled to the store's own median address spacing, no clipping) replaces it and the pixel line is retained in the JSON under an explicit `INVALID_in_phi` name so the w24 comparison stays auditable. ⇒ **any future φ-space use of `exp_retry_compute` must use the corrected control or it will silently report a collapsing, meaningless "floor"** (§7-CURRENT defect, w25).
- > **⚠ WAVE-26 — CAVEAT (2) IS NARROWED, NOT RETRACTED, AND THE COMPETING HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED (`carried-remeasurements` §1 → N117).** N103's clause *"τ is NOT the binding element of the gate in φ-space … the threshold clause must not be quoted as load-bearing in φ-space"* **replicates exactly** — at **p = 0.8**, all four thresholds give **bit-identical** ladders (`max|Δacc| = max|Δcompute| = 0.000e+00`, **3/3 seeds × 2 store snapshots = 6/6 cells**, asserted with `==` on floats) — **but it is TOO GENERAL.** At **p = 0.5, in the same φ store, minutes apart**, the identity is **false in 6/6 cells** and **τ = 1.0 costs −0.485 ± 0.064 accuracy** (−0.546 ± 0.023 end-of-stream; e.g. 0.9950 → 0.4171) while spending **1.80×** instead of 1.12–1.30×. ⇒ **The correct statement is a rule, not a space:** *the threshold is load-bearing **iff `#{cos₀ < τ} < k·step_n`*** (pool ≥ 160/200 at p = 0.8; 24–60/200 at p = 0.5). ⛔ **"φ-space vs pixel-space" was the analyst's own pre-registered hypothesis (T5) and it is FALSIFIED — do not keep that framing.** **w24 and w25 measured the two ends of one axis; neither is retracted.** ⛔ **Any statement about the threshold names the corruption level.** The laundering picture is unchanged by the remeasurement: the gate **ties** the matched-compute kNN-in-φ floor at p = 0.8 (0.8631 vs 0.8698, −0.007 ± 0.010) — **the tie stands and is not upgraded.**

### N104 — ⛔ Settling-displacement routing (R3) is broken on the shipped flat-vacuum geometry — only R2 and the classical registry survive  · tier A (HUB-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (broad guard)

- **Tried:** the §5.3 read-parity check (Prop L4) on **designed** shards with **no write at all**, so the read side is isolated from the write ceiling under test — d=4, K=32, 3 seeds, deadband 0, global vs local allocation, N ∈ {1,2,4,8}, routers **R2** (`argmin_r V_r(q)`, pre-settle energy) and **R3** (`argmin_r ‖x_final − q‖`, settling displacement) (`lattice-sharded-store` §2).
- **Numbers (verbatim, global allocation, strict / route):** **R3 = 1.000 / 0.5495 / 0.2363 / 0.2279** at N = 1/2/4/8, while **R2 = 1.0000 / 1.0000 / 1.0000 / 1.0000** with route accuracy 1.000 at every N. Under local allocation R3 = 1.000 / 0.8984 / 0.4401 / 0.2220 (R2 1.000 / 0.9935 / 0.9863 / 0.9779). **P5 (global-allocator parity) CONFIRMED EXACTLY: `max |Δ vs monolithic| = 0.0000` at N = 2, 4, 8 with R2** ⇒ **Prop L4 stands — sharding conserves read-side discrimination and there is no unmodelled cross-shard channel.**
- **Why it failed (mechanism — structural, not tuning; pinned by a unit test rather than asserted):** at item 0's site the **owning** shard has `V = −0.991` with gradient norm **2.9e-4** (it is a minimum) and the **foreign** shard has `V = −8.0e-5` with gradient norm **2.3e-3**. `BallRegisterPotential` is **flat inside the address ball by design**, so the forces that drive the displacement are **≈0 in every shard and within an order of magnitude of each other**, while the **energies differ by ≥3–4 orders**. **R2 has a huge signal; R3 has none.**
- **Scope:** the shipped designed store's flat-vacuum register geometry, d=4, K=32, N ≤ 8, no write. N97's R3 result was measured on **analytic Gaussian stores with gradient-flow settling**, where R3 *was* exact (1.000) — the two are not in conflict, and N97's own scope line anticipated it (*"R3's constants could shift under the true settling path"*): **R3's exactness does not survive the shipped potential's flat interior.**
- **Disposition:** ⭐ **N97 is EXTENDED, not overturned** (see its dated block): *"post-settle energy (R1) **and** settling displacement (R3) are both broken; only pre-settle energy (R2) and the classical registry (RG) survive."* This overturns a **shipped recommendation** and imposes a design rule: **the routing statistic must be evaluable without running the dynamics** — R2 and RG are, R1 is not, and R1 is also the one that does not work. Enforced in code (`router_scores("R1", …)` raises *with the N97 reason*; `test_r1_router_is_not_shipped`). ⚠ Companion (N89 discipline, unchanged): R2 is, at the read moment, a classical nearest-well score — **the routing half of a sharded store is classical indexing.**

### N105 — ◐ Sharded additivity is real on the write side and partly spent on the read side (`K = 32N` is NOT unclamped)  · tier A (HUB-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the first real N-unit sharded CLU store (`CLULattice` container, the N98 localized init, a **global** address allocator/registry, routers R2/R3 + a classical registry router RG, per-shard query noise, ⛔ no R1) and the §5.1 **2×2 discriminator**: does splitting the same items across N units, each written by its own dig, clear a wall the monolithic store cannot? Geometry/read/write/pass criterion **inherited verbatim from w23/w24**; laundering control = **the monolithic store at the same `K_total` and matched total atoms**; 3 seeds everywhere except the d=8 monolithic line (2, declared) (`lattice-sharded-store` §1).
- **Numbers (verbatim, §1, bar = 0.90, every PASS blank-controlled):**
  - **d=6 K=64 — the wall IS fixed by sharding, two independent ways.** With the **shipped dynamical router** and the N98 localized init: **sharded 2×32 (matched atoms) 0.9251 ± 0.0030 PASS** vs the **monolithic laundering line at identical init and identical total atoms 0.8802 ± 0.0075** ⇒ Δ = **+0.045 (≈6 sd)**, crossing 0.90 where the monolithic does not. With **no init change**, using the classical registry router: **0.9043 ± 0.0064 vs 0.8288 ± 0.0186** ⇒ Δ = **+0.076**. The budget-adequate arm also passes (per-shard 0.9150 ± 0.0115 RG).
  - **d=4 K=32 — the control is NOT fixed** (see N106) ⇒ **had it passed, the law would be `K = 32N` unclamped. It did not.** Reading: **`K_total = min( K_addr(Q, s, σ_q) , Σ_r K_write(unit r) )`** (THEOREM-L1).
  - **The routing cost, measured as `RG − R2`:** 0.061 / 0.067 (d=6 2×32 matched / per-shard) · 0.081 / 0.120 (d=4) · 0.036 (d=8 2×32) · 0.149 (d=8 4×16) · **0.023 (d=6 with local init)** ⇒ **at d=6, ~60 % of the monolithic store's entire deficit from the bar is ROUTING, not writing**, and the N98 init cuts the routing cost by **2.6×** as a side effect of putting each shard's atoms where its own items are.
  - **Calibration (the laundering control is the same object w23/w24 measured):** monolithic d=6 K=64 **0.8288 ± 0.0186** (w23 0.855 / w24 0.858 ± 0.001); d=4 K=32 **0.8346 ± 0.0151** (w24 0.801); d=8 K=64 **0.9121 ± 0.0029** (w24 0.9067 ± 0.0068); and the w23 *"more atoms make d=6 K=64 worse"* anomaly **reproduces independently** (0.8288 @4096 → **0.8008 ± 0.0037** @8192). Determinism verified (independent re-run of d=6 K=64 sharded seed 0 → **0.8105**, identical to four digits).
  - **Cost side:** routing is **0.63 % / 1.22 % / 2.82 %** of one read at N = 2/4/8 and read time grows only **1.37×** from N=2 to N=8 (one joint Verlet rollout settles all shards simultaneously; `V` is separable). **The sharded write is 4–5× cheaper wall-clock at the same total atom count** (d=6 K=64 end-to-end: monolithic **1900 s** vs sharded **412–492 s**) because `write_loss`'s barrier term is all-pairs `O(K²)` → `O(K²/N)`.
- **Why it is only *partly* a win (mechanism):** the write half is **literally additive** — shards are **separate parameter trees**, so Prop L2's "N independent optimizers" is not approximated here, it is *literal*, and no optimizer state crosses a shard boundary. The read half is not free: on a **learned** store the dynamical R2 score is a poor nearest-well proxy (route accuracy 0.913 scatter init / **0.970** with the N98 init / 0.670 at d=8 N=4 starved), and the gap between R2 and the classical registry **is** the price. ⚠ The global registry is load-bearing, and measured so: 24 items offered round-robin to 4 MVC-0 controllers — **global registry** admits 4/24 with union separation **1.698 (respects `d_safe`)** vs **per-shard registries** admitting 14/24 with union separation **0.208 — 7.4× too close to be told apart** (every shard's own gate satisfied, the union unretrievable). *This is Prop L4's sharp form: the read-side condition is on the **union**, and only a global registry can enforce it — and it is a registry, not an optimizer.*
- **Scope:** one synthetic geometry with **supplied** placement (N46 applies — the writer is given the sites); nothing here says items find their own addresses and **nothing here beats a kNN** (a classical kNN over the registry solves the routing task outright — RG route accuracy 1.000 in every cell — stated up front, not buried); d=8 monolithic is 2 seeds; the budget-adequate d=8 arms and the d=8 K=256 8×32 probe were **not run** (compute, declared); the abstention deadband was never exercised on learned cells, and **the headline used deadband 0 throughout, so no number takes abstention credit**; mid-sweep instrumentation (`RG`, `by_router`, `strict_oracle_route`) was **purely additive** and verified by re-running one cell to four digits.
- **Disposition:** **approved wording (verbatim from the source): *"the write is additive at zero optimizer cost, and the read stays O(1) in depth, because a classical O(N) score suffices to route"* — plus the new half: *at d=6 roughly 60 % of the monolithic store's deficit is routing, not writing.*** ⛔ **Never "capacity multiplies by sharding" as a dynamical claim** (N89/N97 discipline). ⚠ Two live consequences: the two w25 R2 levers now interact — the N98 init narrows the *effective atom placement* while N100's reach condition governs the *width* — **and they must be measured jointly before either becomes a default** (`r2-excursion-reach` Stage A, w26, per Head Addendum-2 decision 4); and every sharded design pays **~N× parameters** to stay budget-adequate (N107).

### N106 — ◐ (scope guard) The d=4 K=32 wall is geometry, confirmed with routing removed  · tier B (HUB-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the 2×2's **control** cell — d=4 K=32 split as 2×16, both at matched total atoms and at per-shard (budget-adequate) atoms, scored with the **classical registry router (RG)**, i.e. **with routing removed entirely** (route accuracy 1.000 by construction), blank-controlled (`lattice-sharded-store` §1/§1.1, P2).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** **RG 0.8932 ± 0.0056 (matched) / 0.8984 ± 0.0028 (per-shard) — both FAIL the 0.90 bar**; the dynamical-router arms are 0.8118 ± 0.0193 / 0.7786 ± 0.0341; monolithic laundering line 0.8346 ± 0.0151 (0.8158 ± 0.0166 at 2× atoms).
- **Why it "failed" (mechanism):** the cell is **`K_addr`-bound** — below the write ceiling, so there is nothing for additivity to add. It is *supposed* to fail (declared as a non-falsifier in the task's dial declaration), and it failing **with routing removed in both arms** is what makes THEOREM-L1's `min(·,·)` reading interpretable rather than a router artifact.
- **Scope / honesty:** ⚠ **the pre-registered band was "≤0.87" and the measured RG values are 0.89–0.90 — closer to the bar than predicted.** Quote it as **"0.89–0.90, does not clear 0.90"**, never as a comfortable failure; **a 5-seed re-check is owed before the band is quoted in a paper.**
- **Disposition:** the scope guard on any *"`K = 32N` unclamped"* reading — **sharding relocates the binding constraint onto geometry and cannot exceed it** (N105 / Prop L2 / CM-23(p)).

### N107 — ◐ (design guard) The w23 atom floor `512·√2^d` is per-STORE, not per-item ⇒ parameter-matched sharding is automatically starved  · tier B (HUB-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** reading the w23 atom-budget rule (`n_atoms = max(32·K, min_atoms_base·√2^d)`) against the sharded arms that were built to be **parameter-matched** to the monolithic control (`lattice-sharded-store` §1.1 / recon 4).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** every `sharded_matched` arm in the wave is **2–8× below the per-store floor** (d=8 4×16: **2048 atoms per shard against a floor of 8192**), and the write loss shows it — **7.3e-3 at N=4 vs 3.7e-5 at N=2**. The 4×16 cell scores **0.6559 ± 0.0143** (R2) / 0.8053 ± 0.0280 (RG).
- **Why it matters (mechanism):** the floor is a **per-store** coverage requirement, so an N-way split at matched *total* parameters gives each shard `1/N` of the coverage it needs. ⇒ **(i)** every matched-arm *win* in N105 is **conservative** (it was won while starved); **(ii)** every matched-arm *collapse* at N ≥ 4 is **not a capacity result** — under the N92 protocol *a stall under an inadequate budget is not a ceiling.* The honest statement of the 4×16 cell is **"the parameter-matched split does not survive past N=2 at d=8"**, not "shard size matters"; the budget-adequate d=8 arms (16 384 / 32 768 atoms) were **not affordable**, so P3b's falsification is **confounded, and reported as confounded**.
- **Disposition:** a design guard with its arithmetic: **any R2/sharding figure must state that additivity costs ~N× parameters unless the floor is re-derived per shard.** The budget-adequate arm (`sharded_per_shard`) *also* passes at d=6 (0.9150 RG), so this is a **cost, not a blocker**.

### N108 — ⛔ Amplitude decay does not reduce an EXACT adversary's per-example distinguishability at any point in an item's life  · tier A (HUB-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture / positioning

- **Tried:** put **retention** and a **per-example (U-LiRA-style) distinguishability** curve on one `τ = leak·t` axis and report where they cross; measure what survives `evict`; run the TTL laundering line. Designed store (`AtomStorePotential(dim=3, capacity=8, α=0.02, s=0.35)`), shipped `Controller` (`d_safe = 1.540`), shipped two-phase read, **no learning anywhere**; 8 targets × 3 seeds = **24 per-example values**, **128 paired IN/OUT worlds** per target, 16 queries/world, **18 amplitude levels**, 11 radii, 4 probe-noise levels; PREREG written **before the harness existed** (`mia-decay-measurement`).
- **Numbers (verbatim, §0/§1/§3):**
  - ⛔ **Against an EXACT adversary decay buys nothing:** white-box (TM-2a, paired) AUC = **1.000 at all 18 amplitude levels** down to the floor. What decays is the **effect size**: the depth gap is **`0.3935·A` to four decimal places at every level** (the pre-registered closed form `1 − e^{−1/2}`) and `d′` falls **1 560 → 79.6**, exactly linear in `A`. **The dial declaration's falsifier FIRED on the AUC metric, exactly as pre-registered (P3).**
  - ⭐ **The store stops answering before it stops leaking (the headline — a finding, and pre-declared as non-falsifying):** at the last amplitude before self-eviction (`A = 0.051`, `τ = 2.976`) **retention = 0.832** while query-MIA is **AUC 0.983 (TPR 0.858 @ FPR 1 %)** and white-box is **1.000**. **The curves never cross**; the gap opens from 0.000 (`τ ≤ 1.2`) to **+0.151** at the floor and to **+0.500 / +1.000** immediately after eviction (paired / allocator-trace).
  - ✅ **Against a resolution-limited adversary the grading is real and the pre-registered law survives:** `A₇₅ = 2.57·σ_obs` measured **0.0780 / 0.2627 / 0.7537** at `σ_obs = 0.03 / 0.1 / 0.3` vs predicted 0.0771 / 0.2570 / 0.7710 (**+1.2 %, +2.2 %, −2.2 %**); the whole `AUC(A)` curve lies on the registered `Φ(0.3935A/1.5σ)`.
  - **The TTL laundering line decides the "physical amplitude vs bookkeeping flag" question, and the answer is CONDITIONAL:** at `A = 0.06`, CLU vs a CLU-with-a-TTL-flag control — exact white-box **1.000 vs 1.000 (separation 0.000 — no differentiator)**; query 0.9895 vs 1.0000 (0.011); `σ_obs = 0.01` 0.946 vs 1.000; `σ_obs = 0.03` 0.709 vs 1.000 (0.291); **`σ_obs = 0.1` 0.559 vs 0.996 (0.437)**; `σ_obs = 0.3` 0.533 vs 0.818.
  - ⭐ **The one differentiator that needs no adversary caveat is RETRIEVAL GEOMETRY:** `R₅₀` (read radius at which retention halves) contracts **1.146 / 1.083 / 0.979 / 0.874 / 0.752** as `A: 1 → 0.5 → 0.2 → 0.1 → 0.06` — a **1.52×** contraction matching the pre-registered saddle prediction at all five points (±0.20) — while a **TTL vector-store's lookup radius is a constant hard step at 0.75–0.77, independent of age.**
- **Why it fails against an exact adversary (mechanism):** the background contributes `exp(−4.4²/2) = 6.3e−5` at `c_i` while the target still contributes `0.3935·A ≥ 0.0197` at the floor ⇒ the separation shrinks but never reaches the (zero) noise floor of a *paired* adversary, so **AUC saturates at 1.000 while `d′` decays.** Against a **natural (history) OUT** adversary — where the background differs between worlds and supplies a real noise floor — the white-box curve **is** graded: 1.000 → **0.791**, saturating at the post-evict allocator-trace level **0.760**.
- **Scope / limitations (declared by the source):** **the STORE only** — no φ, no learned `V`, no payload encoder; **no (ε,δ) claim is made** and the words *certified / unlearning / privacy guarantee* are not used (CM-22 m/n/o). Small store (capacity 8, dim 3, 7 background items, Newtonian, `p₀ ≈ 0`); **`σ_obs` is a modelling choice, not a property of CLU** (a security referee will say a constant we choose makes the story unfalsifiable — its defensible use is *mechanistic* ("the leak signal is `0.3935·A`"), never *protective*); TPR @ FPR 1 % is at the resolution limit of 128 OUT worlds (treat as indicative; the 5 % column and the AUC are well resolved); the paired-placement OUT world is an **idealisation** that hands the adversary a matched background (the right instrument for isolating the amplitude channel; the natural surface is the history condition, reported alongside); amplitudes were **set directly** rather than by ticking (justified — the shipped law is exactly `amps *= exp(−leak)`, verified P9: `[1.0, 0.7047, 0.4966, 0.3499, 0.2466, 0.1738, 0.1225, 0.0863, 0.0608, 0]`, evict at tick 9, reproducing `controller-mvp`'s 0.705).
- **⚠ Two exploratory findings from the same harness, flagged as not-pre-registered:** (1) **the lifetimes dial is NOT payload-independent** — retention at the floor correlates **r = −0.846 with `a_i²`** (and **r = +0.015** with `|c_i|`): at `A = 0.06` retention is 0.999/1.000 for `a = ±0.1429` but **0.663 ± 0.093 for `a = −1.0` and 0.500 ± 0.110 for `a = +1.0`**, because the `q₂(0) = 0` guard makes each site a payload **hill** of height `0.5κa_i²` (up to 0.5) against an address well of depth `A` (0.05 at the floor) — directly visible as `s5` crossing zero between `A = 0.4` and `A = 0.3` and reaching **−0.113** at the floor ⇒ **two items written with the same `leak` have different effective half-lives, and only the USER loses — query MIA is flat in `a_i` (0.983 regardless)**. Filed as **§7-CURRENT defect D3**; needs a **theorist ruling** before the potential is changed (`readout-channel-theory`, w26; Advisor-2's cheap calibration option — user sets half-life, store solves per-item leak, potential untouched — is on the table). (2) `evict` **is not erasure at the data-structure level** — `centers[slot]` and `payloads[slot]` keep the written values verbatim (max err **5.62e−8 / 0.0** over 3 072 evictions); invisible to `V` (the mask multiplies both terms) so **no measured result moves**, but *"the item is gone / the slot is freed"* is false at the data-structure level (defect **D1**, one-line engineer fix, commissioned in `placement-landing`, w26).
- **Disposition:** **both halves of the laundering verdict travel together.** ✅ Safe wording: *"retention and distinguishability are different curves and they separate: at one lifetime the store answers 83 % of queries while an adversary still separates membership at AUC 0.98"* · *"decay contracts the addressing tolerance of an item (`R₅₀` 1.15 → 0.75), which a timestamped row cannot express"* · *"amplitude decay reduces an attacker's advantage in proportion to `A` relative to its measurement resolution `σ`; against an exact-arithmetic attacker it does not, and neither does any deterministic bookkeeping alternative."* ⛔ **Forbidden:** any claim that decay reduces distinguishability **per se**, and any claim that eviction removes the item (under the shipped placement it does not — see the N99 update).
- > **⭐ WAVE-26 — D3 IS RULED, D1 IS RESOLVED, AND THE LEAK NUMBER BECOMES A CURVE.** **(a) D3 ruled (`readout-channel-theory` §3 → N119).** The payload-dependent lifetime is **not a bug in the potential — it is a corner of a TRILEMMA** (value fidelity · amplitude-independent hold · amplitude-independent latency: **pick two**). ⛔ **Both fixes this entry floated are REFUTED:** `payloads*amps` kills the value criterion at `A = 1 − tol/|a_i|` (measured death amplitudes 0.90/0.80/0.70/0.30 vs the formula's 0.900/0.860/0.767/0.300 — exact) and **inverts** the dependence; launching at `q₂ = S(q_addr)` **breaks the anti-decoration guard** (the trivial substitute passes **0.672** of queries with **no dynamics at all**, amplitude-independently). Advisor-2's calibration option (c) is **honest-but-thin** (only **4/8** codewords ever halve; for those, `A* ∈ [0.070, 0.077]` against a floor of 0.05 ⇒ the retention *shape* is a near-step). ✅ **Recommended: option (d) gated stiffness**, measured **1.000 payload-independent retention at every amplitude to the floor** at `g₀ = amp_floor` — at the price that the on-site curve becomes a **step** (the TTL shape); the *graded* configuration needs `g₀ ≪ amp_floor` **plus a longer read as the item decays**, which ⭐ **is the compute-adaptive-read dial, not a defect.** ⚠ **`R₅₀` — the differentiator this entry leads with — was NOT measured under the gate** and **must be re-measured before the claim is re-used** (`deletion-waitlist-stiffness`, C1W27, behind a flag, defaults OFF). ⚠ **And every retention magnitude in this entry is placement-dependent:** on a max-radius ring the same store gives **0.500 at A = 0.06** where the controller-placed disk gives **0.886** ⇒ **state the `|c|` distribution with any retention number.** **(b) D1 RESOLVED (`placement-landing`):** `evict` now scrubs `centers`/`payloads` as well as `active`/`amps`; verified neutral two ways (`max |ΔV| = 0.0`; the whole relocate arm reproduces this entry's published numbers to 4–5 dp) ⇒ *"the item is gone"* is now true at the data-structure level. **(c) The allocator-trace number is a CURVE** — `AUC(z_hole)` **0.6715 / 0.9165 / 0.9961 / 0.99985** at 2/4/6/8 offers ⇒ ⛔ **never quote 0.99985 without its load** (see the N99 w26 block).
