### N109 — ⭐ (POSITIVE) The learned-capacity wall at d=4 is a property of the READ-OUT CODE, and it moves when the code moves  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the two-arm read-out excursion experiment the w25 review commissioned under **five binding fairness conditions** — **(a)** a **multi-channel payload code** (`payload_code="grid"`, K codewords on the Δ-spaced lattice in `R^m`, **Δ = 2/(K−1)** held at the 1-channel value at every m, so the item still carries `log₂K` bits at the same per-axis noise) and **(b)** an **anisotropic continuation ("annealed") read** (widen **only** the payload channel, `κ: κ₀ → 1` over L stages, `address_steps`/`read_steps` split so the step count is unchanged). d=4, 8192 atoms, global write, `pscale = 1`, **payload read-noise ON** (`σ_launch = 0.05`), nearest-codeword **decode** scoring, value-blank on every PASS (`r2-excursion-reach` §3–§7).
- **Numbers (verbatim, `r2-excursion-reach` §3/§4/§5/§6):**
  - **Arm (b), the w23 firm wall (d=4 K=32, flat at 0.825–0.840 over a 16× atom sweep), 3 seeds:** base **0.8210 ± 0.0028** → `κ₀=3, L=4` **0.9997 ± 0.0005**; Δ = **+0.1787**, SE of the difference **0.0016 ⇒ ~110 SE**; under noise **0.8190 ± 0.0033 → 0.9980 ± 0.0000** at σ_obs = 0.010, where the **designed** reference still passes (0.9990). Broad optimum κ₀ ∈ [2, 5], L ∈ {4, 8} and two schedule shapes agreeing to ≤ 0.01. **Zero extra parameters, zero extra latent dimensions, zero extra Verlet steps, no change to the stored format.** ⚠ **Convention note (Hub, w26 review):** this report quotes **population** sd; the Hub's §10 entry quotes the **sample** sd of the same data (0.8210 ± 0.0034 → 0.9997 ± 0.0006, ~20 % larger). **Same numbers, two conventions — do not "correct" either table.**
  - **Arm (a), K=32, 3 seeds, decode:** m=1 **0.8047 ± 0.0060** → **m=4 1.0000** (σ=0 and σ=0.005) and **0.9980 ± 0.0008** at σ_obs = 0.010, where m=1 sits at 0.8034 ± 0.0064. Max ‖a‖ falls **1.0000 → 0.0912** at identical code Δ = 0.0645.
  - **The wall table (the result):** at σ_obs = **0** designed **128** / shipped **16** / arm (b) **32** / arm (a) **128** (0.9634 ± 0.0159, 2 seeds); at **0.005** — 64 / 16 / 32 / **64** (0.9950 ± 0.0008, 3 seeds); at **0.010** — 32 / 16 / **32** (0.9980 ± 0.0000) / **32** (0.9980 ± 0.0008). ⇒ **the learned/designed prefactor tax at d = 4 goes from 1/8 (w23: 16 vs 128) to 1/1 at every noise level measured.**
  - **The three controls that make it a mechanism, not a knob:** **`readonly`** (anneal the value phase only) reproduces the baseline **to four decimals** (0.8210 vs 0.8210 at K=32; 0.9368 vs 0.9368 at K=16) ⇒ **the entire gain is address acquisition**; **`static`** (widen and never sharpen) reaches **basin 0.9993** and reads the **wrong value** (strict 0.6250 ± 0.0255 at σ=0 tol; **0.2389 ± 0.0150** under decode) ⇒ *"just use wider wells" is a different, failing result and the continuation is load-bearing*; **`spectator`** (m=4 latent dims and **+43 % parameters**, code left at excursion 1.0) buys **+0.034** where the code buys **+0.195**.
  - **The isotropic blur is REFUTED and the refutation is the mechanism:** K=32 **0.8242 → 0.2383** at `s_extra = 0.30`, and the **designed** register collapses on the identical schedule (**1.000 → 0.3438**) ⇒ geometric, not optimisational. Reach wants `s ≳ |a|max/κ ≈ 0.33`, packing wants `s ≲ sep/2.4 = 0.30`: **the two windows do not overlap** — and they live on **different axes**, which is why widening only the payload channel dissolves the conflict instead of trading it off.
  - **Laundering line intact:** `K_designed(4) = 128` at m = 1, 2 **and** 4 (1.0000 / 1.0000 / 0.9968 / 0.8884 at K=32/64/128/256); the designed arm also **defines the format's noise ceiling** (it fails K=128 at σ_obs = 0.005 and K=64 at 0.010), and **no learned PASS is claimed above it**. The multi-channel code is very slightly *worse* for the designed arm under noise (0.9946 vs 0.9980) — the lattice kissing-number cost, pre-registered.
  - **Budget adequacy (N92 protocol) at arm (b)'s first-fail cell (K=64):** 8192 → 16 384 atoms gives 0.8506 → 0.8027 (flat-to-slightly-worse) ⇒ **the arm-(b) wall at 32 is real, not starvation.**
- **Why it works (mechanism):** the read launches on the payload-zero manifold, so a well whose payload sits at ‖a‖ = 1 is *invisible while the address is being chosen* — which is why **`basin ≡ strict` at every failing cell in w23, w25 and w26**. Shorten the reach (arm a) or lend the payload channel a temporary width during the address phase (arm b) and the same landscape becomes addressable.
- **Scope / limits (declared by the source):** ⚠ **d = 4 ONLY — d = 6 and d = 8 were NOT RUN** (compute; declared in the PREREG's priority order), so **no exponent is re-measured** and `K_designed = 4·2^d` is untouched (128 = 4·2⁴, measured). K=128 is **2 seeds**; K=256 not run ⇒ arm (a)'s learned wall is `≥128`. Arm (b)'s K=64 FAIL rests on **1 seed + the 2× atom re-check**. Arm (a) × arm (b) **in combination: NOT RUN**. The σ_obs grid is a **design choice, not a measurement** — every claim is anchored to the designed arm at the same σ_obs. **`w21's ~1.3-vs-2 bits-per-param is STALE** (measured under this ceiling); items-per-parameter at the same cell rises ×2.00 (arm b, zero extra params) / ×2.80–5.60 (arm a) — **nobody has re-derived bits-per-param.**
- **Disposition:** ⭐⭐ **R2 is UNCLAMPED at d = 4, with a named mechanism and payload noise ON.** ⛔ **Never write "R2 is unclamped" without "at d = 4; d=6/d=8 not run."** ⛔ The `pscale ≠ 1` never-quote **stands and is reinforced** (see N110). The standing R2 wording ("learned pays a widening tax vs designed; 4× prefactor gap") is now **scoped to the shipped read-out code** and must say so. Successor: the **d-sweep at m=4** + the **arm(a)×arm(b) cell** (`r2-d-sweep-close`, C1W27).

### N110 — ⛔ (methodology) The absolute-tolerance value criterion is VACUOUS for any read-out code whose excursion is below `payload_tol`  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture (broad guard)

- **Tried:** scoring the multi-channel arm with the shipped `pass_metric="tol"` (value-ok ⟺ `‖read − a_i‖ < payload_tol = 0.1`) versus a nearest-codeword **decode** metric, with the standard value-blank control (`r2-excursion-reach` §4/§7).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** at **m=4, K=32** the whole codebook lives inside **‖a‖ ≤ 0.0912 < 0.1**, and a **blank landscape scores `strict = 1.0000`** on `tol`. The same blank under **decode** scores **0.0312 = 1/32, exactly chance** (K=64: **0.0156 = 1/64**; K=128: **0.0063**, chance 0.0078). Blank on `tol` at K=32/64/128, m=4: **1.0000 / 0.9990 / 0.9341**. (`evaluate_arm_cell`'s `trivial_ceiling` guard detects this and refuses the cell — it is why the guard exists.)
- **Companion measurement — the hole the w25 `pscale` probe fell through:** halving the codebook *and* the tolerance together (w25's manipulation) reproduces its free lunch at zero noise (**0.9995**) and then **dies as read noise rises: 0.9985 → 0.8936 ± 0.0049 (σ_obs = 0.010) → 0.5894 (0.020)**, because it halves Δ. The constant-Δ multi-channel code, at the same cells, gives **1.0000 → 0.9980 → 0.8099**. **At σ_obs = 0.010 the difference is decisive: m=4 PASSES at 0.998, `pscale` FAILS at 0.894.**
- **Why it fails (mechanism):** an *absolute* error tolerance is structurally blind to codebook spacing, so it neither rewards nor punishes a change of excursion; any code compressed below the tolerance is scored correct for free.
- **Scope:** the shipped `pass_metric="tol"` at **m > 1** or after any excursion/codebook manipulation; harmless at m=1 with the shipped excursion (0.0645 ≫ … no, Δ < tol there too — the guard is that at m=1 the *excursion* spans ±1, so a blank is not inside tol).
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **No `tol`-metric number at m > 1 may EVER be quoted** (every arm-(a) number in N109 is the decode metric). ⭐ **C1W27 changes the shipped default to `decode`** (Head ruling 2026-07-29, queue item 3: *"a correctness fix, not a lever promotion"*) — the engineer left it alone in w26 under B1.4 discipline and said so. Any future excursion or codebook study is scored by **decoding**, never by an absolute tolerance.

### N111 — ⛔ The localized atom init and `atom_init_width` are SUBSTITUTES; at the shipped width the localized init is a NULL (and N98 does not cross-replicate)  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the init × width **2×2 factorial with the interaction term** that the Head made a precondition for promoting either lever (Addendum-2 decision 4) — d=6, K=64, monolithic, 3 seeds, 4096 atoms, value-blank ✅ on all 12 cells (`r2-excursion-reach` §1).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** strict — `local=False, width 0.30` (shipped) **0.8551 ± 0.0106** · `local=True, 0.30` **0.8620 ± 0.0114** · `local=False, 0.15` **0.1429 ± 0.0424** · `local=True, 0.15` **0.6087 ± 0.0046**. Main effects: `atom_init_local` **+0.2363**, width 0.30→0.15 **−0.4827**. **Simple effect of `local` at the shipped width: +0.0068 (± ~0.016) — a NULL.** At width 0.15: **+0.4658**. ⭐ **INTERACTION +0.4590, SE 0.0321 ⇒ 14.3 SE.**
- **Why (mechanism):** both levers attack *"atoms in the wrong place"*, and `atom_init_width = 0.30` **already puts them there**, so there is nothing left for the localized init to buy. The residual **0.246** that localization does not recover at width 0.15 is the part of the narrow-width collapse an address-side lever cannot touch (N46: the localized init is address-only by construction).
- **⛔ The cross-harness non-replication:** N98's **+0.051** for the monolithic d=6 K=64 cell **does not reproduce here** (+0.0068 ± 0.016, 3 seeds, value-blank-gated). The harnesses differ (`exp_sharded_store`'s allocator/partition/router vs the designed-mechanism harness), so this is a **non-replication, not a refutation of N98's own number** — but **the localized init cannot be quoted as a general gain.**
- **Scope / limits:** d=6 K=64 monolithic, one budget. ⚠ **Confound not resolved:** the localization radius is `mult × atom_init_width`, so the width-0.15 arms localize into a ball of radius 0.30 and the width-0.30 arms into 0.60 — the interaction is *"localization scaled with the width"*, not *"localization at fixed radius"*; the clean control (`mult = 4.0` at width 0.15) is **NOT RUN** (compute, declared).
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **The factorial does NOT license promoting `atom_init_local`** (B1.4 respected; **no default changed** — it stays `False`). Its only measured value is as a **repair for a width that is itself wrong**. Advisor-2's *"substantially one effect"* prior wins the **interaction** call (≥ +0.15 ✓) and loses its **rescue** clause (0.6087 < 0.85); the engineer's own registered additivity prediction (0.00 ± 0.05, P = 0.70) is **REFUTED**. ⚠ **Attach the cross-harness caveat wherever N98 is cited.**

### N113 — ⛔ The matched-BYTES contested-win attempt FAILED as pre-registered — the 5th consecutive laundering  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture / positioning

- **Tried:** Addendum-2 §B2's **Candidate 1** — the forgetting-vs-**BYTES** Pareto frontier on Split-MNIST Class-IL, 6 budget points spanning **50×** (6 280 · 19 625 · 39 250 · 78 500 · 157 000 · 314 000 floats), 3 seeds, against tuned **ER / DER++ (new) / GDumb / iCaRL** at every point, with byte accounting **pinned and published before any run** and **the launder run at matched BYTES too** (`matched-bytes-frontier` §1–§2).
- **Numbers (verbatim, mean ± sd over 3 seeds):**
  - **Byte accounting (pinned, deliberately conservative against CLU):** CLU store **41 floats/item** (164 B) · kNN-φ ring buffer **34** · ER/GDumb/iCaRL **785** · DER++ **795** ⇒ **19.1× more items for CLU at the same bytes**, and **the launder gets 1.21× more keys than CLU gets wells** at every point (184/153 … 9 235/6 085).
  - **⭐ Against the replay field:** CLU **higher ACC at 6/6** budgets — **0.903 ± 0.003 vs iCaRL 0.885 ± 0.002** at 1.2 MiB, +0.064 over iCaRL at the smallest, +0.05–0.39 over ER/DER++/GDumb — and **lower forgetting at 5/6** (all but 24.5 KiB, where GDumb's near-degenerate 0.128 at LA 0.549 wins). **This reverses w25's matched-ITEMS picture** (CLU sat 0.153 below iCaRL there).
  - ⛔ **Against the launder:** the matched-bytes ring buffer has **lower forgetting at 6/6** (Δ = **+0.032, +0.042, +0.027, +0.039, +0.018, +0.005**) and **higher ACC at 6/6**. The gap narrows monotonically with budget and **never closes**.
  - **Under the strict pre-registered rule** (strictly lowest **and** ≥ 1 sd separated **and** LA within 0.10 of the best), the dominance-vs-replay region is **one point: B = 314 000 floats** (Δ vs iCaRL −0.019, LA 0.942 vs best 0.982). ⚠ Knife-edge, disclosed: 76.7 KiB is sd-separated and fails the LA clause **by 0.007**; 153/307/613 KiB are lower and pass LA but are not sd-separated (GDumb's sd 0.056/0.033/0.009).
- **Why it fails:** the store approximates a lookup on this metric, so a trivial kNN over the same φ at the same bytes is not structurally handicapped. Three of the six pre-registrations failed **in the same direction**: the store's advantage over replay is a **large-budget** effect, not a small-budget one (P1d, P5, P3b).
- **Scope / limits:** one dataset (Split-MNIST), the PRIMARY leakage-free φ arm only (`generic_frozen` not run — a declared compute saving; it would shift CLU **and both launders** together), 3 seeds, decay OFF (the frontier item never ticks).
- **⚠ Corrections to w25's published table that travel with any quotation of it:** **(i) "24.5× fewer floats" → 19.1×** (the w25 figure used the landscape-only 32-float count; the pinned accounting is 41). **(ii) iCaRL ran up to 2.5× OVER its item budget** at small budgets (`m_per = max(1, budget // n_classes)` kept one exemplar per class ⇒ 10 items on a budget of 4); fixed and regression-tested. **(iii) `memory_floats` under-counted every method.** **(iv)** w25's *"CLU 0.169 vs ER 0.264"* stands but is a matched-**items** statement and must never be quoted as a matched-bytes one.
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **The pre-registered falsifier FIRED ⇒ Candidate 1 files as SUPPLEMENTARY, not primary** (Head standing ruling: win-by-construction is supplementary only). ✅ **What is real and quotable, with the launder sentence in the same breath:** *"at matched bytes the designed store beats the entire replay field on ACC at 6/6 budgets and on forgetting at 5/6 — and a trivial kNN over the same features at the same bytes still beats it on both."* ⚠ The replay-field dominance is **partly by construction** (replay stores 785 floats/item by definition).

### N114 — ⭐⛔ THE SAME-KEYS LAUNDER: deleting the settle IMPROVES the store  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture / positioning

- **Tried:** the second laundering arm of the byte frontier — **kNN "same keys"**: plain arg-min over the store's **own admitted wells**, i.e. the damped-Verlet settle deleted and **nothing else changed** (same φ, same admission policy, same eviction, same keys, same bytes: 41 floats/well). 6 byte budgets × 3 seeds (`matched-bytes-frontier` §2.4).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** forgetting — same-keys **0.179 / 0.132 / 0.101 / 0.100 / 0.065 / 0.044** vs CLU **0.193 / 0.149 / 0.113 / 0.108 / 0.076 / 0.049** ⇒ **lower at 6/6, mean Δ 0.011**. ACC — same-keys **0.698 / 0.782 / 0.827 / 0.846 / 0.888 / 0.908** vs CLU **0.673 / 0.764 / 0.815 / 0.837 / 0.878 / 0.903** ⇒ **higher at 6/6, mean Δ 0.013**. ⇒ **on Split-MNIST Class-IL the physics costs ≈ 1 pp on both axes.** (Corroboration at a different φ: `cl-encoder` §7 measures the same-keys launder at 0.325 vs the ring buffer's 0.350 on Split-CIFAR-10 — the same ordering.)
- **Why it matters (and why this is the sharpest form of the negative):** every previous laundering result could be answered with *"the baseline has a different memory"*. This one cannot: **the only difference is the settle.** The store's admission, placement, eviction and address space are all still doing their work; running the dynamics on top of them is a **measured net negative** on clean classification.
- **Scope / limits:** one dataset, one task family (**clean-query classification**, where the query is a *different image*, not a corrupted copy of a stored one), 3 seeds, 6 budgets. ⭐ **The contrast that scopes it is the surviving lead:** in the one regime with **corrupted queries and no constructible oracle** (N103) the settle **ties** the matched-compute floor rather than losing. *"The settle costs you when the query is clean and pays when it is ambiguous"* is the honest, and currently best-evidenced, form.
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **No performance sentence about the CL entry may omit this control.** ⭐ The program's genuine-win bar now points at exactly one question: **is there any read for which the settle beats arg-min over the same wells?** Six budget points × 3 seeds say **no** on this benchmark. Registered here so the paper's appendix carries it in the author's own words rather than a referee's.

### N115 — ◐ The CL store's binding constraint switches from BUDGET to SPACING GATE at ~314 000 floats — the packing law inside a benchmark  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** reporting saturation as a **result** rather than as a failure: at each of the 6 byte budgets, how many wells the store was allowed, how many it actually held at end-of-stream, the per-task admitted fraction, and whether the capacity alarm (`refused_full`) ever fired (`matched-bytes-frontier` §3, pre-registered as P3).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** budget wells → live at end — **153 → 153 · 478 → 478 · 957 → 957 · 1 914 → 1 914 · 3 829 → 3 829 · 7 658 → 6 085 ± 66** (per-seed 6 027 / 6 177 / 6 051), **fill 0.795**. Admitted fraction per task **stable at 0.57–0.62** from 39 250 floats upward; **`refused_full = 0` at 18/18 runs** ⇒ every refusal is a **spacing** refusal. Geometry across a 50× budget range: median-NN address spacing 4.409 → 3.107, `s` 0.870 → 0.622 (`s_policy="refit"`), σ_q 4.225 → 2.839, and the **corrected packing slack essentially constant at 0.337–0.353** (⛔ *never the retracted 1.08*) — the store runs ~3× **past** the packing bound at every budget.
- **Why (mechanism):** offering a 20 %-larger store does not buy 20 % more items, because the **address space**, not the allowance, runs out. Crowding is intrinsic to a *classification* stream (the query is a different image, not a corrupted copy).
- **⚠ Registered prediction P3(b) FALSIFIED:** forgetting was predicted to flatten above 157 000 floats (< 0.02 change) and instead fell **0.076 → 0.049 (−0.027)**. Saturating the **item count** did not saturate the **forgetting** — what keeps improving is class coverage per well, not well count.
- **Scope:** measured at **one** point (the top budget is the only saturated one), so this is a saturation **point**, not a saturation **law**; extending the grid 2×/4× upward (~20/40 min per seed) would turn it into one — and the source's own prediction is that **the launder gap should re-open above P6** if the store's geometry is the limiter.
- **Disposition:** ⭐ Quotable as *"the capacity law shows up inside a benchmark: the store stops taking items because the address space is full, not because the byte budget is"* — with the fill fraction, the admitted band, and `refused_full = 0` in the same sentence.

### N117 — ◐ The retry threshold τ is inert exactly when the low-confidence pool exceeds the compute budget (and it is NOT a φ-space property)  · tier B (HUB-PROPOSED, curator concurs ✧) · memory-architecture / all

- **Tried:** the carried w25 item — multi-seed the single-seed observation that *"τ is not the binding element of the gate in φ-space"*, which contradicted w24's measurement that τ = 1.0 over-retries and costs accuracy. 3 seeds × 2 store snapshots, both corruption levels, **configuration-only change** (`retry_mask_levels: [0.5]`), with an A4 cross-check that the p=0.5 cell is bit-identical between arms (`carried-remeasurements` §1).
- **Numbers (verbatim):**
  - **p = 0.8 (the hardest level, the one the shipped code sweeps): identity CONFIRMED 6/6.** All four thresholds {0.99, 0.999, 0.9999, 1.0} give **bit-identical** ladders at every k: **`max|Δacc| = 0.000e+00`, `max|Δcompute| = 0.000e+00`** (asserted with `==` on floats, not a tolerance); compute@8 = 1.8000/1.8040; eligible pool **≥ 160 of ~200** = the full 8·step_n budget.
  - **p = 0.5, same stores, same code: identity FALSE 6/6.** acc@k=8 end-of-stream **0.9950 / 0.9900 / 0.9950** (τ=0.99) vs **0.4171 / 0.4600 / 0.4650** (τ=1.0); **Δ = −0.5460 ± 0.0226** end-of-stream, **−0.4846 ± 0.0640** over all six cells (range [−0.578, −0.405]); compute 1.121–1.300× → 1.800×. Eligible pool **24 / 28 / 31** (end-of-stream) and **47 / 52 / 60** (mid-stream) of ~200.
- **The rule (exact arithmetic, not a fit):** reads retried by round k = `min(k·step_n, #{cos₀ < τ})` because an unretried read's cosine is frozen at its first-pass value ⇒ **τ is load-bearing iff `#{cos₀ < τ} < k·step_n`.** When the pool saturates the budget, every τ selects the same reads in the same order; when it does not, τ = 1.0 keeps spending on **high-confidence, mostly-correct** reads and the boost corrupts them.
- **⛔ The falsified hypothesis (the analyst's own, pre-registered):** T5 — *"the identity is a φ-space property; pixel space differs"*. **FALSIFIED**: both behaviours occur **inside φ-space, in the same store, ~3 minutes apart**, distinguished only by query difficulty.
- **Scope:** one dataset (Split-MNIST), one φ (task1_only PCA-32), one store (200 items); the crossover corruption level (between p = 0.5 and p = 0.8) is **not swept**. The laundering control is unchanged by the remeasurement: the gate **ties** the matched-compute kNN-in-φ floor at p = 0.8 (0.8631 vs 0.8698, −0.007 ± 0.010) and at p = 0.5.
- **Disposition:** **This retracts neither w24 nor w25 — it scopes both** (see the **N103 w26 block**). ⛔ **Do not keep the "φ-space vs pixel-space" framing.** ⛔ Any statement about the threshold **names the corruption level**. Two cheap code items follow (neither moves a published number): the harness saves `mean_confidence` but **not** `#{cos₀ < τ}` — the quantity that decides the whole question — and the τ-sweep only ever runs on the **last** corruption level, which is why the contradiction survived a wave.

### N118 — ⛔ (positioning) Blelloch–Golovin FOCS'07 own the placement algorithm outright; our Theorems 1–2 are instantiations  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · positioning

- **Tried:** the pre-drafting citation gate — verify the load-bearing SHI/deletion citations **from primaries**, pin the unlearning arena's per-deletion cost model, test whether *"deletion cost at matched utility"* is already occupied, and re-confirm the "certified" ban (`deletion-prior-art`, read-only, no git footprint).

- **Corrections this forces:** ⚠ **Hartline et al. (Algorithmica 2005) Thm 1 requires a *reversible* structure** — our **placement** layer is reversible, our **amplitude** layer is not (decay and `born` are monotone in time) ⇒ cite Hartline for the SHI ⇄ canonical **definitional equivalence only**, never inside a proof. ⚠ **Naor–Teague's numbered definitions could NOT be obtained from the primary** (ePrint 403/CAPTCHA, ACM paywalled) ⇒ cite the paper for the *notions*, never a definition number. ⚠ Micciancio (STOC'97) is a **contrast, not a precedent** (randomisation route, not canonicalisation).
- **New vocabulary bans (alongside the standing "certified"/"unlearning"):** ⛔ **"deletion-compliant"** — a EUROCRYPT'20 term of art (Garg, Goldwasser & Vasudevan, Def. 2.2) whose **dependency clause we fail** (the encoder φ saw the item); ⛔ **"our fix-up cascade"** as a possessive — **it is theirs**; ⛔ **"we prove placement is order-independent" as a novel theorem** ("follows from"); ⛔ **"the first order-independent/uniquely-represented store"**; ⛔ unqualified **"exact deletion"** (distributional, model-level in this literature — SISA Def. III.1).
- **Candidate 2 is occupied in pieces:** **Ginart et al. NeurIPS'19 Def. A.5** (α-deletion efficiency) owns the cost side; **Sekhari et al. NeurIPS'21 Def. 3** (deletion capacity at fixed excess risk 0.01) owns the at-matched-utility side; **MUSE** criteria 4+5+6, **CURE4Rec**'s four dimensions and **SISA §VII**'s shards-vs-accuracy curve cover the benchmark/practice side. ⛔ **Do not coin a benchmark** — adopt the vocabulary, with the flat-datastore row-delete as the mandatory trivial substitute.

### N119 — ⛔⭐ THE TRILEMMA (value fidelity · amplitude-independent hold · amplitude-independent latency — pick two), and both proposed D3 fixes are REFUTED  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture / positioning

- **Tried:** the theorist ruling the w25 review demanded **before any potential change** — why effective lifetime correlates `r = −0.846` with `a_i²` (N108 D3), and which of four candidate fixes is admissible (`readout-channel-theory` §3, shipped read, 3 seeds, theorist's toy stores).
- **The ruling (proved, then measured):** any potential that returns the right value at the site necessarily puts a **hill of height `0.5·κ_eff·a_i²`** at the launch point, of address stiffness `κ_eff a_i²/s²`, against a well of stiffness `A_i/s²`. In the shipped store `κ_eff` is **constant while `A_i` decays**, so `κa_i²/A_i` diverges and the site becomes a net address **maximum**. ⇒ **the payload-dependent lifetime is not a bug in the potential — it is the corner of the trilemma the shipped store chose.**
  > **THE TRILEMMA.** With a quadratic payload channel, the `q₂(0) = 0` guard and a **fixed** read budget you cannot have all three of **(i) exact value fidelity**, **(ii) amplitude-independent address hold**, **(iii) amplitude-independent read latency**. (i) ⇒ the launch point is a hill of height `0.5κ_eff a_i²`; (ii) then requires `κ_eff ∝ A_i`; but the payload settling time is `τ_y = η/κ_eff ∝ 1/A_i`, violating (iii). ∎
- **The four options, ruled (verbatim numbers):** **(a) `payloads * amps` — ⛔ REFUTED, strictly worse than the defect it fixes:** the read returns `A·a_i`, so the value criterion dies at `A = 1 − tol/|a_i|`; measured death amplitudes **0.90 / 0.80 / 0.70 / 0.30** for |a| = 1 / 0.714 / 0.429 / 0.143 vs the formula's 0.900 / 0.860 / 0.767 / 0.300 — **exact** — everything is dead by A = 0.3 and the payload dependence **inverts** (small-|a| items outlive large ones by **11×** in τ). **(b) launch at `q₂ = S(q_addr)` — ⛔ REFUTED, it breaks the anti-decoration guard:** the **trivial substitute** (return `S` at the launch point, run **no dynamics at all**) already passes the shipped value criterion on **0.672 of queries** (per-item 0.44–1.00, median err 0.057) and is **amplitude-independent** (0.672 at A = 1.0, 0.5 **and** 0.06) ⇒ the value channel would stop responding to decay altogether. **(c) solve `leak` per item for a target half-life — ◐ calibration, not physics:** retention halves before the floor for only **4 of 8** codewords (the other four sit at 0.688–1.000 at the floor), and for the solvable four `A* ∈ [0.070, 0.077]` against a floor of 0.05 ⇒ **the half-life lives in the last 8 % of the amplitude range** and the retention *shape* is a near-step for every item. **(d) gated-stiffness payload channel — ✅ RECOMMENDED, with the trilemma's price stated:** at `g₀ = amp_floor = 0.05`, retention **1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000** across A = 1.0 → 0.051, **payload-independent** (value err 0.029 at the floor) — but the on-site retention curve becomes a **step**, i.e. the TTL shape; at `g₀ = 0.005` retention stays **graded** (1.000/1.000/0.750/0.643/0.508) and payload-independent **only if the read gets longer as the item decays** (4× read steps ⇒ 1.000/0.995/0.763). ⭐ **That is not a defect for this program — it is the compute-adaptive-read dial**: *"a faded memory costs more integration steps to read"* is a physical statement a timestamped row cannot make.
- **⚠ A self-refutation on record:** the theorist's **first** implementation floored the normaliser too (`ā = A·a/(g₀+A)`), which destroys the value at small A and measured **worse than baseline — refuting his own P2.7**; the corrected version (un-floored normaliser, floored stiffness) is the one above.
- **Scope / limits:** option (d) is a **theorist's toy** (`GatedStore2`), not shipped code — one 8-item store, no controller, no eviction, no φ; **`R₅₀` — the differentiator N108 leads with — was NOT measured under the gate.** The Q2 store is a **ring** (all sites at the same |c|), a worst case for reach: on a max-radius ring the same store gives **0.500 at A = 0.06** where `mia-decay`'s controller-placed disk gives 0.886 ⇒ ⚠ **every quoted retention magnitude needs its `|c|` distribution stated.**
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **The engineer must not implement (a) or (b).** Option (d) is commissioned **behind a flag, defaults OFF**, with `g₀` a knob and the mia harness re-run **including `R₅₀`** (`deletion-waitlist-stiffness`, C1W27). ⭐ **Register the trilemma as a standing result** and name the third corner as the **compute-adaptive-read dial**.

### N120 — ⭐ The reach bound is SUPERSEDED by a saddle criterion — verified 31/32 on the trained shipped `V` with zero free parameters  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** one rigorous pass over the read-out channel — derive the reach constant κ, decide which of three candidate mechanisms binds, and test the resulting criterion on **the trained shipped potential** rather than an idealisation (`readout-channel-theory` §1–§2; the learned cell reproduces `r2-geometry-revival`'s `mech_reach` to 4 dp — `w_atom` 0.3013 vs 0.30129, strict 0.9473 vs 0.947266).
- **The result (the object, verbatim):** every stationary point lies on the ray through `z_i = (c_i, a_i)`, at distance `R` from `z_i` solving **`(D·R/s²)·exp(−R²/2s²) = 2α·(L − R)`, `L ≡ |z_i| = √(|c_i|² + a_i²)`** — so with `v = R/s`, `A = L/s`, `β = D/(2αs²)`: for `β ≤ e^{3/2}/2 = 2.2408` **no spurious minimum can ever exist**; for `A > κ_stat(β)` there are three roots and the middle one is a **saddle**. ⇒ **(U) REACH CRITERION: the query is captured by item `i` iff `L/s < κ_stat(β)` or `|a_i| < R₂`.**
- **Numbers (verbatim):** **shipped integrator, 7 variants:** measured/predicted capture threshold ratio **1.013 ± 0.025 (2.4 % rel. sd)**; the PREREG's closed form `Ψ` is systematically **1.357 ± 0.064 too tight** and `κ_stat·s` **0.871 ± 0.036 too loose**; the transition is a **saddle-node bifurcation** (`both` goes 1.000 → 0.000 in one 0.1 grid step at every variant) and **100 %** of failures collapse to the origin. **Trained shipped `V`, zero free parameters:** (U) classifies **15/16** at width 0.30 and **16/16** at width 0.15 ⇒ **31/32**; the unpinned **flow test** scores 16/16 and 15/16 (radial-profile fits R² ≥ 0.9938 at all 32 sites). **Which mechanism binds:** spurious-minimum-on-the-payload-ray fires **0/32 items at both widths**; the payload-descent time budget is slack by **≥ 10×**; the **address-hold** criterion is the binding one ⇒ **the reach failure is an ADDRESS failure, which is why `basin ≡ strict` at every failing cell.**
- **⭐ The quotable no-go — reach is logarithmically un-buyable:** every closed form for the ceiling is a **square root of a logarithm** (`κ_stat ≈ √(2 ln β)`; `κ_R = √(2 ln(D/(2α|c|s)) − 1)`), measured `κ_stat` = **3.33 / 4.08 / 4.67 / 6.06** at β = 10 / 10² / 10³ / 10⁶ ⇒ raising κ **4 → 5 needs β ×55** (D 0.69 → 37.9 at s = 0.3) and **4 → 6 needs ×9200**. The only levers with leverage are `s`, `|a|max`, `α` and `|c|`, and all four enter algebraically. Shipped d=4 operating point: `a_U = 1.06` against `|a|max = 1.0` — **a 6 % margin**, which is why every one-flag intervention moves it.
- **⛔ What this supersedes:** **(1) w25's `s ≳ |a|max/κ`, κ = O(3)** (N100's mechanism line and `r2-geometry-revival` §4/§8) — the criterion is a **saddle condition on `L`, not a threshold on `|a|/s`**; **κ ≈ 3 wording is retired.** **(2) w25 §5's conjecture** that `sep/w` correlates because numerator and denominator both drift with d — **replaced, not confirmed**: the denominator is the width the *write chooses* (a function of d alone, ±3 % within a d), and **`sep` ALONE separates 11/11 Stage-0 cells** (min PASS **0.849**, max FAIL **0.795**) where `sep/w` separates only d ≥ 4 ⇒ **the ratio is a reparameterisation, not a cause**; forcing `sep/w = 4.90` destroys retrieval because it does so by *shrinking `s`* (a_U 1.06 → 0.63, and D falls with it, 0.91 → 0.46), the **opposite** sign to the ratio's implication (predicted strict 0.625 vs measured 0.5859). *(POST-HOC on existing data.)*
- **⚠ Two knobs are now load-bearing, and one new fact about the write:** `learned_confine = 0.05` and the ball radius `R = 1.0` enter the ceiling through **`2α|c_i|`** ⇒ **reach parameters, not free knobs** (halving α moves the threshold +9.1 %; moving a site from |c| = 0.9 to 0.3 moves it +9.5 %). And `atom_init_width` moves the ceiling through **two** channels, because the trained depth follows **`D ∝ s^{1.46}`** (0.910 at s = 0.320, 0.459 at 0.200). ⭐ **New measured behaviour of the write:** it **adapts the per-item well width to the payload excursion** — `corr(s_fit, |a_i|) = +0.821` at width 0.30 (+0.630 at 0.15), far-payload wells **1.31× wider** (0.353 vs 0.270) — and a constant-width designed surrogate on the same geometry reproduces only **5/11** cells, i.e. **the write's per-item width adaptation is load-bearing** (a point *for* the learned arm).

### N122 — ⭐ The strict-φ cost is a property of a WORKING φ — and here it is exactly the difference between clearing and missing  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✧) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** the number w24's `phi-stream-discipline` asked for and w25 could not supply (its φ was broken) — `generic_frozen − task1_only` at the same trunk config, same stream, same read-out, `phi_dim = 256`, **fit-pool-size-matched** (`cl-encoder` §5), plus the second cause of the CIFAR null (§6).
- **Numbers (verbatim, 3 seeds):** **PCA-32:** 0.219 ± 0.017 vs 0.222 ± 0.017 ⇒ **+0.003** (w25 measured +0.001 — reproduced). **`simclr`-256, pool-MATCHED at 4 966 images:** `task1_only` **0.339 ± 0.015** vs `generic_frozen` **0.358 ± 0.015** ⇒ **+0.020 ± 0.010, per-seed +0.026 / +0.008 / +0.025 — 3/3 positive**. ⭐ **And it is decision-changing: the leaky reference arm CLEARS the gate (0.358) and the defensible arm MISSES it (0.339).**
- **⚠ Confound found and controlled:** `build_cl_stream` hands the reference arm `n_fit_pool` = 6000 images but the strict arm only the task-1-class members (≈4966) — a **+21 % data advantage**. Re-running all three `generic_frozen` seeds at `n_fit_pool = 4966` barely moves the cost (+0.021 → **+0.020**) ⇒ **the cost is the class restriction, not the data volume.** The matched row is the one to quote.
- **The second cause of the CIFAR null, measured:** at the 8 k arm the gate goes **0.339 (200 items) → 0.357 (400) → 0.398 (1000) → 0.455 (5000)**; at the 20 k arm **0.357 → 0.395 ± 0.007 → 0.433 ± 0.013 → 0.482**. ⇒ **doubling the memory is worth about as much as 2.5× the φ-fit compute** (≈ +0.02 per doubling near 200), and **the gate clears at 400 items even at the under-trained arm**. At the 20 k arm the full-stream kNN (0.482) has **already reached the reduced protocol's joint bound (0.480)**.
- **Why it matters (mechanism):** on a broken φ strictness costs nothing **because everything is broken**; on a working φ the class restriction costs ~7× more than at PCA, in the same direction on every seed.
- **Scope / limits:** Split-CIFAR-10 reduced protocol, 8 k arm only (whether the cost stays ≈+0.02 at 20 k is **unmeasured** — one more 3-seed `generic_frozen` run, ~3.2 h, settles it); 200 items is a **matched-item** constraint, and at matched **bytes** this φ is already at 0.40–0.46.
- **Disposition:** ⭐ **`PREREG_CL_PHI` §7's conclusion "the strict φ costs essentially nothing" must be SCOPED to MNIST/PCA** and paired with this measurement (the binding `phi_dim ≥ 16` parameter is unaffected). **The Split-CIFAR-10 null has TWO causes** — the address space (+0.14 recovered) **and** the 200-item budget — so w25's single-cause framing (N102) is now **the larger half of a two-term explanation**. ### N135 — ⭐⭐ (POSITIVE, structural) `∂q*/∂q₀ = 0` EXACTLY — a settled-point read sends NO gradient to its read-in  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤) · memory-architecture

### N143 — ⛔ "Prop D1 is violated (1.5–7.44×)" is RETIRED, and two NEW blockers replace it  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤) · memory-architecture

- **What C2W1 measured (the superseded form, kept as history):** the harness measured `D/U` **1.5–2.5×**; the gym reached **7.44×**, and scoped it by measurement — Prop D1 **holds** (0.81–1.04) where `U` is large (queries *between* wells) and **fails 4.4–7.4×** where `U → 0` (queries near centres) ⇒ *"the error is STRUCTURED, not loose"*. The doctrine's own §2b guard had claimed the proxy over-claims by "up to 4.8 %".
- **⛔ THE CORRECTED ENTRY (C2W2 `doctrine-repairs` R1):** **`D ≤ U` is a theorem UNDER A CERTIFIED BALL**, and the gym computed `U` from **`sep/2` on stores whose sites were NOT MINIMA** — **all 7 cells with `D/U > 4` have `λ_min ∈ [−1.199, −0.372]`.** The proposition was never violated; the **proxy** was applied outside its hypothesis. ### N192 — ⛔⛔ (methodology) The registered P5 launder is a WEAKER control than its own text implies — "launder by omission", on the rival side  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤✤✤) · memory-architecture (protocol)

- **Tried:** applying `PREREG-Bprime.md` §5's registered launder (read the memory's byte-matched table **through the memory's own `θ_K, θ_V, θ_O`**) to five rival arms, **and** scoring a **raw-metric** table at the same bytes beside it.
- **Numbers (verbatim):** the gap between the two controls, **n = 3**: **0.216 / 0.203 / 0.458 / 1.208 / 1.065**; **re-quoted at pooled n = 9: 0.276 / 0.263 / 0.425 / 0.856 / 0.942 — all > 2 SE, direction and significance unchanged on 5 of 5.** ⇒ **the registered launder costs the table 0.19–1.21 `neg_mae`** purely by being read through projections it was never built for.
- **Why it happens (mechanism, two causes, both stated):** (i) those projections are trained for the **recurrence**, not for a table; (ii) **a single stored `v` is out of distribution for an output head trained on kernel-averaged reads.**
- **⭐ Why it is a contribution and not a caveat:** ⛔ **a paper running only the registered launder would have published +0.88…+1.02 dividends that do not exist.** This is ***launder by omission*** — the exact failure mode the gym-side +0 B callers were built to prevent — **appearing on the RIVAL side of an audit for the first time.**
- **Scope / limits:** ⛔ **`PREREG-Bprime.md` is NOT EDITED** (standing Hub ruling — a revised pre-registration stops being one); the correction of record is `ERRATA-Bprime.md`, and the **protocol description B′ publishes must include the raw-metric control.** ⚠ The magnitudes are `aggregate@base` only.
- **Disposition:** ⭐ **the raw-metric +0 B table is now a MANDATORY column beside any projection-read launder**, on either side of an audit. Owner of the prose: `bprime-draft`. ⚠ **Re-quote the magnitudes at n = 9, never at n = 3.**

### N194 — ⛔ (methodology) Best-of-grid on the FIT split makes a 6×2 tuning grid operationally 6×1  · tier B (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤✤✤) · memory-architecture (protocol)

- **Tried:** running `rival-recon` F3's full grid (`lr ∈ {1e-4, 3.16e-4, 5e-4, 1e-3, 3.16e-3, 1e-2} × wd ∈ {0, 0.1}`, TTT also `b ∈ {1,16}`) under **C2W4's own selection rule** (best-of-grid on the fit split) and, from the *same fits at zero extra training cost*, under a **held-out** stream (`seed + 103`).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** under the fit-split rule the widened **lr axis selects nothing new — 0 of 15 cells, 0 of 45 pooled** (P1, ✅ **EXACT**), and `wd = 0.1` is chosen only by **4th-decimal tie-breaks (6 of 15 / 12 of 45, Δfit < 0.005 in every case)**. Under **held-out** selection, **26 of 45** cells pick an lr < 1e-3 and **24 of 45** pick `wd = 0.1`, and `ttt_linear` improves **−0.6075 → −0.4461** pooled. The delta arms' whole fit surface spans **0.0011–0.0155** — **they are not lr-limited.**
- **Why (mechanism):** ⭐ **selecting best-of-grid on the objective being optimised means a regulariser can essentially never win.** The surface is *flat* in `wd`, so selection is a tie-break, not a preference.
- **Scope / limits:** measured on this harness at `aggregate@base`. ⛔ **The held-out rule rescues nobody against the raw table either** — the finding is about the *instrument*, not the verdict.
- **Disposition:** ⭐ **standing-rule candidate for `rival-recon` F3: "best-of-grid must be selected on a HELD-OUT split; selecting on the fit objective makes the weight-decay axis unselectable."** Implemented behind `--n-val` / `select_on="val"` and reported as a **declared secondary**; ⛔ **adopting it as primary is a Hub decision, not the engineer's.**

### N198 — ⛔ FB2's shape at tier iii: a GRU cannot be two-sided matched, and the TTT-class cell is the two-sided control  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤✤✤) · memory-architecture (protocol)

- **Tried:** constructing the system-level swap honestly — matching a rival cell to the CLU store on **params** and on **state bytes** at once, under the learned-initial-state rule (*an initialisation is PARAMETERS; only the per-sequence deviation is STATE*, `PREREG-Bprime.md` §4), applied to `V_θ` exactly as to a GRU's `h₀` and a TTT cell's `W₀`.
- **Numbers (verbatim, toy geometry):** **CLU** — params **8 616** (`V_θ` init 5120 f + ψ 3424 f + selectors 72 f), state **5 144 f = 20 576 B**; **GRU matched-params** — 8 682 params (**+0.77 %**), state **204 B** ⇒ ⛔ **the CLU carries 100.9× the GRU's state bytes**; **GRU matched-state-bytes — 79 469 668 params, NOT CONSTRUCTED** (3.06× an entire 26 M model at toy geometry; **1 525×** at pilot geometry); **TTT-class matched BOTH** — 8 620 params (**+0.046 %**), state **20 556 B (−0.097 %)**. **`params/state` = 1.675 (CLU) · 170.2 (GRU) · 1.677 (TTT).**
- **Why (mechanism, arithmetic not measurement):** ⭐ **a GRU cell has `params = Θ(h²)` against `state = Θ(h)`; the CLU store's parameters ARE its state.** A cell whose parameters are its state can be matched on both axes; a cell whose parameters are quadratic in its state cannot.
- **⭐ The item count at matched state bytes (D2's real consequence):** the corrected law `[A(D+2)+d]/(d+m)` with `A = 128, D = 3, d = 2, m = 1` gives **214.00× per item** ⇒ at the store's own 5 144 floats of state, **a plain table gets 1 714 rows where the store gets 8 items** (pre-registered pilot-geometry value **299.33×**, 9 578 rows vs 32 items). ⚠ **Floor check: 89× above the law's 2.40× floor, because `A = 128`.**
- **Scope / limits:** ⚠ `params/state = 1.675` is a **toy** figure (ψ is a larger fraction of the cell at toy); at pilot geometry it is **1.02**, so ⭐ **the TTT two-sided match gets EASIER with scale and the GRU's impossibility gets HARDER (100.9× → 566×)** — R1's conclusion strengthens with scale.
- **Disposition:** ✅ **Hub-ACCEPTED as the answer to R1/FB2 at tier iii: the pilot brackets with BOTH one-sided GRU columns PLUS the two-sided TTT arm — never a single one-sided match**, and both columns are published in `swap_ledger`. ⭐ **General rule: state which axis a "matched" baseline is matched on, or the match is not a control.**

### N201 — ⛔ Two self-caught correctness defects, each of which would have been published as a null  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤✤✤) · memory-architecture (instrument)

- **Tried:** running the block end-to-end and auditing its own bookkeeping before reporting a result.
- **Numbers (verbatim).** **(i) The inner write was ARITHMETICALLY inert.** With plain SGD at `atom_depth_init = 1e-4` the write objective's gradients are ~1e-4, the atoms moved ~1e-6/step, and **the read output moved by 7.5e-9 — below float32 resolution.** ⭐ **The shipped store digs its wells with 300 Adam steps at 3e-3, and Adam moves a parameter by ~`lr` per step regardless of gradient magnitude; sign-SGD reproduces that behaviour STATELESSLY** (a real Adam would add two moment tensors per sequence = 2× the store's state bytes and **break the D2 ledger**). **Post-fix the read moves 3.5e-4 over 8 writes — a 10⁴ improvement.** **(ii) Eviction bookkeeping** sliced the controller log by a **count** of past evictions and looked the victim up by item id, but the allocator had already deleted the record ⇒ **133 evictions reported from 64 offers**, and **not one `reset` ever marked**, so evicted atom groups were never re-drawn. **Post-fix: 24 / 19 / 37 evictions from 64 offers.**
- **Why it matters (mechanism):** ⭐⭐ **defect (i) is why §3's settled-point gradient is exactly `0.0` — `jnp.sign` has zero derivative, so the shipped sign-SGD inner write severs `∂(store state)/∂φ` BY CONSTRUCTION.** ⇒ ⛔ **anyone quoting the "∞" trajectory-vs-point ratio must quote WHICH WRITE**: with a plain-SGD write the same probe gives **1.5e3 – 2.0e9 (geometric mean ≈ 2.3e5)**, which is the theorem's own contribution isolated. ⚠ **And it is NOT `trainability-spike`'s 2.42e6** (a frozen store with no write path) — do not conflate them.
- **Scope / limits:** ⚠ **the whole 3-seed table was re-run after both fixes and the bpc figures were unchanged to 4 d.p.** — ⭐ *which is itself evidence for N196's inertness, not evidence that the fixes did not matter.* ⚠ **Declared budget overrun (13 h against a declared 8 h)**, caused by these re-runs and one crash — **the honest call, declared rather than absorbed.**
- **Disposition:** ⭐ **standing engineering rule: any streaming / inner-loop write must use an Adam-like STEP-SIZE rule (sign-SGD is the stateless one), or it is inert at the shipped depth init.** ⭐ **And the epistemic point: reporting an inert memory caused by one's own optimiser would have been a false first-order finding — the re-run was the right call.**

### N202 — ⛔ (process, program-wide) A formula bug invisible at the default geometry survives every green test  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤✤✤) · all (process)

- **Tried:** fixing `memory_gym.byte_ratio_law`'s denominator and asking why three waves of a fully green suite never caught it.

### N204 — ⛔⛔ Our own theory placed our own rig on the `d/s` axis wrongly, by 45–52× — and the 1089× span retires  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤✤✤) · memory-architecture

- **Tried:** measuring, rather than inferring, where the shipped rig sits on the axis the coupling law is a function of (`bprime-c6` D1/D2).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** T5.5's *"the rig C2W3 actually runs: `d/s ≈ 1.9–2.0`, coupling `0.69–0.80`, O(1)"* takes `d = d_safe_override = 0.58` — **an admission gate, i.e. a refusal radius** — as if it were the achieved spacing. **Measured on `overload/load1x_shipped`: `sep = 1.3459` ⇒ `d/s = 4.34` (atom ruler) / `3.72` (fitted ruler), measured coupling `1.53e-2`.** ⛔ **The span across the whole admissibly-writable sweep (`d/s` 1.77 → 5.32) is `10^2.72 = 525×`, not 1089×**; from where we run to the designed gate is **≈10×**. **`atom_init_width = 0.30` is a 1.33×-low proxy for the fitted `s = 0.40`, and because the exponent is `d²/2s²` that overstates the law's decades by 1.74×** (measured span 2.72 decades vs 4.73 predicted on the atom ruler).
- **Why (mechanism):** ⭐ **a gate is not a geometry.** `d_safe` is the radius at which a write is *refused*; the achieved separation is what the store actually realises, and on this rig it is 2.3× larger.

### N211 — ⛔ (engineering) The x64 import-order landmine bites MODULE-SCOPED fixtures too  · tier C (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✤✤✤) · all (silent-hazard family)

- **Tried:** adding a new test module (`tests/test_cluformer_pilot.py`, 46 tests) that constructs JAX store objects inside a **module-scoped** fixture, under the repo's existing float32 discipline (the N72 remedy: a float32 fixture per test module).
- **Numbers (verbatim).** **Before the fix, on the full suite: `10 failed, 1172 passed` — all 10 the new module's, and all 10 PASS in isolation.** The ordering was reproduced exactly with `pytest tests/test_lattice.py tests/test_blocks.py tests/test_cluformer_pilot.py`: **10 failed before, 60 passed after.** ✅ **Final branch suite after the fix: `1182 passed, 0 failed` in 1025.40 s** (main venv, **JAX 0.9.0**, worktree).
- **Why it failed (mechanism):** ⭐ **several test modules enable `jax_enable_x64` at MODULE IMPORT, and pytest sets up module-scoped fixtures BEFORE function-scoped ones** ⇒ a cell **constructed in float64** was then **exercised in float32**. ⛔ **N72's fix pattern (a function-scoped float32 fixture) is therefore insufficient the moment a module builds its objects module-scoped.** ✅ **The fix pattern, filed for reuse: any new test module that builds JAX objects in a module-scoped fixture must declare its float32 fixture `scope="module", autouse=True`** (commit `f173db6`).
- **Scope / limits:** a **test-harness** hazard, not a science result — ⛔ **no reported number is affected** (the pilot's results were produced after the fix, and its bpc table was re-run twice more for unrelated defects without moving to 4 d.p.). ⚠ **It is order-dependent by construction: the failure is invisible when the module runs alone**, which is how it reaches CI green on a branch and red on a suite.
- **Disposition:** ⚠ **filed as the C2W4 half of the standing N72 hazard** (C2W4 reconciliation 3, assigned *"curator (§7)"*). ⛔ **The repo-level remedy is still unbuilt** — a `conftest.py`-level guard so no numerically-marginal test is order-dependent (`future_work.md`, `OPEN`, N72). ⭐ **The transferable sentence: a precision fixture must be scoped no later than the thing it protects is CONSTRUCTED.** ⚠ **Handover §7 (Known Issues) is the Hub's document — this entry is proposed for it, not written into it.**

### N213 — ⭐⭐ The physics settle DESTROYS set information the launch geometry already carries  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (tier ii / protocol)

- **Tried:** scoring occupancy precision and distinct-well occupancy for the physics read against the tightest available control — **the same launch points with the store deleted** (`orgdiv-cat-test` §1.2), then re-measuring the same statistics independently on the null-arms rig (`orgdiv-null-arms` §3).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** occupancy precision **launch 0.406 → settled 0.297** (2-SE-separated) — *the settle destroys 27 % of the set information the raw launch geometry already carries.* Distinct wells occupied: **raw launch 2.202 ± 0.02 → 1.70 after the settle**. Independently reproduced: null-arms measures the raw-launch precision at **0.4106** against cat-test's **0.4061**. The cat test's **−0.109 address-leak "dividend"** is the same fact with the opposite sign convention.
- **Why it happens (mechanism, named this wave):** ⭐ **the settle MERGES particles into shared basins.** A dissipative relaxation is a contraction onto minima; two particles launched into the same catchment arrive at *one* answer, and a set-valued query loses a member every time that happens.
- **Scope / limits:** measured at the cat-test cell (`N_a = 32, F = 4, K = 128, a = 32, d = 4, m = 8`, `P = 4`, `γ_address/γ_read = 0.05/0.02`, 400 → 800 Verlet steps at `dt = 0.05`). ⚠ **It is a statement about a set-valued occupancy read, not about settled-point reads in general** (for which O1/N206 already applies).
- **Disposition:** ⭐⭐ **Standing doctrine, adopted: occupancy / co-activation precision is scored against the BLANK STORE / raw launch geometry — NEVER against `F/N_a`.** ⛔ **`F/N_a = 0.125` as a baseline is a never-quote** (it is beaten by a blank store, because the wells sit at the frozen query codes and the launch geometry alone is a matched filter). ⭐ **And the design consequence is sharp: any read that must express `F` distinct answers has to fight its own relaxation** — which is precisely what §A20.3(b)–(c) replaces rather than patches.
- **⭐ Dated C2W7 ADDENDUM (2026-08-06, `doc-curator-c2w7-fold`; nothing above rewritten) — the same defect at a multiplicity head has the OPPOSITE SIGN, and the two must never be quoted as one another.** At `P = 4` occupancy the settle **MERGES** (distinct wells **2.202 → 1.70**, precision 0.406 → 0.297). At the C2W7 `k = 12` multiplicity head the settle **SCATTERS**: distinct wells **4.834 ± 0.125 → 5.668 ± 0.396**, raw precision **0.4578 ± 0.0260 → 0.4107 ± 0.0191** — *particles committed to the same well end in different basins*, because the store's attractors sit **1.09 = ~1.4 `sep`** from its designed anchors (**N233**). ⛔ **Consequence for the instrument: `R2` (registered to fire iff settled < launched) CANNOT SEE the multiplicity failure** (**N236**). ⭐ **What survives unchanged and is now doubly-evidenced: a set-valued read must fight its own relaxation in whichever direction that relaxation happens to run** — and the named fix is store-side (attractor–anchor alignment, §A26.6(a)), not another read. **Source:** `c2w7-read-cardinality` §4.1; charter **§A24/§A25.2**.

### N214 — ⭐⭐ THE READ-PROTOCOL REFUTATION AT `P = 4` — the read cannot express the answer, and the family is not what failed  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (tier ii)

- **Tried:** measuring, on the frozen launch protocol every arm shares, how many **distinct wells** the `P = 4` particles actually occupy — the quantity the `F = 4` sum requires — plus an out-of-protocol `P`-sweep as a declared diagnostic (`orgdiv-null-arms` §3/§3.1).
- **Numbers (verbatim, unseen queries, 5 seeds, 2 560 queries):** distinct wells occupied **2.202 ± 0.02** · fraction of queries with **≥ F = 4** distinct wells **0.050** · occupancy precision **0.4106** · ⛔ **exact-set occupancy (occupied set == `A(x)`) 0.0000 / 2 560.** After N3's fitted static-geometric assignment: 2.207 / 0.050 / 0.408 / **0.0000**; after N2's fitted codebook: 2.224 / 0.053 / 0.111 / **0.0000**; ⛔ **after the physics settle: 1.70 distinct.** **`P`-sweep (declared out-of-protocol — changing `P` re-draws the launch offsets, so these are NOT matched arms and never a score):** `P = 4/8/16/32/64` → distinct **2.19 / 2.74 / 3.30 / 3.88 / 4.34**, `≥ F` **0.047 / 0.201 / 0.412 / 0.607 / 0.741**, exact-set occupancy **0.0000 / 0.0004 / 0.0016 / 0.0016 / 0.0016**, combinatorial ceiling **0.288 / 0.501 / 0.720 / 0.861 / 0.938**.
- **Why it lands (mechanism):** ⭐ **you cannot sum four vectors you never visited.** Every reader in the frozen class (`sum_linear`, `well_table`, `knn`, `mlp_small`) consumes the same `(P, d+m)` object, which contains **at most ~2.2 distinct payloads** — so the ceiling is **structural, set before any organizer exists**, and it is **0.05** on the `≥ F` event alone. ⚠ **And the `P`-sweep says two different things:** more particles fix *addressability* and *information* but **not precision (0.40 at every `P`)** ⇒ ⛔ **`P` alone is not the fix; the assignment rule is also wrong.**
- **Scope / limits:** ⛔ **`P > 4` as a matched ARM is a declared NOT-RUN** (it would need a new frozen φ and a new cat-test cell). ⚠ The physics settle row was rebuilt on the null-arms rig; **no K-verdict was re-adjudicated there.**
- **Disposition:** ⛔⛔ **THE MANDATORY RE-LABELLING (charter §A20.2, binding on every artifact and every future draft): the refuted object is "the `P`-particle occupancy read protocol at `P = 4`", NEVER "the compositional family".** ⭐⭐ **`K0` is ADOPTED as a pre-condition beside K1–K5 for any future compositional cell: `P(≥ F distinct wells occupied)` is computable from the launch geometry alone, store-free, in seconds — before anything is written.** ⭐ **The two named requirements for any revival read: (i) address `F` distinct wells; (ii) do not quantise away the continuous launch coordinate** (N215). ⚠ **Neither is a physics question — both bind the physics arm exactly as hard as they bind the nulls.**
- **⭐ Dated C2W7 ADDENDUM (2026-08-06, `doc-curator-c2w7-fold`; nothing above rewritten) — both named requirements were BUILT, and the first one is MET.** The C2W7 multiplicity read addresses `F` distinct wells and keeps the continuous coordinate: `F_hat` **4.542 ± 0.122**, asserted-set size **4.194 ± 0.224**, exactly `F` on **39.4 %** of queries, and ⭐ **`R1` clears for the first time in the program (0.065625 ± 0.023876, mean−2SE 0.0417 vs bar 0.02; iteration 1 0.0023 — 28×)** (**N232**). ⛔ **And it does not rescue the tier:** `G1` fires significantly (**−0.007031 ± 0.001562, 5/5 seeds**) — **the gain is entirely LAUNCH-SIDE**, and the designed/untrained head beats the trained one (0.0695 vs 0.0539). ⚠ **`K0`'s adoption as a pre-condition (above) now carries its own caveat: it is a REACHABILITY statement only** — a collapsed head scores `K0 = 1.000` while every reader reads 0.0000 (**N235**). ⛔ **This addendum does NOT re-open the §A20.2 re-labelling: the refuted object is still "the `P`-particle occupancy read protocol at `P = 4`."** **Source:** `c2w7-read-cardinality` §1/§3/§4.2; charter **§A24/§A26.5**.

### N216 — ⭐ N1 memorises perfectly and composes not at all — at five times the bytes  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (tier ii)

- **Tried:** N1, gradient-placed atoms in **the identical store parameterisation as the physics arm**, trained to place and to fit, at `a = 64` (**28 672 free floats = 114 688 B, 5× the physics arm's store**), then scored on rule-4-valid held-out combinations both **inside SEEN** (validation) and on `Q_unseen`.
- **Numbers (verbatim, `orgdiv-null-arms` §1.2):** **in-sample fit 1.0000** (96/96 trained rows, and **1.0000 on all 128**) · **held-out 0.0000**, on **all 4 readers × 5 seeds = 20/20 cells** · grid-max over its 180 configs **0.00039**.
- **Why it lands (mechanism):** ⭐ **the failure is not capacity, not optimisation and not the fit — it is that nothing in the objective forces the learned placement to be COMPOSITIONAL.** A store with enough parameters to memorise every written combination will do exactly that, and the held-out combinations are then a different problem it was never asked to solve. ⚠ **Read with N214: even a perfectly compositional placement could not be *read* through a `P = 4` occupancy protocol that occupies 2.2 wells.**
- **Scope / limits:** one family, one φ, `F = 4` of `N_a = 32`. ⛔ **Not a statement about gradient-trained placement in general** — it is a statement about this objective on this read.
- **Disposition:** ⛔ **Per Hub ruling 2(b) (Head, C2W5 first review): N1's score was PRE-REGISTERED as the revival target the tuned physics arm would have to beat *if it cleared chance*. It did not clear ⇒ NO REVIVAL TARGET IS SET by this wave.** ⭐ **The sharpest single sentence the audit produced, and it belongs in the tier-ii write-up verbatim: identical parameterisation, 5× the bytes, 1.0000 train, 0.0000 held-out.**

Read-objective agreement **0.2576** (0.273 / 0.229 / 0.271) against registered **0.22**, band [0.15, 0.30] ⇒ ✅ **in band, and it independently reproduces the cat test's 0.211–0.233.** **F5 fires (≥ 0.99)? NO, at either fitting** — as registered.
- **Why it matters (mechanism):** ⭐ **the physics arm's assignment is 89 % reproducible by a static power diagram when you fit the diagram to the assignments, and only 26 % reproducible when you fit it to the read objective.** ⛔ **The gap between 0.89 and 0.26 is NOT "a structurally non-VQ channel"; it is an optimisation gap in fitting the diagram.**

- **Disposition:** ⚠ **STANDING CAVEAT, must travel with every quotation of cat-test F5:** *"does not fire" means "the read objective is a bad way to recover the assignment", NOT "the physics organizer is non-VQ".* ⛔ **Anyone using F5 to argue the store's partition is not a power diagram is over-reading it.**

Beside the incumbents at the same n: **ttt_linear −0.4602 ± 0.1038 (4.43 SE) · ttt_mlp −0.4425 ± 0.0869 (5.09) · deltanet −0.2732 ± 0.0395 (6.92) · gdn −0.2600 ± 0.0278 (9.35) · gdn2 −0.2592 ± 0.0292 (8.87)**. **Prereg: 11 in band / 2 partial / 0 refuted** (M2 landed 0.004 from its registered point).
- **Why it lands (mechanism):** **Mamba-2 is the erase-free degenerate case of the delta-rule family and behaves like it.** ⭐ **It posts the audit's best `full` score and still loses decisively to a zero-extra-byte reader of a raw table holding the same 5 184 bytes.**
- **Scope / limits:** ⚠ **two honest qualifiers, first-class:** its `full` beats `gdn2`'s by **0.0029 ± 0.037 — a TIE, not a win**, and **no ordering among the four delta/SSD arms is quoted**; its **+0 B margin +0.0047 ± 0.0519 is a tie with zero, not a positive rival row** (the load-bearing column is the raw one). ⛔ **On `overload@load1x_shipped` it is NOT RESCUED in 3/3 selections** (`f3` +0.028 ± 0.035 · `f3_lite` +0.009 ± 0.037 · `f3_val` +0.014 ± 0.045, all within noise of its own blank and of chance) ⇒ **labelled null: no curve, and no margin quotable there — including against the CLU's banked `decode 0.972`.** ⚠ **Prereg self-flag: the bands were drawn with the incumbent cluster visible; the sharp rows are M2b and the six exact ledger integers.** ⚠ **Venue/year/id and the reference-implementation state accounting come from `rival-recon` §1.4's pinned record and are NOT re-verified — `bprime-cite-check-2`'s item.**
- **Disposition:** ⭐ **The headline moves 0-of-5 → "0 of 6 rival arms"**, margin range **−0.2563 … −0.4602** (minimum 4.43 SE unchanged, still `ttt_linear`), and **§5.2's "SSMs named, none measured" limitation RETIRES.** ⛔ **"0 of 5" is superseded everywhere.** ⚖ **And a THIRD code path changes a standing verdict:** under **held-out `f3_val` selection at n = 9**, `deltanet` (+0.077 ± 0.045) and `gdn2` (+0.669 ± 0.339) fall **below** the 2-SE rescue bar; only `gdn` and `mamba2` clear under all three selections ⇒ **Hub ruling (selection-stability, extending A17.4): rescue verdicts are quoted only where STABLE across registered selection rules; `deltanet` and `gdn2` are SELECTION-DEPENDENT and no flattering margin against them is quotable** (see the N193 addendum).

### N220 — ⛔ Both TTT arms read below their own same-keys null at n = 9  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (tier i / B′)

- **Tried:** the n = 9 four-column re-aggregation's `full − same-keys null` column, which had never been computed at power (`pilot-placement-probe` R5; filed in-draft at `bprime-draft-r3` §4.1.1 + App. L 18).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** `ttt_linear` **−0.2063 ± 0.1016** · `ttt_mlp` **−0.1995 ± 0.0665** ⇒ **both below their own same-keys null**; all three delta arms are above it: **+0.2174 / +0.5642 / +0.7438**. ⚠ **Companion (R4):** the TTT n = 9 ledger columns are **not constant across seeds** — `ttt_linear` **5220 / 5328 B**, `ttt_mlp` **4656 / 5376 B** — because best-of-grid picks the mini-batch `b` per seed and `b` enters the declared state.
- **Why it matters:** ⭐ **reading below a null built from the same keys is arguably a stronger statement of malfunction than failing the blank-store gate** — the arm is not merely uninformative, it is worse than a control that shares its keys.
- **Scope / limits:** ⛔ **rival-side only; it changes no CLU claim.** One family, `aggregate@base`.
- **Disposition:** ⭐ **This was `bprime-draft-r3`'s "homeless finding" (its reconciliation 2, owner: curator) and it now has a registry home.** ⛔ **Never-quote: a single TTT byte figure as *the* n = 9 value** — the modal-value rule (same discipline as N218's R2).

### N221 — ⛔ Both ranked placement hypotheses are refuted in a streaming block: H1 is HARMFUL, H2 is bit-identically INERT  · tier B (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (tier iii)

- **Tried:** the pilot's §5.3 hypotheses at toy scale, 3 paired seeds, against a pre-registered success signal (acquisition off chance · live ≠ blank at float32 · depth leaves the 0.045 saturation): **H1** = `atom_local_radius` (the N98 localized init), **H2** = `write_lambda_traj` (the trajectory write term), plus a streaming-adapted placement **H1b** (`atom_place_radius`) and a raised hinge margin (`pilot-placement-probe` §5/§6).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** **H1 is worse than doing nothing** — up to **−6 orders** of well depth at its designed band. **H2 is bit-identically inert at 3.9× wall-clock** (gradient ~**1e-13** at flat init; sign-SGD needs a sign flip). **H1b + margin wakes depth: 0.0288 → 0.1668**, still **5.8× below** the pilot's saturation — and ⛔ **the saturation IS the shipped `write_margin = 0.15`, not the budget** (×10 steps with placement buys **1.03×**). ⛔⛔ **Margin 1.0 collapses between-item `q*` discrimination: 0.114 → 0.054.** ⛔ **ADDENDUM-3's C1 is refuted on magnitude** (predicted depth 0.35–0.9 at margin 1.0; measured **0.1668**). **Laundering control, mandatory here:** a blank store carrying the SAME localized init gives `acq(live) − acq(blank)` = **exactly 0.000 on 14/14 cells × 3 seeds**.
- **Why they fail (mechanisms, both named):** **H1** places atoms at *init*, but the write site is **controller-chosen at write time and unknown at init** — a localized init in the wrong place is worse than a scattered one. **H2**'s gradient is ~1e-13 at a flat init, and the shipped sign-SGD write takes the *sign* of it — so the term is arithmetically present and behaviourally absent.
- **Scope / limits:** ⛔ **TOY (0.16 M params, `d_model 64`, 2 layers, `seq_len 512`, 3 seeds) and formally NON-PROMOTABLE under N94** (4 inner write steps against a floor of 40, except the two `*_w40` cells, which say the same thing). ⛔ **Nothing here touches tier ii or the CSF3 scale run.** ⚠ **A finding that RE-PRICES, never closes, the route (A18.4).**
- **Disposition:** ⭐⭐ **The pilot's THREE §5.3 candidates are now ranked by measurement, and the survivor is the one that was ranked LAST — the ψ payload residual (N222).** ⛔ **The design lesson, quotable: a deeper well at a shared payload location is a WORSE memory** — depth and discrimination are not the same axis, and the hinge margin trades one for the other. **N111 gains a third harness, this time with a mechanism.**
- **⭐⭐ Dated C2W6 addendum (2026-08-05, `doc-curator-c2w6-fold`; nothing above rewritten) — H1b's placement path turns out to carry a GRADIENT CHANNEL nobody had named.** The very assignment that wakes depth here — `centers[:, :addr] = z[:addr] + jig`, live whenever **`atom_place_radius > 0`** — is a plain **differentiable** path from φ into the store's state, **outside the sign-gated write loop**: it carries **27 % of φ's layer-0 gradient (0.0908 → 0.0659)**, and `erosion_partition` is what closes it (**N228**). ⇒ ⛔ **every *"the write cannot train φ"* statement now needs the placement qualifier**; and ⚠ **H1b is no longer only a placement lever — it is also a training channel**, which is a second axis on which this entry's re-pricing must be read.

### N222 — ⭐⭐ The isolated cause of the acquisition null: the dynamics deliver the payload and ψ compresses it away  · tier A (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (tier ii + tier iii)

- **Tried:** decomposing the read into (a) *does the trajectory carry the payload into `q*`?* and (b) *does ψ preserve it?* — `decode_dispersion.json` / `qstar_payload.json`, lane 0, seed 0, 3 live items, three cells (`pilot-placement-probe` §6.1/§6.2).
- **Numbers (verbatim).** **(b) The read's decoded payload is compressed and is not item-specific:** decoded range **0.0085** (`baseline`) / **0.0065** (`h1b_r0.3`) / **0.0117** (`h1b_m1.0`) against a **true payload range of 0.2277** ⇒ **7–25× compression**; and the between-item decode spread (**0.0065–0.0117**) is **the same order as the live-vs-blank decode max \|Δ\| (0.0031–0.0063)**. **(a) The dynamics DO deliver it** (blank store: **0.000** on all items): `q*[payload]` reaches **−0.233 / −0.181 / −0.211 ≈ 30 %** of the true payloads (−0.622 / −0.779 / −0.850) at baseline, **~48 %** with placement, and **130–175 % (overshoot)** at margin 1.0 — with between-item spread **0.053 / 0.114 / 0.054**.
- **Why it lands (mechanism):** ⭐⭐ **the nearest-stored-payload assignment is a fixed permutation of a nearly constant vector, which yields exactly one hit per lane ⇒ `acq = mean(1/n_live) = chance`, identically.** That is why the acquisition null was *exact* and not noisy — and it locates the loss **downstream of the physics**, in the read-out.
- **Scope / limits:** ⛔ **TOY scale, one lane, one seed, three live items, NON-PROMOTABLE under N94.** ⛔ **The fix was NOT BUILT this wave** — declared NOT-RUN, ~1-day build, sharp acceptance target already written: *does decoded spread reach `q*` spread?* ⚠ **Independently indicted from the other side by the cat test** (whose read also fails to express what the geometry carries).
- **Disposition:** ⭐⭐ **Head ruling (C2W5 second review, charter §A20.3(a)): the ψ payload-residual fix is the FIRST experimental TODO of the read-fix iteration** (`psi-payload-residual`, wt1), **its acceptance is §A20.3(a) verbatim** (decoded spread reaches `q*` spread; **blank-decode stays at chance — the leak check is blocking**), and it **GATES CSF3 RUN 2** (the decoder-fixed config is run 1's pre-registered designed ablation, same config otherwise). ⛔ **Standing: no run-1 number is ever quoted as the scale verdict** (§A20.4).
- **⭐ Dated C2W6 addendum (2026-08-05, `doc-curator-c2w6-fold`; nothing above rewritten) — the ψ payload residual is now measured as a DEPTH PROTECTOR over 1000 outer steps, not only as a read fix.** With the residual OFF (the store useless to the loss) retention falls to **0.141 ± 0.095×** untrained against **0.708 ± 0.57×** with it ON — a **5.0×** difference — and destructive rewrites rise to **0.512 ± 0.238** vs **0.228 ± 0.182** (**N225**, ⛔ DIAGNOSTIC-labelled corner, never a claim cell). ⇒ ⭐ **the channel this entry isolated as the acquisition fix is also the channel that gives the wells a reason to exist.** ⚠ **The C2W6 P-residual interaction row was scored ✅ (P1 NOT disproved) — but the analyst's F2 shows that row is near-unpassable as written** (a per-seed quantity against a pooled mean the reference arm itself meets on 1/3 seeds, at a mismatched 200-vs-1000-step horizon); **F2 is POST-HOC and was NOT applied as a re-scoring.**

### N223 — ⛔ Two hundred steps of outer training destroy the store's wells  · tier B (CURATOR-PROPOSED ✦) · memory-architecture (tier iii / §7.27)

- **Tried:** measuring fitted well depth **through** the outer training loop rather than after a single write (`pilot-placement-probe` R3/§10, 3 seeds, shipped config, 200 steps, AdamW warmup-cosine peak lr 1e-3).
- **Numbers (verbatim):** median fitted depth **0.029 → 4.95e-63**. **Placement + margin keeps depth at 0.0616 ± 0.037** through the same training. ⭐ **This is the same object as the pilot's monitor-#9 `Δ_ret = 7.8e-86`, whose cause was never named.**
- **Why it matters:** ⛔ **an experiment that only inspects the store after the write will report a healthy store and then train it to nothing** — the destruction is invisible at every checkpoint the pilot was taking. ⚠ **The cause is still unowned:** the one gradient probe that would distinguish **φ-drift** from **amplitude suppression** is unrun (`plan-pass-vectorise` reconciliation 2).
- **Scope / limits:** TOY scale, 3 seeds, 200 steps; ⛔ **not a statement about the shipped standalone store**, which is not trained through an outer loop.
- **Disposition:** ✅ **Instrumented, not merely noted:** `store_health_probe` ships **on by default** (`[watch/clu_store]` log lines + artifact `arms.*.train.store_health`), landed by `plan-pass-vectorise`. ⭐ **CSF3 abort criterion, pre-registered (Head, C2W5 second review):** *any seed whose trained well depth falls below **1e-3 absolute**, or below **0.1× its own untrained depth** on two consecutive watch reads ⇒ the Hub flags PAUSE, the Head `scancel`s, and the run reports as **PAUSED-WITH-MECHANISM** — the allocation never burns silently.* ⭐ **The 1e-63 signature is caught at the first read.**

> ### ⛔⛔ **Dated C2W6 ADDENDUM (2026-08-05, `doc-curator-c2w6-fold`, [C2W6] + charter ADDENDUM 7 §A22–§A23 — the entry above is NOT rewritten; every number in it stands as measured at its own config).** Three things move, and one of them is program-wide.
>
> **1. ⛔⛔ THE PREMISE IS RETIRED, WITH A SCOPE QUALIFIER: N223's MONOTONE COLLAPSE DOES NOT REPRODUCE AT THE RUN-2 CONFIG.** Over **1000** outer steps × 3 paired seeds the partition-OFF arm does **not** decay: the registered E1 statistic (final ÷ step-200) reads **9.782 / 0.9035 / 0.5305** against a rule of ≤0.3× (band ≤0.5×) ⇒ ⛔ **E1 is REFUTED 0/3.** N223's `0.0288 → 4.95e-63` was measured at the **SHIPPED** config (**no placement, `write_margin = 0.15`, pre-ψ-fix**); **placement + margin + the ψ residual have between them removed it.** ⛔⛔ **NEVER-QUOTE: *"there is no erosion at the run-2 config"*** — that sentence is **estimator-dependent** (final/untrained arith **0.708×** vs geo **0.327×**; 2 of 3 seeds lost ~7× depth, one gained 1.85×). ⭐ **The defensible form is *"N223's monotone collapse does not reproduce at the run-2 config."*** ⚠ **On the registered E1 statistic the refutation is robust under BOTH estimators (arith 3.739, geo 1.674), so no verdict moves.** **Where erosion still lives:** the **residual-OFF** corner (**0.141 ± 0.095×**, N225) and **w40 seed 0** (0.0730 → 2.12e-04, ×0.0029; N227).
>
> **2. ⛔ THE CENSORING ERRATUM (§A23.4, PROGRAM-WIDE): "4.95e-63" IS A CENSORING STATEMENT, NEVER A POINT ESTIMATE.** The banked figure is the **arithmetic mean of per-seed depths spanning 114.8 orders of magnitude — 1.439e-87 / 1.486e-62 / 2.493e-177** — i.e. ≈ seed 1 ÷ 3, *a single seed wearing a mean's clothes*; the **geometric mean is 3.764e-109**, 46 orders lower. ⭐ **Replacement wording, mandatory everywhere:** ***"200 outer steps drive well depth below 1e-62 on 3/3 seeds (1.4e-87 / 1.5e-62 / 2.5e-177)."*** ⚠ **The qualitative R3 claim is UNTOUCHED and if anything STRENGTHENED** (3/3 seeds annihilate; two go far below the quoted figure). ⛔ **Any band phrased as a ratio to this anchor is ill-conditioned.** **Sites swept this pass:** this entry · `claims_matrix.md` §0.10 · `philosophy-synthesis.md` (⟲ C2W6) · `future_work.md` (C2W6 fold) · `HEP_primers.md` (Records 18/21 updates) · a dated curator erratum banner on `pilot-placement-probe.md` §7. ⛔ **`PREREG-*.md` files are NOT edited** (a revised pre-registration stops being one) — annotated only.
>
> **3. ⛔⭐ THE PRE-REGISTERED CSF3 ABORT CRITERION IS SUSPENDED (Head ruling §A23.1) — stronger than the amendment the Hub proposed.** The rule in this entry's Disposition (*depth < 1e-3 absolute, or < 0.1× own untrained on two consecutive reads ⇒ PAUSE*) is **a measured FALSE-POSITIVE GENERATOR at the run-2 config**: replayed against C2W6's curves on the exact arm CSF3 is running, **seed 0 trips on 15 of 41 readings, first at step 25, reaching 4.12e-4 — below the 1e-3 immediate-escalation floor — and then RECOVERS 15.2× to 6.25e-3; seed 2 trips 10/41 from step 50 and recovers 2.6×; only seed 1 never trips.** Two of three healthy seeds would have been paused mid-dip. ⇒ **NO abort criterion is in force; all in-flight CSF3 runs finish regardless; §7.27's watch item is INSTRUMENTATION ONLY** (depth telemetry still logged as post-hoc evidence, **no run is paused or escalated on it**). ⭐ **The Head's run-1 seed-0 override is recorded VINDICATED BY MEASUREMENT** (3-seed toy replication + a mechanism, not a judgement call). ⚠ **Accepted risk, stated knowingly by the Head and recorded in §A23.1: a genuinely destroyed store now burns its allocation to completion.** ⇒ **Operational consequence for whoever babysits: there is nothing to escalate — do not propose a pause on a depth reading.**
